## B-077 — CHANGED 2026-10-06, seen in the iPadOS 18 simulator and on the iPad, VoiceOver's place too under B-079 (2026-10-20). The panes moved in a way of their own; now they move as Mail's

**Asked** on 2026-10-06. B-066 built the view button's motion and put
two questions to the owner (TODO, "Blocked on the owner"): keep its
motion, or later Mail's; and should "< Mailboxes" and a folder tap in two
panes slide. He answered: "copy apple mail for these".

**What Mail does.** Mail is UIKit's split view, three columns, and in a
narrow window its navigation controller; it moves as they move. Mail
itself was not filmed. UIKit was measured in the iPadOS 18.6 simulator on
2026-10-06, frame by frame and from the animations it installs.

- *The sidebar button*, three columns and two: one motion of half a
  second on a spring, mass 3 and stiffness 1000, critically damped. Half
  the way by 0.09 to 0.10 s, 90% by 0.21 s, 99% by 0.37 s, done at 0.5 s.
  Every column moves at once on the same curve. Nothing moves up or
  down, and there is no second phase. Hiding the sidebar, the list keeps
  its width and slides left over it, a shadow on its leading edge; the
  sidebar goes left at half the list's speed and darkens, black at a
  tenth; the letter's left edge goes with the list. Showing it is the
  exact reverse.
- *A push and a pop*: the new screen slides in from the right edge of its
  column, over the old, with a shadow on its leading edge; the old goes
  30% of the column to the left and darkens. A pop is the reverse. The
  same spring. The bar's title and back button cross-fade and slide over
  0.35 s on cubic(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1).
- *Reduce Motion* changes neither. With *Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions*
  as well, the sidebar still slides, the same spring and the same paths;
  a push and a pop become a cross-fade of 0.5 s, nothing moving.
- *The layout.* On an iPad 1194 pt wide or narrower, Mail with its
  sidebar shown pushes the letter partly off the screen and dims it. From
  1210 pt it puts the three side by side.

**What it was** (B-066). Pictures slid 0.4 s, easing in and out, then
faded 0.2 s over the panes beneath. The folders stood still; the list kept
its three-pane width, and from three to two a strip of canvas opened
beside it. With Reduce Motion or Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions, the screen
faded for 0.3 s. "< Mailboxes" and a folder tap in two panes were instant.

**Changed.**

1. *One motion, on UIKit's spring.* Half a second, mass 3, stiffness
   1000, critically damped, every picture at once (`PaneMove.progress`,
   `Theme.paneMoveDuration`). No settle. UIKit asks for a damping of
   500, which iPadOS 18 runs as critical; asked for as it is on an older
   iPadOS it might not be, so the damping given is the critical one,
   109.5.
2. *Three to two.* The list, laid out as it will be, 375 pt, slides left
   over the folders from where its right edge meets the letter's to the
   screen's edge, 205.5 pt on the 11-inch. A shadow comes on its leading
   edge. The folders go left half as far, 102.75 pt, and darken to a
   tenth. The letter's left edge goes with the list.
3. *Two to three, the list in front.* The exact reverse: the list, laid
   out as in three, 330 pt, slides right off the folders; they come back
   from 102.75 pt left, laid out, darkened, and lighten; the shadow goes.
4. *Two to three, the folders in front.* Mail has no such switch. B-066's
   shape stays, on the same spring and with no settle: the folders'
   column draws in, cut off, the letter's edge goes right, and the list
   is there between them.
5. *A folder tapped in two panes.* Its list slides in from the column's
   right edge over the folders, a shadow on its leading edge; the folders
   go 112.5 pt left, 30% of the column, and darken. Only what is under
   the bars moves. The folders' bar slides half the column left and fades
   out, the list's comes from half the column right and fades in, over
   0.35 s on UIKit's bar curve, over an empty bar that stays. The view
   button's glyph stays in the corner. Nothing goes over the letter: the
   pictures are cut off at the column.
6. *"< Mailboxes"* is the reverse: the list slides off to the right, its
   shadow going, and the folders come back from 112.5 pt left, lightening,
   the open one highlighted.
7. *Reduce Motion*, Mail's rule. The view button's switch slides whatever
   is set. "< Mailboxes" and a folder tap slide, and with Prefer
   Cross-Fade Transitions, which iOS gives only with Reduce Motion on,
   the column as it was fades for 0.5 s over the column as it is, its
   rows on UIKit's ease in and out, its bar on the bar curve, and nothing
   moves (`PaneMove.motion`, `PaneMotion.crossFading`).

**The layout is Blackmail's.** The motion is copied, not the layout. The
three panes stay side by side at every width, his own choice (D-015), where
Mail on an iPad as narrow as his pushes the letter off. So the letter's
picture keeps its left edge with the list's right edge, as Mail's does on
a 1210 pt iPad, and its right edge stays the screen's. The list is 330 pt
in three panes and 375 in two on the 11-inch, where Mail's is 375 in both;
its picture has the width it ends at, all the way.

**Not UIKit's own push.** A real push and pop were weighed first, and
do not fit. The list has a navigation controller of its own
in both arrangements, beside the Mailboxes' (D-003, D-015). Pushed onto
the Mailboxes' stack it would leave the window at every switch of the
view button, the search field and its keyboard with it, and UIKit's back
button would take the corner where the view button stays. So the push and
the pop are pictures moved on UIKit's numbers, as the view button's
switch is.

**When things change their look.** B-066's rule holds: nothing changes its
look while it moves. Pictures move; the panes are laid out anew at the
tap, beneath, as before. Then two kinds of picture:

- *Laid out anew*, for what comes or stays: the list, the folders coming
  back, a list pushed in, the bar coming. Cut from each pane after the
  layout, while a picture of the whole screen as it was covers the glass.
  So the list is at its new width, its bar dressed, from the first frame
  that moves, as UIKit lays its columns out before it moves them, and
  its last frame is the screen beneath.
- *As it was*, for what goes or is cut off: the folders going, their
  column drawing in, a list popped off, the bar going, and the letter.
  WebKit draws the letter in another process and wraps it again in its
  own time, so no picture of it at its new width can be had at the tap.
  Its words go with its left edge and land where they now are.

So the end of the motion is the screen beneath but for the letter's line
ends, which change at once as the pictures go, as at a switch made at
once, where B-066 faded them over 0.2 s; and, from two panes with the
folders in front, the folders' title and counts, which move to the
column's new width then.

**What stays from B-066.** The cover takes every touch for the half
second, and VoiceOver reads the real panes beneath, final from the tap. A
change made while a list, the folders or the letter in the pictures
bounces past an end is made at once, with `pane motion: bouncing;
switched at once` in the connection log; one coasting is stopped first.
That holds for a pane hidden at the tap too. A change made at once hides
a pane that goes on springing back, and the next can come within the half
second: the list pulled down, "< Mailboxes" tapped and the open folder
tapped at once after it. The list coming back would be pictured as laid
out, past its top, and its rows would jump as the pictures went. The
cover goes before
anything else lays the panes out, as the iPad turns, as the app stops
being in front, and at a deadline a second after the motion's end. The
letter's actions and the view button's glyph hold still. "No message
selected" keeps to the middle of the pane. The highlights are in the
pictures as the panes are laid out: the open folder as the folders come
back, the open letter's row in the list. A picture that cannot be trusted
turns the motion down with a `pane motion:` line. The launch, a return
after a while away and the date jump stay instant.

**The cost.**

- The list changes its width and its bar at the tap, then moves: 45 pt
  on the 11-inch and 75 on the 10.2-inch the simulator runs, wider over
  the folders from three to two, narrower from two to three, where the
  darkened folders show through on its left. On a 12.9-inch, where the
  list is 377 pt in three panes, it narrows from three to two, and 2 pt
  of empty canvas show beside it until it covers them.
- The letter's line ends change at once at the end, not over 0.2 s.
- Darkening at a tenth and a shadow of a few per cent are hard to see on
  the app's dark panes.
- With Reduce Motion on, the panes now slide where they faded, as Mail's
  do.
- A list pushed in is pictured as it is at the tap: rows that come during
  the half second appear as the pictures go.

**Tests.** `PaneMoveTests`, now 26, 12 more, rewritten for the new model;
`PaneArrangementTests` the same 27, five changed.

- `PaneMove`, at every landscape width from 1024 to 1376 pt. What moves:
  the view button's three switches, a folder tapped in two panes and
  "< Mailboxes"; nothing for no change. Each move written out at 1194 and
  1366, with Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions too. The list keeps its width
  and its right edge rides the letter's left edge at every twentieth of
  the way. The folders go half the list's travel the same way, and 30% of
  the column in the stack. What is darkened and what casts a shadow, from
  and to what. What is pictured as laid out and what as it was, each
  checked against the columns alone. The last frame is the screen
  beneath, or under a picture that is, or past the column's edge, but for
  the letter. The lines ride their edges; everything is rigid and
  sideways and goes one way; only the real screen meant to show shows,
  every half point, every twentieth; the backdrop at the letter's right
  from three to two; the actions' plate; the view buttons painted over;
  the letter with its left edge; the empty pane's words in its middle;
  every pane pictured looked at for a bounce, hidden or not; where a
  list rests, as before. The
  spring: 0.5 s, mass 3, stiffness 1000, damping squared four times their
  product. The curve: half the way at 0.092 s, 90% at 0.213, 99% at
  0.364, the formula at every thousandth, never back and never past the
  end. The bars, 0.35 s, (0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1), half the column; the
  cross-fade's curve, (0.42, 0, 0.58, 1). Mail's rule for Reduce Motion
  and Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions. The product spec's rule for moving
  panes (`spec/docs/UI_SPEC.md`), read against `Theme` and the model:
  the view button, "< Mailboxes" and a folder tap, half a second on the
  spring, black at a tenth, and the cross-fade.
- `PaneShell`: the view button, "< Mailboxes" and a folder tap in two
  panes say where the panes were; a folder tap in three, "< Mailboxes"
  with the folders in front, a folder opened another way and a return say
  nothing.
- `RootViewController` and `PaneMotion`, which are UIKit, are read. The
  container asks the model with Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions read at the
  tap and Reduce Motion asked nowhere, looks at the panes the model names
  for a bounce, and hands over all three view buttons. The motion cuts the
  screen as it was only in `cut`, and the panes as laid out only in
  `play`, after the cover with the screen as it was is up, and before
  that picture goes and anything moves; checks each picture against the
  model, as it was where it was and as laid out where it is now; moves on
  Core Animation's spring with `Theme`'s mass, stiffness, critical damping
  and duration, the bars on the bar clock, the cross-fade on its curves,
  and on nothing else; darkens and shadows as the model says; draws the
  corner's glyph only when the pictures move; never touches a real view,
  and never asks Reduce Motion.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. The motion of 0.4 s,
as B-066 slid: 302 in 3. UIKit's damping of 500 as asked: 3 in 1. A
stiffness of 500: 509 in 2. The curve eased in and out, not the spring:
507 in 1. The folders held still under the list, as in B-066: 23 in 3.
The folders going half the column under a pushed list: 21 in 2. The
folders not darkened from three to two: 11 in 2. The list's shadow going
rather than coming from three to two: 11 in 2. The list starting with its
left edge where it was rather than its right edge on the letter's: 200
in 3. The folders coming back pictured as they were: 4 in 2. The letter
pictured as laid out from three to two: 38 in 2. A pushed list coming in
from the left: 47 in 4. The bars sliding the list's way round: 4 in 2.
The bars on the panes' half second: 2 in 1. The view button's switch
faded with Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions: 3 in 1. Prefer Cross-Fade
Transitions ignored in the stack: 110 in 2. Only the panes on the
screen looked at for a bounce, as this change first had it: 103 in 3.
The product spec's rule put back as B-066 wrote it: 7 in 1. The stack
not cut off at the column:
787 in 3. "< Mailboxes" laid out with nothing moving: 2 in 2. A folder
tapped in two panes laid out with nothing moving: 4 in 2. Read from the
source: B-066's rule, Reduce Motion fading the stack, 2 in 1; the spring
given UIKit's damping of 500, 2 in 1; the panes laid out pictured from
the glass, not drawn first, 1 in 1; the screen as it was taken away

The full suite, serially, with nothing undone: 1,502 tests, 5 skipped,
none failing. The release build for the iPad links.

**Reviewed 2026-10-06, and fixed.** A review found two things, each fixed
in the text above. The product spec still gave B-066's rule: 0.6 s, no
dimming, and nothing but the view button's switch moving the panes. It
now says what is built (`spec/docs/UI_SPEC.md`, under "Do not animate
panes dramatically."), and a test reads it. And a bounce was looked for
only in the panes on the screen at the tap, where B-066 looked in every
pane it pictured. A pane hidden a moment before by a change made at once,
still springing back, was then pictured past its end and jumped as the
pictures went: a list pushed in and the folders coming back. Every pane
pictured is looked at again. The counts above are after the fixes.

w = 18.26 a second.

- *Against UIKit.* The probe of 2026-10-06, its own recording measured

next. "sa" and Return under the menu made a bubble hidden under it,
seen only once the menu closed. Each bubble tried did it, "Example,
Sam" as well as "Al", both in To. The keyboard hidden with its key,
the sheet dropped and the arrow landed on the bubble. With the
keyboard down from the start, UIKit put the menu under the bubble,
its arrow on it, as the simulator always had. Cancel's question,
which hangs from a bar button, was in its place.

**What it was.** Measured inside the running app. With the keyboard
up, the form sheet sits 53 points higher than without it. "Al" was at
(409, 107) in the window, 44 by 30. The menu was at (453, 55), 317 by
134, its body centred on the bubble, but UIKit chose the left arrow,

offset 0, the menu's top at the bubble's bottom.

The app's anchor is right. `RecipientField.bubbleTapped(_:)` hangs the
menu, an action sheet and so a popover on the iPad, from the bubble
and its bounds. It left the arrow's side to UIKit, which allows any.
On 16.5.1, with the sheet raised for the keyboard, UIKit picks the side
and the arrow's place from geometry out of date. Set again once the

alone, on an app freshly started.

**Changed.** The bubble's menu opens under the bubble or over it,
never beside it: its popover's `permittedArrowDirections` is
`[.up, .down]`, set with the anchor, before the menu goes up. Beside the
bubble, the menu covers the rest of its line, which is the line he
types on and every bubble after this one. Under it or over it, the menu
covers the rows below or the bar above, and the line stays in sight.
Where UIKit already chose up, as with the keyboard down and in the
simulator, nothing changes. Both composers use the one field for To,
Cc and Bcc, so the change is in all three, in the app's composer and
in the share sheet.

Tried on the iPad before it was built, set on the app's own menu as it

No other popover hangs from a view inside the sheet. The bubble's menu

## B-079 — FIXED 2026-10-07, 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20, changed a fourth time and seen on the iPad fixed. After "< Mailboxes" and a folder tap VoiceOver went to the letter's Flag, not to the folders or the list

**Found on the iPad, 2026-10-07**, at B-077's check 8: the test iPad on
iPadOS 16.5.1, the 11-inch, landscape, master 434422b, VoiceOver and its
Caption Panel on. Seen twice, the second time from a fresh launch, in
which Flag had never had VoiceOver's cursor.

**What he would hear.** Two panes, the list in front, a letter open in
the pane. At "< Mailboxes" the folders slid in and VoiceOver said "Flag,
Button": its cursor was on the letter's Flag, not on a folder. A tap on
the open folder brought the list back, and VoiceOver went to Flag again,
not to the list. With the pane empty it went to the view button in the
corner, "Show Mailboxes, Button": the right column, but not a folder and
not a row. Nothing of the pictures was read, during or after any move.
The view button's own switch put VoiceOver on the view button, as meant,
even while its pictures moved.

**The cause.** In `RootViewController.swift`, `backToMailboxes()` posted
`UIAccessibility.post(notification: .screenChanged, argument: nil)`, and
the folder tap in two panes (`mailboxList.onSelectMailbox`, in
`wireNavigation()`) did the same. With nil, VoiceOver chooses where to go.
The three panes sit side by side in one view, and on iPadOS 16 it went
to the reading pane's Flag when a letter was open, and to the view button
in the corner, in the folders' or the list's bar, when the pane was empty.
The folders' column being hidden a moment before did not decide it: with
the pane empty, the same hiding and the same cover ended in the right
column. The view button's switch names its
button (`.layoutChanged`), and that worked.

**What Mail does**, as far as it can be known here. Mail in a narrow
window is UIKit's navigation controller. UIKit's pop puts VoiceOver back
on what it was on before the push: the row that pushed. Its push names
nothing, and VoiceOver starts at the top of the new screen. Neither Mail
nor UIKit was heard with VoiceOver on the iPad.

**Fixed.**

1. *"< Mailboxes"* names the open folder's row, which
   `mailboxList.select(mailboxID:)` has just highlighted. If none of that
   row is in sight, it names the folders' table, and VoiceOver takes its
   first element. This is UIKit's pop.
2. *A folder tap in two panes* names the list's highlighted row, the
   letter being read, if any of it is in sight; else the first row wholly
   in sight, below the search field; else the list's table, whose first
   element is the search field at its top. The list is read after the
   shell has acted, since a folder opened has a new list.
   For the list brought back this is the pop's rule: where he was in it.
   For a new folder it is the top of the list, under its bar. UIKit's push
   would start in the bar, but the first thing in the list's bar is the
   view button, which belongs to the corner, not to the list.
3. *In sight* means between the table's bars and below the search
   field, which stays at the top of the list while it scrolls. The rows
   the table counts as on the screen include the ones under the bar and
   the search field. Once the list is scrolled, the first of them is
   partly or wholly under the search field. VoiceOver put on it would
   scroll the list to show it, or put its box on a row he cannot see.
   The first row wholly in sight does neither. The folders have no search
   field, so for them only the bars are left out.
4. Both stay `.screenChanged`: a pop and a push.
5. *Shown when posted.* The panes are hidden and shown in `arrange`,
   which the shell calls before it returns, before `arrange` can return
   early, and with nothing left for a later turn. The motion's cover is
   hidden from VoiceOver, but it lies over the panes as their sibling, not
   around them, and nothing of a real view is faded, moved or hidden by
   it. So the row or table named is in the window, shown and opaque when
   posted, and VoiceOver is not left on anything hidden. Nothing needs to
   be posted later.

**The other posts.** There are three in the app, all in
`RootViewController`: the view button's switch, which names its button
and is kept, and the two above. `PaneShell`, `PaneMotion` and the folders'
and the list's controllers post none. Two changes hide what VoiceOver may
be on and post nothing, and are not changed: a return after a while
away, in two panes with the folders in front, puts the list in front
(B-003), and the date jump across mailboxes puts a new list in place of
the one whose calendar was used. VoiceOver chooses after both, as before.

**Seen in the simulator, 2026-10-07**, an iPad (7th generation) on iPadOS
18.6, landscape, on the test account. The simulator has no VoiceOver, so
where VoiceOver goes was not seen. A scratch build of this change wrote
to the system log what each post named and its state at the post, on the
next turn and 0.8 s later. Two panes, a letter open: "< Mailboxes" named
the Inbox's row, highlighted; the Inbox tapped named the letter's row,
highlighted. Starred, a new folder with no rows, named the list's table,
and "< Mailboxes" then named Starred's row. The Inbox, opened anew, had
rows at once and named its first row. With the pane empty, "< Mailboxes"
named the Inbox's row, and the Inbox again the list's first row. At every
post the element named was in the window, on the screen, shown and
opaque, under nothing hidden from VoiceOver, with the cover up; the same
on the next turn, and 0.8 s later with the cover gone. When the Inbox
opened anew had its first page, its rows were put in again, and the row
named was then the second. Nothing on the screen changed.

**Seen again in the simulator, 2026-10-07**, the same way, with the rows
under the search field left out. The bars were read as they are: 70
points of bar over each table, 50 points of toolbar under the list, a
44.5-point search field in the list and none in the folders. The pane
empty, the Inbox scrolled 90 points, so that 6 points of its first row
showed below the search field: "< Mailboxes" named the Inbox's row, and
the Inbox tapped named the second row, the first wholly in sight. Taken
from the rows the table counts as on the screen, it would have been the
first.
A letter open, its row scrolled until 12 points of it showed: it was
named. Its row scrolled wholly under the bar: the fourth row was named,
the first wholly in sight. Sent Mail, opened anew with no rows yet,
named the list's table. Scrolled the same 90 points, "< Mailboxes" named
Sent Mail's row, and Sent Mail tapped named its second row. Nothing on
the screen moved. The simulator has no VoiceOver to move it.

**Tests.** `PaneArrangementTests`, now 28, one more:
`testVoiceOverIsPutWhereTheMoveTakesHim`, which reads `RootViewController`
and `PaneMotion`, as B-077's tests do. No post passes nil, and there are
three. The view button's names its twin in the corner. "< Mailboxes"
posts `.screenChanged` with the open folder's row or the folders' table,
after the highlight and after the shell has moved the panes. A folder tap
posts `.screenChanged`, in two panes only, after the tap, with the list's
highlighted row if any of it is in sight, else the first row wholly in
sight, below the search field, else its table, in that order, the list
read after the tap. What is in sight is worked out from the table's
bars and the band pinned at its top, not from the rows the table counts
as on the screen. The panes are hidden and shown in `arrange` before its
early return, with nothing left for later, and nothing else in the
container is hidden. The motion hides only its cover
from VoiceOver, and puts it on the container's view.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. "< Mailboxes" naming
nothing: 2 in 1. The folder tap naming nothing: 2 in 1. "< Mailboxes"
naming the folders' table alone: 1 in 1. The folder tap naming the
folders: 1 in 1. The list read before the tap: 1 in 1. No first row:
1 in 1. The first row before the highlighted one: 1 in 1. "< Mailboxes"
posted before the panes move: 1 in 1. "< Mailboxes" as a layout change,
not a screen change: 2 in 1. The panes hidden and shown on the next
turn: 2 in 1. The panes hidden and shown after the early return: 3 in 1.
The motion hiding the list from VoiceOver: 1 in 1. With the rows under
the search field left out, the two undone in the choosing were undone
again: no first row, 1 in 1; the first row before the highlighted one,
1 in 1. And six more. The first row taken from the rows the table counts
as on the screen, as before: 1 in 1. The search field not left out:
1 in 1. The bar over the table not left out: 1 in 1. The toolbar under
it not left out: 1 in 1. The highlighted row named with none of it in
sight: 1 in 1. A first row named with only part of it in sight: 1 in 1.
Eighteen in all, each caught, with nothing failing in any run but the
test named.

The full suite, serially, with nothing undone: 1,580 tests, 5 skipped,
none failing. The release build for the iPad links.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-07**, iPadOS 16.5.1, the 11-inch,
landscape, built from the first change with B-078, VoiceOver and its
Caption Panel on. A tap went straight to the control and did not move
VoiceOver, so each step was done with taps. The caption and its box were
read from frames taken in bursts from each tap. Steps 1, 4, 6 and 7 of the
TODO's check passed. Steps 2, 3 and 5 did not.

- *Step 1 passed*, four times. At "< Mailboxes" VoiceOver went to the open
  folder's row, highlighted, at about 1.3 s, and stayed there. It never
  said "Flag, Button", in the run that began on Flag as well.
- *Step 4 passed.* The pane empty, "< Mailboxes" put VoiceOver on Sent
  Mail's row, not on the view button. Sent Mail tapped again: on its first
  row at 1.3 s, read to the end, and the list did not move.
- *Step 6 passed.* "Hide Mailboxes, Button" at 1.5 s, and "Show Mailboxes,
  Button" at 1.5 s, the box on the corner button.
- *Step 7 passed.* In fourteen bursts nothing of the pictures was read.
  While a move ran, the caption kept what it had said before.
- *Step 2 failed once in three.* The open folder tapped, VoiceOver went to
  the letter's row at 1.4 s, and the list did not move. In one run, at
  2.75 s, it went to the pane's Flag and stayed. Nothing in the list
  changed but the box.
- *Step 3 failed* in each folder with letters. Sent Mail: at 1.3 s
  VoiceOver was on the view button in the corner, and stayed. Important:
  at 1.3 s its box was round the first row while it read the second row's
  words, and at 2.2 s it went to the view button. The Inbox opened anew:
  the view button. Starred, with no letters, passed: the search field at
  1.3 s. The pane was empty each time.
- *Step 5 failed* where the list moved. VoiceOver went to the right rows.
  The pane empty, the Inbox scrolled 40 points, its first row 40 points
  under the search field: VoiceOver went to the second row, the first
  wholly below the search field, and as it did, the list went back the 40
  points to its top. The letter's row half under the search field:
  VoiceOver went to it, and the list moved 48 points, so that the row
  showed whole below the search field.

**What did it.**

- *Step 3: the folder's fresh page.* A folder opened draws its page kept
  on the iPad at once (`showKeptPage`), and the post named a cell of it.
  The folder's newest page came 0.4 to 0.9 s after the tap, before
  VoiceOver had got there, and was drawn over the kept one
  (`landFreshPage`, `regroup`). `reloadData` hands every cell out again,
  the same letters or not. At 1.3 s VoiceOver took the cell it had been
  given, which by then showed another row: in Important, the first row's
  box and the second row's words. Then it let go of it and took the first
  element itself, the view button in the list's bar. Starred had no rows,
  and its table, which was named, is not handed out. The simulator had
  shown this, the row named then the second, and it was taken for
  nothing, as nothing on the screen changed.
- *Step 2: most likely a reload of the list under VoiceOver.* Not caught
  on the iPad, where the connection log could not be read. VoiceOver let
  go of the row as in step 3, with nothing changed on the screen, and took
  Flag, as it did before the first change. With the folder already open,
  the list reloads only in `regroup`. The watch's check every 30 s reloads it when it puts a letter come
  or gone on the list, which it does with the list at its top, as it was
  (`showNewsIfAtTop`), and when the list is owed a fetch afresh. A check
  with nothing new reloads nothing. A letter gone below the rows in sight
  changes nothing on the screen, and letters of other checks come into
  the test account's Inbox and go from it. In the simulator, 31 s after
  the same tap, the watch took a letter gone from the Inbox off the list
  and reloaded it. A read mark or a Flag the server refused reloads it
  too. *Not so, as the third round showed: nothing in the app ran when
  VoiceOver left the row. It leaves by itself, once in a launch
  (2026-10-19, below).*
- *Step 5: VoiceOver's own scroll*, not the app's. The tap on the open
  folder puts its list back in front with nothing fetched. What moves the
  list in the app is `regroup`, which keeps the rows in sight where they
  are, or goes to the top for a list replaced or for news put on at the
  top, which needs the list at its top already; `scrollToTop`; Go to
  Date's scroll to its day; and the motion, which stops a list still
  coasting. None of them runs then. On the iPad the list was still at
  0.85 s, with the motion over, and had moved at 1.3 s, as VoiceOver
  landed. In the simulator, with a build that logged every change of the
  list's place, the same steps moved nothing in the 4 s after the tap.
  Each move on the iPad was the part of a row that was under the search
  field. In the first, that row was the list's first, 40 points under,
  and showing it whole is going back to the top. The row VoiceOver was put
  on was whole already. In the second, it was the letter's row, 48 points
  under. So as VoiceOver takes up the list, UIKit shows whole the row it
  is put on, or the row just above it, when part of that row is under the
  search field. Which of them it picks is UIKit's. The app's sums were
  right: the row named was wholly in sight. *Only in part, as the third
  round showed: a row named with part of it under the search field is put
  in the middle of the list, or the list taken to its top, not shown whole
  with the least scroll. The 48 points were most likely that, stopped at
  the top (2026-10-19, below).*

**Changed again, 2026-10-07.**

1. *VoiceOver kept on its letter.* When the list's rows are drawn again
   with VoiceOver on a row of the list, or just sent to one, VoiceOver goes
   after it to the cell that now shows the same letter, with a layout
   change. The row is taken before the reload by its letters, and found
   after it as `ListPlace` finds a row he could see: by the conversation's
   newest letter, else by any letter in it. Its letter gone: the row now in
   its place, the one that came after it, or the last. That row out of
   sight: the first row wholly in sight, as after a move. No rows: the
   table. It is done at the end of the reload, with the list where it goes
   and the highlight back (`keepVoiceOver` in `MessageListViewController`;
   the choosing in `ListVoiceOver`).
2. *On a row* is VoiceOver's own element (`UIAccessibility.focusedElement`):
   one of the list's cells, or something inside one, or the element UIKit
   gives VoiceOver for a row, whose container is the table, found by where
   it is and not on the search band. Anything else is not a row: the
   list's own bar, its table and its search field, the folders, the
   reading pane, a sheet. Then nothing is posted, unless VoiceOver has just
   been sent to a row (3). While he types in the search field, or
   VoiceOver is on a key, nothing is posted at all. Nor with the list's
   column out of sight, as after "< Mailboxes": the row sent to is let go.
   With VoiceOver off nothing is posted.
3. *Just sent to one.* The folder tap in two panes asks the list where
   VoiceOver goes (`placeVoiceOver`), by the same rules as before, and the
   list holds that row for VoiceOver until it has been on it through the
   folder's fresh page, or for 3 s at most. On the iPad the screen change
   landed 1.3 to 1.6 s after the tap. If, before it has been on the row,
   VoiceOver goes to another of the list's rows, to a cell drawn since for
   another letter, or to the list's own bar or table, it is put on the row
   it was sent to, once. On the iPad, in Sent Mail and the Inbox, it went
   straight to the view button, in the list's bar. On the folders, the
   reading pane or a sheet the row stays held while VoiceOver is on its
   way, until 1.6 s (`ListVoiceOver.screenChange`), and is let go after.
   VoiceOver is never taken from there. When he types, the row is let go.

   The list's own post after the fresh page can take VoiceOver to the row
   before the screen change lands, and the screen change then lands after
   it, on the cell it named. So when VoiceOver got to the row after a post
   of the list's own, the row stays held until 1.6 s, and a landing on
   another row or on the list's bar in that time is put back on the row,
   once. Which of the two VoiceOver takes first on the iPad is not known.
   In each order it ends on the row, or is put there once. Any other move
   after VoiceOver has been on the row lets it go: he may have moved on.
4. *Once.* A reload posts once, at its end, and a post reloads nothing, so
   nothing repeats. A landing is put back at most once: the row is let go
   as it is. So the list now posts too, layout changes only; the
   container's three posts are as before.
5. *The reloads.* There are three, all in the list, and each now keeps
   VoiceOver. `regroup`, at every change of the letters: the fresh page
   over the kept one, which was step 3; the watch's news put on at the top
   and a fetch afresh it is owed, likely step 2; a page below or above,
   which VoiceOver reaches by moving down the list; a read mark at a tap,
   and one or a Flag the server refused; a Refresh, a return after a while
   away, a search and its end; the reading pane's and Edit mode's Delete,
   Move and Flag; Settings saved; Drafts and the Outbox changing. The kept
   page, drawn once as the list is made, before anything names it. Go to
   Date's day, drawn as its sheet goes. The ones he starts from a button,
   a sheet or the reading pane find VoiceOver there, not on a row, and
   post nothing. A preview fills its row in place and is not a reload.
6. *A reload with the same rows is not skipped.* `regroup` reloads at every
   call, whether anything changed or not: the fresh page with the kept
   page's letters, a Refresh with nothing new, Settings saved with the same
   addresses. Skipping it is not certain to be safe. A row's time is worked
   out from now as the row is drawn, so a reload with the same letters is
   what turns "9:34 AM" into "Yesterday" after midnight, at the Refresh
   after a night. Settings draws the rows again for his addresses with the
   same letters, and VoiceOver's words for a row are set only as it is
   drawn. A skip would have to know all of those. With the change a reload
   no longer takes VoiceOver off its row, so it is left.
7. *Step 5 is left.* The move is VoiceOver's, to show a row whole. The
   TODO's step now expects it. It was taken here to be by less than a
   row. It is not: for a row it cannot see whole, VoiceOver puts the row
   in the middle of the list, or takes the list to its top, 230 and 284
   points on the iPad for rows 38 and 29 points under the search field.
   Since the third change the app shows the row whole first (2026-10-19,
   below).
8. The sums of what is in sight, which "< Mailboxes" and the folder tap
   used, and which the list now uses after a reload, are in one place:
   `UITableView.voiceOverPlace(at:orFirstRow:)`.

follows its letter across a reload; there on the kept page, held through

Its three reloads are the only ones, and there is no other kind. Each takes

The row is from VoiceOver's own element, only with it on. A row of the list

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-19**, iPadOS 16.5.1, the 11-inch,
landscape, built from the second change with B-080 to B-083, VoiceOver
and its Caption Panel on. A tap went straight to the control, as before.
The caption and its box were read from bursts of frames taken from each
tap, about 45 bursts and 860 frames. Steps 1, 3, 4, 5a, 6, 7 and 8 of the
TODO's check passed. Steps 2 and 5b did not.

- *Step 1 passed*, in 16 runs with a letter open, begun on the row, on
  Flag or on the view button. VoiceOver went to the open folder's row,
  highlighted, at 1.1 to 1.35 s, and stayed. It never said "Flag,
  Button". In 6 runs with the pane empty it went to the folder's row too.
- *Step 3 passed.* Sent Mail: its fresh page at about 1.1 s, VoiceOver on
  the first row at 1.39 s, its box and its words that row's to 8.2 s.
  Important: the fresh page at 0.83 s, the first row at 1.40 s, held to
  8.2 s. The Inbox opened anew: the first row at 1.42 s, and the fresh
  page after it, at about 1.55 s; VoiceOver stayed on the row's letter
  through it, to 8.1 s. It never touched the view button or another row
  on the way. Starred, with no letters: the search field at 1.40 s.
- *Step 4 passed.* The pane empty, "< Mailboxes" put VoiceOver on the
  Inbox's row at 1.12 s, and the Inbox tapped again on its first row at
  1.42 s. The list did not move.
- *Step 5a passed.* The Inbox scrolled about 40 points, its first row
  that much under the search field, the pane empty: VoiceOver went to the
  second row at 1.15 s, the first wholly below the search field, and as
  it landed the list went back about 39 points to its top. It moved no
  further.
- *Step 6 passed.* "Show Mailboxes, Button" at 1.16 s and "Hide Mailboxes,
  Button" at 1.14 s, the box on the corner button.
- *Step 7 passed.* Nothing of the pictures was read. While a move ran,
  the caption kept what it had said before.
- *Step 8 passed.* Refresh fetched the page and drew the list again, and
  VoiceOver stayed on the letter's row, its box and its words, to 8.9 s.
  It was still there after 45 s, through two checks for new mail.
- *Step 2 failed once in 15.* In the first run VoiceOver was on the
  letter's row at 1.11 s, then at 2.27 s went to the reading pane's Flag,
  and stayed. The list did not move. The other 14 stayed on the row for 5
  to 12 s.
- *Step 5b failed.* VoiceOver went to the letter's row each time, but the
  list moved far more than the part of it under the search field. The
  third row, 38 points under: the list went about 230 points, to its top,
  twice. The sixth row, 29 points under: the list moved about 284 points
  before the caption changed, and the row ended in the middle of the
  list, with the third row now half under the search field. Then the list
  stayed.

**What did it.** Both tried again on the iPad the same day.

- *Step 2: VoiceOver choosing again by itself*, once in each launch of the
  app. In five runs of the app, each from its launch, VoiceOver left the
  row by itself once. After a fresh launch, four times in four, it was the
  first tap on the open folder. With a letter open, three times, VoiceOver
  was on the letter's row at 1.14 to 1.15 s, then on Flag at 2.01 to
  2.03 s, about 0.9 s after it got there. Not the letter: with the pane
  empty it went from the list's first row, at 1.15 s, to the view button
  in the corner, "Show Mailboxes, Button", at 2.03 s. Not the time since
  the launch: the same after 150 s. Not the view button's switches before
  it, which passed. With VoiceOver turned on while the app ran, it was
  "< Mailboxes" instead: on the Inbox's row at 1.33 s, on Flag at 2.22 s.
  Every later run of each launch passed. The connection log had nothing
  near the tap or the move: the watch's checks went 22 s before the tap
  and 8 s after the move. In the run that failed first, a check had gone
  at the tap itself, with nothing new; in these none did, and VoiceOver
  left all the same. No fetch, no reload: nothing in the app ran. So the
  cause named after the first round, a reload under VoiceOver, was wrong.
  Why it stuck was the app's. VoiceOver there, with the fresh page drawn
  and nothing posted by the list since, the row was let go at once
  (`ListVoiceOver.moved`). The move to Flag, which is not the list's, or
  to the view button, came after that, and was never put back. After
  "< Mailboxes" nothing held the folder's row at all. *In the third
  round the move came only with VoiceOver on as the app started, after a
  screen change of iPadOS's own, and the app never saw it (2026-10-19,
  the third change, below).*
- *Step 5b: VoiceOver's scroll, for a row the app named that it could not
  see whole.* With VoiceOver off the same steps moved nothing: the app
  does not scroll there. The highlighted row is named while any of it is
  in sight (`voiceOverPlace(at:orFirstRow:)`). VoiceOver put on a row
  partly under the search field scrolls it in itself, and puts it in the
  middle of the list, between the bars, or takes the list to its top when
  the middle cannot be reached. It does not make the least move. A row
  wholly in sight just below the search field it did not move, in two
  runs. The 48 points seen on 2026-10-07 were most likely the same, the
  row put in the middle and the list stopped at its top. The TODO's "just
  enough, no further" and the note that VoiceOver's scroll is by less
  than a row rested on a wrong reading of UIKit.
- *Step 5a* moved the list too, back to its top, with the row named
  wholly in sight. Why is not known. It was by the part of the first row
  under the search field.

**Changed a third time, 2026-10-19.**

1. *The row held after VoiceOver is there.* The row a folder tap sends
   VoiceOver to is held for 3 s from the tap (`ListVoiceOver.bound`),
   before VoiceOver is on it and after. A reload while it is held moves it
   to its letter's row, as before, and it stays held; it is no longer let
   go at the fresh page, or once VoiceOver is there. Once VoiceOver has
   been on it, a move to what he could not have reached from a row by a
   swipe is VoiceOver's own, and VoiceOver is put back on the row, once,
   with a layout change. That is the reading pane (`beside`, with the
   folders, which are hidden then), and the list's bar, with the view
   button and "< Mailboxes" (`listBar`): the search field is between the
   rows and the bar. A move to another row, the search field, the toolbar,
   a sheet or the keys is his, and lets the row go with nothing posted. In
   the Outbox, which has no search field, a swipe from the first row
   reaches the end of the bar, Edit, and the next its title: a move to
   those is his. Its view button and "< Mailboxes" are further on, and a
   move there is put back, as in any other folder: on the iPad VoiceOver
   went by itself to the view button with the pane empty, and the Outbox's
   pane is always empty. The 3 s covers every leave seen, 2.0 to 2.3 s
   after the tap, and 2.75 s on 2026-10-07. The list no longer tells
   `ListVoiceOver` whether its rows are the kept page: the row is held the
   same either way.
2. *The folder's row held after "< Mailboxes".* The container holds the
   open folder's row the same way (`FoldersVoiceOver`). Once VoiceOver has
   been on it, within 3 s of the tap, a move to the view button in the
   corner (`corner`) or to the reading pane (`pane`) is put back on the
   row, once. Not the reading pane from the last folder: the folders'
   toolbar is hidden, and so is the list's column, so a swipe of his from
   the last folder goes straight into the reading pane, and that move is
   his (`isLast`, `voiceOverIsLast`). The rest of the folders' bar is a
   swipe from the first folder, and a move there is his, as one to another
   folder is. Before VoiceOver is on the row nothing is put back: it is on
   its way, and may still be on Flag or on "< Mailboxes". The folders'
   table, named when none of the row is in sight, is not held. The folders
   out of sight, the row is let go.
3. *Let go.* A row he opens or ticks in the list lets the list's row go. A
   folder tapped lets the folders' row go. The view button lets both go
   before it names its twin in the corner. The list out of sight lets its
   row go, as before.
4. *Once.* A row is put back at most once, and is let go as it is put
   back. With VoiceOver off nothing is held, so nothing is put back.
5. *The row shown whole first.* Before VoiceOver is put on a row, the
   app shows it whole with the least scroll, if part of it is under the
   search band or a bar (`showWhole(forVoiceOver:)`): down by the part
   under the band, or up by the part under the toolbar, never so far that
   its top goes under the band, and never past the list's top or its end.
   VoiceOver then has nothing to scroll. Only while VoiceOver is running:
   with it off the list never moves for it. For the tap on the open folder
   in two panes it is done before the panes move, while the list is still
   hidden (`showHighlightedRowWhole`), so the motion's pictures are cut
   where the list now is, and it does not jump as they go. Done after,
   the list would jump by the part of the row that was hidden, as the
   cover went. The same for the folder's row at "< Mailboxes", while the
   folders are hidden. A row the list names after a reload, or puts back
   after a leave, is shown whole the same way, and so is the folder's row
   put back. A row with none of it in sight is not named and not moved;
   the first row wholly in sight is named, as before, and needs no scroll.
6. *The sums in one place.* What is in sight and the least scroll are
   worked out in `TableSight`, which the suite runs, from the table's
   offset, height, bars, band and rows (`voiceOverSight`). The rows
   VoiceOver is on, the list's and the folders', are found in one place
   (`voiceOverRow(of:besides:)`), as the list found its own before.
7. *The letter's text found by where it is.* WebKit gives VoiceOver the
   letter's text from its own process, and its elements there are neither
   views nor UIKit's, so no view leads from them (`voiceOverHolder(of:)`).
   Found only by the view it is in, a leave into the text would be taken
   as anything else, and let go. So an element that leads to no view is
   found by where it is: the middle of its frame on a view's part of the
   screen, with nothing presented over the window (`voiceOverHolds`). The
   list and the container tell every landing apart this way: the reading
   pane, the list's column and bar, the view button in the corner. On
   16.5.1 the leave went to the native Flag each time a letter was open,
   never into the text.

  row stayed half hidden to 8.5 s.
- *Step 6 passed.* "Show Mailboxes, Button" at 0.98 and 1.10 s, and "Hide
  Mailboxes, Button" at 1.09 s, the box on the corner button.
- *Step 7 passed.* Nothing of the pictures was read. While a move ran,
  the caption kept what it had said before.
- *Step 8 passed.* Refresh fetched the page and drew the list again, and
  VoiceOver stayed on the letter's row to 8.5 s, then for 49 s more,
  through three checks for new mail.
- *Step 9c passed*, twice. Blackmail opened with VoiceOver off, then
  VoiceOver turned on: at "< Mailboxes" VoiceOver was on the Inbox's row,
  and at the Inbox on the letter's row, and it did not leave.
- *Step 9a failed.* Blackmail ended and opened again with VoiceOver kept
  on, a letter open, "< Mailboxes", then the Inbox. "< Mailboxes" held the
  Inbox's row each time. At the Inbox VoiceOver was on the letter's row
  at 1.04 to 1.06 s, then on the reading pane's Flag at 1.91 to 1.94 s,
  and it stayed there. It was never put back: 6 launches in 7. The one
  that held was the first launch after VoiceOver had been turned on again
  in Settings. A second try in the same launch held, as before. Tried
  again later, 2 launches in 2.
- *Step 9b failed*, the same with the pane empty: VoiceOver on the first
  row at 1.05 s, then on the view button in the corner, "Show Mailboxes,
  Button", at 1.90 to 1.92 s, and never put back. 3 launches in 3, and
  tried again later, 5 in 5, one of them with the app started again only
  8 s after it ended.
- *Step 5b failed under the toolbar*, twice, and again when tried once
  more.
  The letter's row half under the toolbar: as the list slid in it was
  moved up by the hidden part, the row whole, its bottom on the toolbar's
  top. As VoiceOver landed on the row, at about 1.05 s, the list moved
  about 295 points, and the row was in the middle of the list. It stayed
  there.

**What did it.** Both from the iPad's own system log.

- *Steps 9a and 9b: the app never saw VoiceOver leave.* Once in each
  launch with VoiceOver on as the app started, iPadOS posted a screen
  change of its own, naming nothing, 0.9 s after the folder tap and 0.8 s
  after the app's. VoiceOver got to the row at 0.97 s. At 1.8 s it acted
  on iPadOS's screen change by taking the app's first element: the
  reading pane's Flag with a letter open, the view button in the corner
  with the pane empty. Nothing in the app ran then: the connection log was
  idle, and the app posted nothing from the tap to 9 s. With VoiceOver
  turned on while the app ran, iPadOS posted no such screen change, and
  VoiceOver did not leave.
  The leave was within 3 s, to the reading pane or the list's bar, and
  the list should have put VoiceOver back. It did not, because it told
  VoiceOver's moves apart by the element each move's notification named,
  and on the iPad that came to nothing: an element the list could not
  find, or no notification at all. So the landing on the row and the
  leave were both taken as elsewhere. Before 1.6 s that keeps the row held
  but not reached; after it, it lets the row go, silently. A Refresh
  drawn at 1.9 s, inside the 3 s, with VoiceOver already on the view
  button, named no row: the row had been let go. VoiceOver itself, asked
  where it was, did name the row: later in a launch where it had left the
  row, a Refresh with VoiceOver on a row put it back on that row's cell,
  found that way. And a Refresh tapped at 1.1 s, before the leave, posted
  the row at 1.37 s, after iPadOS's screen change, and VoiceOver stayed on
  the row to 8.4 s: the row posted then, before VoiceOver acted on that
  screen change, kept it there.
  The container's hold of the folder's row worked the same way, and could
  not have seen a leave either.
- *Step 5b under the toolbar: VoiceOver wants the row clear of it.* The
  app's least scroll did as meant, before the panes moved, and left the
  row's bottom on the toolbar's top. The second move came as VoiceOver
  landed, with nothing fetched and nothing drawn again: VoiceOver's own.
  Tried seven more times with the row already whole, so that the app
  moved nothing: VoiceOver put the row in the middle of the list when it
  ended 4, 9, 25 or 26.5 points above the toolbar, and left it where it
  was at 29, 32.5 and 42.5 points. At the top it left alone a row just
  below the search field, as step 5b under it showed.

**Changed a fourth time, 2026-10-20.**

1. *VoiceOver asked where it is.* The list and the container no longer
   take where VoiceOver went from the notification of its move. At each
   move, while a row is held, they ask VoiceOver itself
   (`UIAccessibility.focusedElement`) on the next turn, after VoiceOver's
   own move, and tell that apart as before. And in case no move is told
   at all, they ask it every tenth of a second while the row is held,
   from the tap to 3 s (`ListVoiceOver.bound`), on a timer on the main
   run loop that a scroll does not hold up. At a tick, what VoiceOver is
   on is told apart only when it is another object than at the last look
   (`FocusWatch`). VoiceOver on nothing, as it may be for a moment as it
   moves, is passed over: the row stays held, and the next look tells
   apart where it went. The ticks stop at 3 s, when the row is let go, and
   once it is put back: about 30 looks at most. None run with VoiceOver
   off, or with nothing held. The same for the folder's row after
   "< Mailboxes".
2. *The row by its place.* VoiceOver on the row it was sent to is now
   told by the row alone, which the list works out for its letter at each
   look. The row's words were compared too, and UIKit's element for a row
   need not have the cell's words. A landing on the right row would then
   have been taken as another row, put back at once and let go, and a
   later leave left where it went.
3. *The rules as before.* What is put back, from where, and once; never
   with VoiceOver off; never after a move of his: another row, the search
   field while he types, a key, a sheet. A row he opens or ticks, a folder
   tapped, the view button, and the list or the folders out of sight let
   the rows go, as before, and now stop the ticks too.
4. *Clear of the toolbar.* A row counts as wholly in sight only if it
   ends at least 32 points, a third of a row, above the toolbar
   (`TableSight.voiceOverBottomClearance`). The least scroll lifts a row
   that far: by the part under the toolbar and 32 points more, or, for a
   row in sight but ending closer to the toolbar, by what is missing. 32
   points, as VoiceOver left the row at 29 and put it in the middle at
   26.5. Never so far that its top goes under the search field, and never
   past the list's ends: the last row at the list's end stays where it
   is. The top has no clearance. The same sums serve the folders.

**Tests of the fourth change.** `ListVoiceOverTests`, now 54, 9 more, and
two changed. The ticks: run only from a send with a row held; stop for
good once none is, at the bound, let go or put back, until the next send;
none with VoiceOver off or the table named; a tenth of a second, 30 looks
in the bound. A tick tells VoiceOver's element apart only on another
object than the last seen, the first look always. The looks as the list
makes them, fed by what VoiceOver is on: the leave seen on the iPad, from
the folder's row to the letter's row at 1.0 s and to Flag or the view
button at 1.9 s, looked at three times, put back once at the first tick
after the leave, the ticks then stopped; told as nothing, as on the iPad,
the row let go with nothing put back. VoiceOver on nothing for a moment
after the row, at a tick and at the look after a move: passed over, the
row still held, and the leave to Flag or the view button a tenth of a
second later put back once; told apart, nothing would have let the row
go. A look after a move and a tick: put back once.
VoiceOver kept on the row: looked at once, the ticks stopped at the
bound. A move of his to another row: let go, nothing put back, the ticks
stopped. VoiceOver off or the table named: no ticks, nothing looked at.
The folder's row the same way, put back once at the first tick after its
leave to the reading pane or the view button, and held through VoiceOver
on nothing just before that leave. The least scroll: a row
under the toolbar lifted by the part under it and 32 points more, the
seventh row 58.5 points where the third change moved it 26.5; a row
ending 0 to 29 points above the toolbar lifted by what is missing of 32,
one 10 points above by 22; one 32 points above or more, or within half a
point of it, not moved; a row that cannot end that far above the toolbar
without its top going under the band, only to the band; a row just below
the band whole; the last row at the list's end not moved, and with the
load-more footer under it lifted the whole 56.5 points.

`PaneArrangementTests`, now 30, one more:
`testVoiceOverIsAskedWhereItIsWhileARowIsHeld`, which reads the list, the
container and the timer. Neither reads the element a move's notification
names. At a move, while a row is held, each asks VoiceOver on the next
turn; VoiceOver on nothing is passed over; at a tick, it tells the
element apart only on another object. The
ticks go on only while VoiceOver runs and the row is held, and stop, the
timer invalidated, at the bound, once the row is put back, and wherever
the row is let go. The timer is made in one place, every tenth of a
second, repeating, on the main run loop in its common modes, and started
only as a row is sent to. The two B-079 tests now read the ticks started
after the send, the letting go that stops them, and the row told by its
place alone.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. In `FocusWatch`: every
look told apart, 15 in 7; the first look after a start not always told
apart, 1 in 1; a start keeping what was seen before it, 1 in 1; the ticks
going on with nothing held, 5 in 2; started with nothing held, 5 in 2; a
look told apart after the ticks stopped, 2 in 1. In the list: the element
named by a move told apart again, 4 in 2; VoiceOver asked on the same
turn as its move, 2 in 1; no ticks at the send, 2 in 2; the ticks not
stopped when the row is let go, 1 in 1; not stopped at the bound, 1 in 1;
not stopped once the row is put back, 1 in 1; every tick telling the
element apart, 1 in 1; ticks with VoiceOver off, 1 in 1; the row sent to
known by its words again, 2 in 1; a row opened stopping no ticks, 3 in 2;
VoiceOver on nothing told apart, as elsewhere, 1 in 1. In the container:
VoiceOver not asked where it is, 2 in 1; no ticks at "< Mailboxes", 2 in
2; a folder tap stopping no ticks, 3 in 2; the ticks not stopped once the
row is put back or at the bound, 1 in 1; every tick telling the element
apart, 1 in 1; VoiceOver on nothing told apart, 1 in 1. The timer in the main run loop's
default mode only, which a scroll holds up, 1 in 1. In `TableSight`: no
clearance, 21 in 3; a row in the clearance taken as whole, 14 in 1; a row
lifted only to the toolbar, 14 in 3; a clearance at the top too, 4 in 4;
a row lifted with its top under the band, 2 in 2. Twenty-nine in all,
each caught, with nothing failing in any run but the tests named.

The full suite, serially, with nothing undone: 1,728 tests, 5 skipped,
none failing. The release build for the iPad links.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-20, the fourth change**, iPadOS
16.5.1, VoiceOver and its Caption Panel on, each move watched to about
8 s, with the iPad's own log of VoiceOver beside it. Every step passed.
VoiceOver left the row by itself 15 times: in each fresh launch and in
the first move of a session, about 0.9 s after iPadOS's own screen
change, it took Flag or the view button. Each time the app saw it,
asking VoiceOver where it was, and put it back 8 to 30 ms later.
VoiceOver was on the row again within about a second, its own time to
move, and stayed. The open folder tapped held 6 times in a session;
from a fresh launch with a letter open, 7 launches; with the pane empty,
4; launched with VoiceOver off and turned on after, twice. A new folder
held its first row through its fresh page. A letter's row half under
the search field, and half under the toolbar, twice each, came in whole
before the move, the one under the toolbar 32 pt clear of it, and
nothing moved after VoiceOver landed. The view button, the pictures
unread, and the rows drawn again under a Refresh and through a check
for new mail, as before. Not done: the last folder's line in 1 (the

**Not covered.**

- The fourth change was not heard. The simulator has no VoiceOver, and the

- VoiceOver's leave was seen on iPadOS 16.5.1 only, a tap there going
  straight to the control: once in each launch with VoiceOver on as the

- Whether VoiceOver's moves are told to the app on the iPad, and with

- The folder's row was never left by VoiceOver on the iPad, so its

- A leave from the row to another row, the search field or the toolbar

- A touch of his own on the reading pane or the list's bar within 3 s of

- A leave into the letter's text is found by where it is: WebKit gives

- VoiceOver reads the row again at each reload under it.
- The folders' table is drawn again at each sweep of the counts, and
  VoiceOver on a folder's row could lose it the same way. Not changed: a

- In Edit mode the list's highlighted row is the first one ticked, not
  the letter being read.
- A highlighted row wholly out of sight is not named, and not moved. In
  the folders the table is named, and VoiceOver takes its first element.

- What Mail does with VoiceOver was not heard on the iPad.

## B-080 — CHANGED 2026-10-07, seen in the iPadOS 18 simulator and on the iPad but for a Wednesday. Every folder but Sent Mail, Drafts and the Outbox ended a conversation's names with its count; Mail has no count on any row and marks a conversation after the date

**Asked** in B-075, 2026-10-06. B-075 took the count off the rows of
Sent Mail, Drafts and the Outbox and marked a conversation there with
Mail's blue chevron in a circle after the date. Every other folder kept
its count on the names and had no mark: "Carlo, Margaret (3)" in the
Inbox, All Mail, Trash, Spam, Important, Starred and his own folders.
The names' line is short, 138 points in three panes on the 7th
generation iPad simulated here, and is cut at its end, so under a long
list of who wrote the count went off it with the names. And one
conversation looked two ways: the same two letters read "Carlo (2)" in
the Inbox and had the mark in Sent Mail (B-075, b075-10). The question
was put to the owner under "Blocked on the owner": keep the count, or
the mark there too. His ruling, 2026-10-07: the mark, as Mail.

**What Mail does**, as B-075 found it from Mail's list code in the iOS
18.6 runtime and from published screenshots. No count on any row of
the message list, in any mailbox. A conversation is marked by a small
blue chevron in a circle, `chevron.forward.circle`, at the right end of
the top line, just after the date. The names are cut before the date,
so they never push the mark off. A single letter has no mark in the
iPad's list. How many letters a conversation holds is shown only once
it is open, as "N Messages" on the iPhone. Mail's strings have "%@
messages", most likely for VoiceOver.

**Changed.**

1. *No count* (`MessageThread.displayRow`). A conversation's row has no
   count after its names, in every folder. The names are as they were:
   who wrote, the newest first, each once, joined by commas, "Carlo,
   Margaret". Only the count goes. Sent Mail, Drafts and the Outbox name
   whom the letters are to, as B-075 has it.
2. *The mark* (`MessageThread.marksConversation(in:)`). Every row of
   more than one letter, in every folder, ends its top line with the
   mark Sent Mail's rows have had since B-075. The same symbol at the
   date's size, the same blue (`Theme.tintBlue`, D-010), in the same
   place: at the text's right edge, 5 points after the date, the date's
   label ending before it (`RowTopLine`). Its size moves with the type
   and not with the text size in Settings (D-007, B-071). The cell and
   its layout are B-075's, unchanged but for item 5; only which rows
   have the mark changed. A single letter has none. In Edit mode the mark stays after
   the date. The mark does nothing of its own when tapped: a tap on the
   row opens the conversation in the reading pane, as before.
3. *VoiceOver* says how many, as it did: "Carlo, Margaret, 3 messages",
   then the subject and the time, in every folder. The label already
   said it everywhere; it is now the only place the list gives the
   number.
4. *A long list of who wrote* is cut with "…" before the date, where it
   was always cut, but for item 5's few points. The mark is not text on
   the line, so no length of names can push it off. The count, being
   text, went with the names.
5. *A marked row's date is never cut* (`RowTopLine`). In Edit mode in
   three panes the room before the mark is 74.2 points, and "Wednesday"
   is 80. There the date's label starts sooner by the difference, 5.8,
   and the names end sooner by as much, as Mail cuts the names and never
   the date. The mark stays at the right edge. The cell gives the line
   each row's own date, as wide as UIKit measures it (`MessageCell`).
   Where the date fits, which is every other date the list writes and
   every row out of Edit, nothing moves. A row without the mark is as it
   was, whatever its date. This reaches Sent Mail, Drafts and the Outbox
   too, whose "Wednesday" was cut the same way since B-075.

**Where a count was written.** One place wrote "(n)" after a row's
names: `MessageThread.displayRow`, which draws every row of the list.
So the change covers every folder, Edit mode, the Outbox, and the rows
drawn again as previews come. A search's rows are one letter each, never
gathered into conversations, so they had no count and have no mark, in
any folder and either scope. With Organize by Thread off, no row has a
mark. Left as they are, being no conversation's count: the folder pane's
unread counts beside each folder's name, and the Outbox's "2 Unsent
Messages" under the list. Comments that described the count on the rows
were changed with it, in the list, the cell, `Theme` and Settings.

**What stays.** The row's layout to the point, the unread dot, the flag,
the paperclip, the preview, the highlight of the open letter, the fixed
type (B-071). A row without the mark is as it was. A plain row's date
keeps its 110 points; a marked row's date ends before the mark, inside
them, as in Sent Mail since B-075. A marked row's date is never cut: in
Edit mode in three panes, "Wednesday", 80 points at 15, takes 5.8 from
the names (item 5).

**Found after the first pass, 2026-10-07, and fixed.** In Edit mode in
three panes a marked row's "Wednesday" was cut to "Wednes…" before the
mark. The list there is 300 points wide on his iPad, in either
orientation. In Edit its text runs from 29 to 245 points, the date has
97.2 of them, and a marked row's date 74.2. UIKit, in the iOS 18.6
simulator, measures "Wednesday" at 80 points in the list's 15-point
font, "Yesterday" at 68, "Thursday" at 64, and a time or a dd/MM/yy
date at about 63 or 64. So "Wednesday" was the one date cut, and only in
Edit in three panes: out of Edit, and in two panes, a marked row's date
has 87. Before B-080 only Sent Mail, Drafts and the Outbox had marked
rows; B-080 brought the cut to every folder. Seen so in the simulator,
with the app's clock moved to a Friday: in Trash, in Edit, "Wednes…" on
each conversation and "Wednesday" whole on every single letter. Item 5
is the fix. The first pass ran on a Wednesday, when no row can read
"Wednesday", and the suite's line was laid out at widths and a mark
other than his iPad's.

**Not like Mail.**

- Mail's chevron opens the conversation's letters in the list. Here it
  is a mark only, as B-075 built it.
- The reading pane has no "N Messages" over the stack (B-074). With the
  count gone from the rows, he sees how many by the letters in the pane;
  VoiceOver says it on the row.

**Tests.** `ConversationRowLikeMailTests`, ten, all new. In the Inbox,
All Mail, Important, Starred, Spam, Trash and two folders of his own, a
conversation names who wrote with no count and is marked; in Sent Mail,
Drafts and the Outbox, the same with the To named. The names are
`participants` joined, as before, his own letters there naming him, and
the row is the one `displayRow()` always drew. A single letter has no
mark and no count in every folder. A long list of who wrote ends with
its last name, not a count, and the line's geometry with a mark keeps
the names' width, the names ending before the date and the date before
the mark at the right edge. That is laid out at his iPad's widths, three
panes and two, in Edit and out, with the 18-point mark and "Yesterday",
68 points, the widest date that fits. A marked row's date of 80 points,
"Wednesday", is never cut: at each of those widths its label is at
least 80 wide, ends 5 before the mark, and starts 8 after the names; in
Edit in three panes it is 80, the names 105, 5.8 less than before; at
the others nothing moves. A row without the mark is the same for any
date, and the names never have less than nothing. The row is the
newest letter in every field but the names, with the conversation's
unread, flag and paperclip. VoiceOver says "3 messages" in every folder, unread and read, and
nothing of a count for a single letter. A search's rows and Organize by
Thread off: no mark, each named by its own sender. Read from the
source: the list gathers a folder's letters and never a search's; the
cell shows or hides the mark by the row alone, with nothing of the
folder or of Edit mode in it, and the names' label is one line cut at
its end; nothing in the list, the cell, `RowNames`, the Outbox or
`ListEdit` writes a count in brackets, and `MessageThread` writes none.
Changed, each with B-080's reason in its comment:
`MessageThreadTests.testTheCountRidesOnTheSenderLine`, now

`SentRowLikeMailTests.testEveryOtherListKeepsItsCountAndHasNoMark`,

the cell giving the line its date's own width
(`SentRowLikeMailTests.testTheListMarksItsRowsAndTheCellDrawsTheMark`),
