## B-081 — FIXED 2026-10-07, seen in the iPadOS 18 simulator and on the iPad. A letter whose To ended in ";" was refused

**Found** on 2026-10-06, in the simulator, during B-075's check, and noted
in its entry: a letter To an address with ";" typed after it was refused
at Send, "Message was not sent.", and stayed in the composer.

**What he saw.** Seen again on 2026-10-07, in a simulated iPad (7th
generation) on iPadOS 18.6, built from master 596f956. In To, the test
address with a tag, then ";". Leaving the field made one bubble, with the
address on it and no ";". Subject "B-081 before", Send: "Message was not
sent.", and the letter stayed in the sheet. A ";" typed after the bubble,
with a space either side, made a bubble of its own, ";".

**What it was.** The ";" was in the bubble, out of sight, and Send sent to
it.

- *The field* split what he typed at commas alone
  (`RecipientBubbles.ended`, `MailFormat.addresses(in:)`). A ";" ended
  nothing, and leaving the field made one entry of "address;". The
  bubble named the address, because `MailFormat.recipient(in:)` reads an
  entry without a ";" at its end, but the entry kept it.
- *The envelope* (`SMTPClient.envelopeAddress`) takes what is inside
  `<…>`, or the whole entry, and drops only spaces and control
  characters. So `RCPT TO:<address;>`. Gmail answered, the connection log
  of the send has it: "553-5.1.3 The recipient address <…;> is not a
  valid RFC 5321 address." With every recipient refused, the send failed
  (`SMTPClientError.rejected`), and he was told "Message was not sent."
  (`MailError.notSent`). The letter stays in the sheet when the server
  refuses it (B-052).
- *The header* (`RFC5322Builder`) took each entry as it was, and would
  have carried "To: address;", a ";" that ends a group with no group
  begun.

Every shape of it went the same way. "a@example.com; b@example.com" was one
bubble naming both and one `RCPT TO:<a@example.com;b@example.com>`. A ";"
alone was a bubble ";", Send live, and `RCPT TO:<;>`. Beside an address
that went, an entry with a ";" was refused alone: the letter went to the
others, and the app's book of addresses learned "jane@example.com;", to
offer it again in the list and in the share sheet, which reads the same
book.

How a ";" gets into To:

- *Typed or pasted.* The iPad's on-screen keyboard has ";" on its .?123
  side; a hardware keyboard and a paste have it too. This is the case
  found.
- *A draft, or a letter in the Outbox,* kept with one by a build before
  this one. Opened, it is a bubble with the ";" in it; in the Outbox it is
  sent as kept.
- *A `mailto:` link* written with ";" between its addresses,
  `mailto:a@example.com;b@example.com`: one entry, as the link is split
  at commas alone (`MailtoLink`).
- *A pick* from the book, once the book had learned such an address.
- *A letter's header.* A ";" at the end of an entry, in Gmail's copy of
  a draft among them, was already dropped as the header was read
  (`recipient(in:)`). The bubble never showed one either, which is why
  the draft in B-075's check seemed to come back from Drafts without it.
  A ";" between two people, `Jane <jane@example.com>; Sam <sam@example.com>`,
  as some clients write a header, was one entry: Reply All named Sam
  alone, with Jane in his name, and could not leave his own address out
  of such an entry.

**What Mail does.** Mail takes a ";" between addresses as it takes a ",":
it separates them, and one at the end, alone or beside a "," is nothing.
That is the rule this was built to. Mail itself was not tried.

**Changed.**

1. *The field* (`RecipientBubbles.ended`, `MailFormat.addresses(in:)`). A
   ";" ends a recipient as a "," does. Typed, it makes a bubble of what is
   before it at once, as a comma does since B-076. A ";" alone, " ; ", ",;"
   or ";;" make nothing, and the ";" goes from the line. Inside quotes,
   `<…>` or a comment it is part of the name or the address, as a comma
   is: `"Example; Jane" <jane@example.com>` is one bubble. A quote never
   closed splits what he typed at every ";" as at every comma. A field
   opened from a draft, a letter in the Outbox or a link splits each
   entry the same way, a bubble for each address, and so does a pick.
   An empty group, `undisclosed-recipients:;`, as a draft written in
   another client can have it, stays one entry, its ";" with it, as
   before: opened, its bubble reads the group whole, and typed, its ";"
   makes that bubble. A ";" after a colon with nothing but spaces or a
   comment between is the end of an empty group. A first build of this
   fix split it there: the bubble read "undisclosed-recipients:", and the
   header went out "To: undisclosed-recipients:", a group begun and never
   ended.
2. *The send* (`Submission.recipients`). Each entry is split the same way
   before the envelope is made. The bubbles are split already; this is
   for a letter kept by an earlier build, in Drafts or in the Outbox. No
   RCPT TO carries a separating ";", and none is empty. A ";" alone is
   nobody: Send stays grey, and such a letter is refused before the server
   is reached, as a letter to nobody always was.
3. *The header* (`RFC5322Builder`). To, Cc and a draft's Bcc are split the
   same way and joined by commas, so the header names exactly whom the
   envelope goes to.
4. *A header read back* (`MailFormat.addressList`). A ";" between
   addresses separates them as a comma does. A ";" that ends a group, after
   a colon with no "@" or "<" before it, stays with the group's last
   entry, as before, so the empty `undisclosed-recipients:;` still names
   nobody (B-075). Reply All on `Jane <jane@example.com>; owner@example.com;
   Sam <sam@example.com>` puts Jane and Sam in Cc and leaves him out.
5. *An address in brackets with a ";" in it* (`MailFormat.recipientEntry`,
   `RFC5322Builder`). A letter's malformed `<a;b@example.com>` is one
   address. Split, it was "a" and "b@example.com", someone the letter
   never named. A reply now keeps it in its brackets when splitting it
   would leave a piece that is not an address, and the header keeps any
   address alone that came in brackets and would read as more than one.
   So the field does not split it, nobody is added, and it goes as the
   one address it is, for Gmail to refuse as it would have. An address
   that splits into addresses alone, "a@example.com; b@example.com" as an
   earlier build's book can hold it, stays bare, and a pick of it makes a
   bubble of each.
6. *The book* (`IMAPMailRepository.send`, `RecipientBook`). It learns
   each address as it went, split, never with a ";" after it. The share
   sheet already told the app's book the addresses
   `Submission.recipients` gives. A book kept by an earlier build is
   filed again as it loads, each address under itself, and written out
   so: "jane@example.com;" is Jane's, her uses added to hers, and
   "a@example.com; b@example.com" is each of them. A malformed one,
   "a;b@example.com", is left whole: split, it would be filed under
   b@example.com, whom nobody wrote to. What the book learns is filed the
   same way, so an address a share sent by an earlier build noted with a
   ";" is filed under the address when the app takes it. The share
   sheet's copy of the book is filed as the sheet reads it, for the time
   before the app makes it again. So Jane is offered once, and not again
   once she is a bubble. A first build of this fix still offered
   "jane@example.com;" from such a book, with its ";", once Jane was a
   bubble, and its pick made a second bubble for her: the letter named
   her twice, in its header and in its envelope.

**Not changed.** An entry that is not an address, "jan", is kept as he
typed it, without the ";" after it, a bubble he can see and take off,
and Send treats it as before, with the same words.

**The empty group, changed after the review.** An empty group in To,
`undisclosed-recipients:;`, stays in the field and the header, and is
no longer offered to the server: it names nobody. Offered, it went
`RCPT TO:<undisclosed-recipients:;>` and Gmail refused it, 553 5.1.3,
while the letter went to the others. Alone in a letter it now leaves
nobody, and Send refuses the letter before the server is reached, with
the words a letter to nobody always had. `MailFormat.isEmptyGroup`
picks it out: the one entry the field's split leaves ending in ";",
with a colon, and no address. Two tests are new
(`testALetterToAnEmptyGroupAloneIsALetterToNobody`,
`testOnlyAnEmptyGroupIsLeftOutOfTheEnvelope`) and two changed to the new
rule. The filter undone in a scratch copy, the whole suite run serially:
4 failures in 4 tests, nothing else failing. The full suite, serially:
1,613 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. `MailtoLink` still splits at commas; the
field it opens splits the rest. The text helpers that split at commas alone,
`currentRecipientToken` and `replacingRecipientToken`, are no longer used
by either composer (B-076), and are as they were.

**What he sees.** A ";" after an address makes a bubble at once, as a
comma does. A ";" with nothing before it goes, and makes nothing. A letter
To such an address goes. An address the book learned with a ";" is
offered once, without it, and not again once it is a bubble. No new
words.

**Tests.** Thirty, all new: `SemicolonLikeMailTests`, sixteen,
`SemicolonSendTests`, five, and `SemicolonBookTests`, five, in one file;
two more in `ShareMirrorTests`, one in `OutboxTests` and one in
`ShareSheetTests`. `ScriptedSubmission` now answers a RCPT TO
with a ";" or a "," in its address as Gmail answered on 2026-10-07, 553
5.1.3 in its four lines, so a test that sends one sees the refusal he
saw.

- *The field:* every shape above split, "jane@example.com;", a name and
  its address with ";", two with ";" between, with and without a space,
  ";;", ",;", ";" first, ";" alone, " ; ", "; ,;; ,"; a ";" kept inside a
  quoted name, `<…>` and a comment; a quote never closed split at a ";" as
  at a comma; "jan;" kept as "jan", Send live for it.
- *The bubbles:* a ";" typed making a bubble, all at once and a letter at
  a time; nothing for a ";" alone; Return with a ";" inside quotes; a
  field opened with ";"s, a bubble each; a pick with a ";"; Send grey for
  ";" alone and live for an address with one.
- *The letter:* the send's recipients, the header's To, Cc and a draft's
  Bcc, and no To for ";" alone.
- *Headers read back:* the cases above, groups and the empty group
  included; Reply All knowing each person and leaving him out; a
  bracketed `<a;b@example.com>` kept one through Reply All, the bubbles,
  the send and the header.
- *Over the scripted servers:* a letter To each shape, sent once, its
  RCPT TOs exactly its addresses, its To and Cc as written, no Bcc
  header, and the book learning the addresses alone; a ";" alone refused
  with no connection made; a draft kept with ";"s saved to Drafts, read
  back a bubble each and sent to the same five addresses; the letter sent
  read back from its header and answered by Reply and Reply All to the
  same people; a letter in the Outbox kept with a ";", there after a
  relaunch, sent by a later pass to its three addresses and gone from the
  Outbox; a share To "Carlo <…>;" and ";" sent to its two addresses.
- *The empty group:* `undisclosed-recipients:;` one entry in the field,
  with spaces, a comment, and beside an address; typed a letter at a
  time, one bubble; a group with people in it still split at its ";"; a
  draft To it with a Bcc, reopened, one bubble, the send's recipients the
  group and the Bcc, the header's To the group ended; over the scripted
  servers, saved to Drafts, read back, sent, its RCPT TOs the group and
  the Bcc, its To the group, no Bcc header.
- *The book:* a book as an earlier build kept it, filed again as it
  loads, Jane once with her name and her uses added, two in one each with
  their uses, "a;b@example.com" whole, written out so and read the same by
  a later book; a clean book loaded as it was and not written out again;
  the clean entry's name kept over a merged one's; "ja" offering Jane once
  and nothing once she is a bubble; what it learns filed the same way,
  each address once; the share sheet's copy kept by an earlier build read
  filed, Jane offered once and not again once a bubble; an earlier share's
  "jane@example.com;" filed under the address when the app takes it.

The first twenty run against master's code, before the fix: nineteen
failed, 84 failures in all, the letter To "jane@example.com;" refused with
`notSent`. The one that passed holds what was right already: a ";"
inside a quoted name, kept at Return.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. The field split at
commas alone, as before: 45 in 13. A header read back split at commas
alone, as before: 8 in 2. A group's ";" not kept with it: 4 in 1. A ";"
typed ending nothing: 16 in 1. A pick not split: 3 in 2. The send's
recipients not split, as before: 9 in 6. The header's To and Cc not
split, as before: 15 in 4. The book learning each entry as kept, as
before: 1 in 1. A quote never closed split at commas alone: 2 in 2. A
reply's malformed address in brackets left bare: 7 in 1. The header's
left bare: 2 in 1. Eleven in all. Every failure in every run was in the
twenty new tests; B-061's and B-076's addressing tests, the replies made
up from 6,000 awkward letters among them, passed in each. In an earlier
pass, before the rule for a malformed address in brackets, the run for
the book also failed `LargeLetterTests.
testPicturesStillComingWhenHeMovesOnAreCalledOff`, which fails now and
then on this host. Those eleven were counted with the first twenty tests,
before the ten for the book and the empty group.

The book and the empty group, undone the same way, with all thirty, each
counted as failures in tests. An empty group's ";" split in the field:
14 in 3. A comment counted as something in the group: 1 in 1. A typed
empty group's ";" left off its bubble: 4 in 1. The book not filed as it
loads: 8 in 2. What it learns not filed: 3 in 2. The share sheet's copy
not filed: 4 in 1. A malformed key split too: 6 in 3. A key's addresses

The field, the typing, the book and the share sheet's copy all undone at

other two hold the filing itself, which was left in place, and a book
with nothing to file. The full suite, serially, with nothing undone:

   The connection log: one RCPT TO, the address alone, and Gmail's 250.
   Over IMAP it arrived once, its To the address alone, with no ";".
2. *Two.* `+jane`, ";", `+sam`, ";": two bubbles. Sent: two RCPT TOs, each
   250, and it arrived once, To the two joined by a comma.
3. *A ";" alone* in To: nothing, and Send stayed grey. Cancel closed it
   with nothing asked.
4. *A draft.* `+jane` and ";", Cancel, Save Draft. Gmail's copy in Drafts:
   To the address alone. Its row in Drafts named the address; opened, one
   bubble. Send: one RCPT TO, it arrived once, and Drafts was empty, in
   the app and on the server.
5. *Reply All* on "R3 B-081 two": To `+jane` and `+sam`, a bubble each,
   nothing in Cc or Bcc. Cancel closed it without a word.
6. *The share sheet,* from Safari on example.com: `+sam` and ";", one
   bubble. Send: it arrived once, To `+sam` alone. The share sheet sends
   from a process of its own, so this send is not in the app's log.
7. *The book.* `+ja` in a new letter's To: one row, "Jane Example" and her
   address, no ";". Picked, a bubble; `+ja` again, no rows. The same in
   the share sheet. Each closed with Delete Draft.
8. *The empty group.* "undisclosed-recipients:" then ";": one bubble,
   "undisclosed-recipients:;", whole, and Send grey; a "," after it added
   nothing. Bcc `+sam`, Cancel, Save Draft. Gmail's copy: To
   "undisclosed-recipients:;" and the Bcc; its row "No Recipients".
   Opened: the group's bubble whole and the Bcc's. Send: it arrived once,
   at `+sam`, its To "undisclosed-recipients:;". The connection log: one
   RCPT TO, `+sam`'s, 250, and none for the group. The simulator saw 8
   only before the group was left out of the envelope; this is the first
   sight of it left out.

Each of the five letters arrived once, in the Inbox, Sent Mail and All
Mail, and none in Spam. They were moved to Trash in the app.

**Not covered.**

- Step 0 of the TODO check was not run on the iPad, this build being on it

## B-082 — FIXED 2026-10-07, seen in the iPadOS 18 simulator and on the iPad. A name changed in Settings went on his letters only after the app was quit and opened again

**What he saw.** Seen on 2026-10-07, in a simulated iPad on iPadOS 18.6,
during B-080's check, and noted in its TODO item. The account's name was
changed in Settings, "Carlo" to "Carlo Wolfeschlegelsteinhausen Example",
and saved. The next reply still went out From "Carlo". Only after the app
was quit and opened again did letters go out under the new name. Mail
uses a changed name at once.

**What it was.** The repository kept the account it was made with, at
launch (`IMAPMailRepository.account`, a `let`). Every letter it made took
the name, the signature and its formatted twin from that copy:
`send`, for a new letter, Reply, Reply All, Forward, a letter sent from
Drafts and one going from the Outbox, and `append`, for a draft going up
to Drafts. Settings saved the account through `CredentialStore` and told
the list (`onSaved`), and the list took his addresses and asked for the
counts. Nothing handed the repository the account saved, and the screens
are not built again for a name. A repository is made at launch, and when
a new password is saved (`PasswordChange`); never for a name.

The same copy kept three more things from Settings waiting for a launch:

- *"Send my signature as plain text instead"*, saved: letters still went
  with the formatted signature.
- *"Restore Original Signature"*, saved: letters went without the
  formatted signature restored.
- *A changed signature:* the composer signs a new letter with the
  signature saved, read as it opens, but the repository looked for the
  old text at the letter's foot to find where the formatted twin goes
  (`AppleMailHTML.layout`). Not found, the twin was left off until a
  launch.

And the book of addresses offered his own address under the old name. The
repository noted the account's name for it once, at launch, and every page
of his own old letters, From the name he had then, named it again.

Already at once, and not changed: the signature in a new letter, Reply and
Forward, read by the composer as it opens; his addresses (B-076), read by
Reply All as it opens and handed to the list by `onSaved`; Organize by
Thread, which acts as it moves; the signature's pictures, read at each
letter; and the share sheet, which reads its copy of the account at each
share and is handed the account saved at Save (`ShareMirror`,
`CredentialStore.saveAccountOnly`).

**Changed.**

1. *The repository reads the account as each letter is made*
   (`IMAPMailRepository.sender`). It is the account it signed in as, with
   the name, the signature and its formatted twin, and his other addresses
   as Settings last saved them (`MailAccount.withSettings`). Where it
   connects, and as whom it signs in, stay its own. A saved account of
   another address, or none, changes nothing. The app's repository reads
   the account `CredentialStore` keeps, in `UserDefaults`; nothing is
   rebuilt for it, so the connection, the list, a search, his place, an
   open letter and one being written stay as they are. The password path
   is as it was.
2. *The book* (`RecipientBook.noteOwn`). His own address is offered under
   the name his account gives him, replacing any name the book had for it,
   and with no name when the account has none. Noted at launch, as before,
   and now at each Save too (`CredentialStore.saveAccountOnly`). A page of
   letters no longer names his own address
   (`IMAPMailRepository.rows`), so an old letter of his does not put the
   old name back. The share sheet's copy of the book is made again as the
   app leaves for Safari, as before.

**A letter waiting in the Outbox** when the name is changed went, from
B-082 until B-083, with the name saved when it went. B-083 made it go as
Mail's does, with the name, the Date and the signature of his Send; what
follows is how it was until then. The Outbox keeps what he wrote, not a
made letter: the letter is made at each attempt, its From from the
account. So such a letter already went under the new name after a launch;
now it does without one, and the name it goes with no longer depends on
whether the app was opened again in between. What he wrote, the
signature's words among them, goes as written; the formatted twin goes
only where those words are the signature saved, so a letter never carries
a formatted signature that is not the one its words show. Nothing new is
kept with a letter on the iPad for it. A draft in Gmail's Drafts keeps the
From it went up with until it is sent: sent, it goes under the name saved,
as a reopened draft always has.

**What he sees.** After Save, the next letter goes under the name saved,
a reply, a forward, a draft and a share alike, with no quit. His own
address is offered under the name saved. No new words.

**Tests.** Fifteen, all new, in `NameAtOnceTests.swift`:
`NameAtOnceTests`, three, `NameAtOnceSendTests`, nine, and
`NameAtOnceWiringTests`, three.

- *The account taken:* the name, the signature, its twin and his other
  addresses from the account saved, the address, the host and the login
  kept; another address's account, or none, changes nothing.
- *The book:* his own address under the name saved, in place of the one
  before, in any letter case; bare when the name is taken off; two
  addresses in one are not his; others' names learned as before.
- *Over the scripted servers,* the repository made at launch with "Carlo",
  the account then saved as a test hands it in: a new letter From "Carlo",
  then From the new name, then "Carlo" again once put back; Reply, Reply
  All and Forward From the new name; a draft saved to Drafts by the
  repository and by the pass for a letter kept on the iPad, From the new
  name, and one saved before the change, reopened and sent, From the new
  name; a letter left in the Outbox with the line down, the name then
  changed, sent by the pass once the line is back, From the new name (From
  the name it was sent with since B-083); the formatted signature gone
  from the next letter once "plain text" is saved and back once restored;
  a changed signature found at the next letter's foot, with its twin; his
  own address offered under the new name, after a page of his old letters
  From "Carlo" and after a relaunch over a book that had learned "Carlo";
  the name taken off, his address bare, the next letter From the bare
  address, past a page and a relaunch.
- *The share sheet:* its copy of the account handed the one saved, the
  next share From the new name.
- *The wiring,* read from the source: the app's repository reads
  `CredentialStore.loadAccount()`; `saveAccountOnly` notes his name in the
  book and hands the share sheet the account, and writes no password;
  Settings' `onSaved` builds nothing again, and a new password still signs
  in afresh once the sheet has gone.

The first fourteen run against the repository as it was, given only the
new parameter it did not yet read: nine failed, 13 failures, the reply
From "Carlo". The five that passed hold what was right already or helpers
written with them: the account taken and the book's rule, the share
sheet, and Save rebuilding nothing.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. The repository's
letters made from the account it launched with, as before: 11 in 7. Send
alone so: 9 in 7. A draft going up alone so: 2 in 1. A page naming his
own address from the letter, as before: 2 in 2. The launch noting his
name as before: 1 in 1. The book keeping the old name when it is taken
off: 5 in 2. The formatted twin not taken from the account saved: 2 in 2.
An account of another address taken: 1 in 1. The app's repository given
nothing to read: 1 in 1. Save not noting his name in the book: 1 in 1.
Ten in all, and every failure in each run was in the fifteen new tests.

The full suite, serially, with nothing undone: 1,669 tests, 5 skipped,
none failing. The release build for the iPad links.

## B-083 — CHANGED 2026-10-09, seen in the iPadOS 18 simulator and on the iPad. A letter waiting in the Outbox went under the name saved when it went, and was dated then; Mail's goes as it was when Send was tapped

**Asked** on 2026-10-08. B-082 made a name changed in Settings go on the
next letter at once, and said under "Not covered" that Mail's own Outbox
had not been looked at. It was then, and the owner ruled: "make the
Outbox work like Mail's — store the name and the time with the letter
when it enters the Outbox, and when an opened Outbox letter gets re-sent
it should keep the stored name and take a new Date."

**What Mail does.** Read from iOS 18.6's code, in the iPadOS 18.6
simulator's runtime, on 2026-10-08. Nothing of it was run.

- *Send makes the letter, whole, on the iPad.* MessageUI's
  `+[MFComposeTypeFactory headersFromDelegate:originatingBundleID:sourceAccountManagement:]`
  takes the sending address, gives it the account's name
  (`fullUserName`) when it has none, writes From, and sets Date to the
  moment (`[NSDate date]`). Both of the composer's ways of sending go
  through it. The signature goes into the body before it
  (`-[MFMailComposeController finalizeSignature:]`).
- *The Outbox keeps that letter.* The app hands the mail daemon the
  finished letter and nothing more: Email.framework's
  `EMOutgoingMessage` carries its bytes, with no account and no name. The
  daemon files it in the Outbox (`MFDeliveryQueue`) before it tries it,
  and a try that fails leaves it there.
- *Every try sends what was kept.* A retry reads the letter back from the
  Outbox, and `-[MFMailDelivery headersForDelivery]` sends its headers as
  they are: it takes off Apple's internal ones and adds X-Mailer if there
  is none. Nothing on that path reads the account's name or touches
  Date. A name changed in Settings changes nothing in a letter already
  waiting.
- *Opened from the Outbox and sent again.* The letter opens in the
  composer (`-[_MFMailCompositionContext initOutboxRestoreOfMessage:legacyMessage:]`);
  its copy goes to Trash, and Cancel offers "Leave in Outbox". The
  composer takes the letter's own From, name and all
  (`_setupForExistingNewMessage:content:`, `firstSenderAddress`), and
  Send keeps an address that has a name. So it goes under the name it
  was first sent with, unless the address is picked again in the From
  menu, which hands the composer a bare address and so brings the name
  saved now. Date is set again, at this Send. The signature is not
  brought up to date (`updateSignature` runs there for another kind of
  letter only).
- *Send Later* is the one letter Mail dates again, on purpose
  (`-[OutgoingMessageRepository_iOS outgoingMessageFromPersistedMessage:]`),
  and it keeps its From.
- *A draft* reopens through the same `_setupForExistingNewMessage:content:`,
  so Mail probably keeps the From a draft was saved with too. That was
  not traced to the end.

**What it was.** A letter in the Outbox is kept as what he wrote
(`LocalDrafts`, `letter.json`, B-052), to go under one Message-ID at
every attempt (B-070). It was made at each attempt
(`IMAPMailRepository.send`) from the account as Settings had it then
(B-082's `sender`), and dated then (`Submission.send`'s own Date). Sent
with no connection as "Carlo", renamed in Settings, and gone at the next
Refresh, it went From the new name, dated at the Refresh. Two attempts
at one letter, the first cut off after its DATA, went under one
Message-ID and two Dates. The formatted signature was chosen at each
attempt from the signature saved then: "Send my signature as plain text
instead", saved while a letter waited, took the formatting off it.

**Changed.**

1. *Kept at Send* (`LocalDrafts.send`, `AtSend`). As the letter enters the
   Outbox at his Send, what it is made with is written with it, in the
   same write as its Message-ID: the name in use, which is the account's
   as Settings saved it (B-082's `sender`, read as
   `MailRepository.sendingAs`), the time, and the signature with its
   formatted twin. This is so whether the letter then goes at once, waits,
   or waits after a first attempt has failed. In `letter.json` they are
   `sentName`, `sentAt`, `sentSignature` and `sentSignatureHTML`, beside
   `outbox`.
2. *Every attempt is made with them* (`OutgoingLetter.atSend`,
   `IMAPMailRepository.send`). From is the kept name at the account's
   own address, Date the kept time, and the formatted twin is laid out
   from the kept signature. Every pass: a page, the watch, coming back,
   his Refresh, leaving the app, the next launch. With the Message-ID,
   an attempt is the same letter as the one before it.
3. *Opened from the Outbox and sent again* (`LocalDrafts.opened`,
   `LocalDrafts.atSend`). The composer's first keep takes the letter out
   of the Outbox, as before, and what it went in with is held while the
   composer has it open. His Send keeps the name and the signature, and
   takes the time of this Send. Its Message-ID is made as before: a new
   one, unless an attempt whose DATA went may have reached Gmail; then it
   keeps that attempt's, and Sent Mail is asked first (B-052, B-070).
   Blackmail sends from one address, so there is no address to pick again.
   Closed as it opened, the letter goes back with all of it, its time too:
   he has not sent it again. Kept as a draft, by Save Draft or by a change
   and a swipe, it is a draft, and keeps nothing of its Send.
4. *A letter B-057 holds* goes only when he opens it and taps Send: the
   way above. Brought back from where a safe start set it aside, it comes
   back with what it went in with.
5. *A letter written in another account*, opened from the Outbox and
   sent, goes from this account's address, and so under this account's
   name and with its signature.

The signature is kept as the name is, because it is small and safe: two
strings, of a few kilobytes at most, and the twin is laid out by the
code that laid it out before, from the signature the letter's words were
signed with. The signature's pictures are still read at each attempt;
only Restore Original Signature changes them, back to the pictures the
original's markup names.

**Not changed.** A new letter, Reply, Reply All and Forward written after
a rename go under the new name at once (B-082). A draft goes under the
name saved when it is sent, as B-082 left it; Mail probably keeps a
draft's own From, not traced to the end, and only the Outbox was asked
about. The share sheet has no Outbox: its letter is made at its Send,
From the account it was handed, and dated then, and a Send that cannot
reach the server keeps the sheet. The Outbox's count, its rows and its
words; the three tries before the pass gives a letter up (B-057); the
Message-ID and the look in Sent Mail (B-052, B-070).

**A letter kept by an older build**, with none of the four, goes as
before: under the name saved when it goes, dated then. Each of the four is
read on its own, and one that cannot be read is taken as not there: a
letter is never passed over or held for one. The signature is taken only
with its twin. A kept name that is empty goes as the address alone. A kept
name with a line break in it cannot start a header: the builder makes it
one line (`RFC5322Builder.headerSafe`), as it does a name saved.

**What he sees.** A letter he sent while the iPad had no connection
arrives with the name and the time of his Send, whatever was saved in
Settings before it went. No new words.

**Tests.** Sixteen, all new, in `OutboxAsSentTests.swift`, and one of
B-082's changed.

- *Queued, renamed, gone:* sent with the line down as "Carlo", the name
  then changed, sent by the pass: From "Carlo", Date the time of his
  Send, the Message-ID it went in with; a letter written after, From the
  new name and dated as it goes.
- *A second attempt:* the first cut off after its DATA, the name then
  changed, Sent Mail asked: the second has the From, the Date and the
  Message-ID of the first.
- *Every pass:* his Refresh, leaving the app, a page or the watch, and
  the next launch with the repository made with the new name: each
  letter From its own name at Send, dated then.
- *An older build's letter,* the four taken out of its `letter.json`:
  the name saved when it goes, dated then, its Message-ID as given.
- *A field that cannot be read:* a Date of the wrong type leaves the
  name, a name and a twin of the wrong type leave the Date; both listed,
  neither held, each sent once.
- *On the iPad:* the four written with the Message-ID, read back the same
  by the next launch, kept through the writes of an attempt, gone when
  the letter is taken back or kept by the composer; an empty name stays
  empty.
- *Opened and sent again:* the kept name, the Date of the new Send, a
  new Message-ID; after a cut, the cut's Message-ID, Sent Mail asked
  first. *Put back:* all of it as it went in, the time too. *Kept as a
  draft:* From the name saved when it is sent.
- *Brought back held (B-057):* with what it went in with; his Send keeps
  the name and takes a new Date. *Another account's letter:* this
  account's name.
- *No name at Send:* the address alone, though a name is saved after.
  *A kept name with a line break:* one From line, no Bcc header, nobody
  added to the envelope.
- *The signature:* the formatted twin of its Send, after "plain text"
  and new words were saved; the next letter plain.
- *The share sheet:* no Outbox; a Send that cannot connect keeps the
  sheet, and the next Send makes the letter then.

B-082's `testALetterInTheOutboxGoesUnderTheNameSavedWhenItGoes` is now
`testALetterInTheOutboxGoesUnderTheNameItWasSentWith`: From "Carlo", the
name it was sent with, and the next letter From the new name.

With nothing kept at Send and nothing read at an attempt, as before, the
new fields left in so the tests build: 13 of the 17 failed, 17 failures.
The four that passed hold what was right already: the store's file, a
draft, another account's letter, and the share sheet.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. Every attempt made as
it goes, what was kept unread: 25 in 12. The kept name alone unread: 14
in 11. The kept time alone unread: 10 in 6. The kept signature alone
unread: 1 in 1. The pass not handing on what was kept: 25 in 12. Nothing
kept at Send: 16 in 12. The repository not saying its name and signature,
so the protocol's empty default: 20 in 12. A Send from the Outbox keeping
the first Date: 3 in 3. A Send from the Outbox taking the name saved now:
3 in 3. Put back with nothing: 3 in 1. A field that cannot be read
failing the whole letter: 1 in 1. A signature taken without its twin: 1
in 1. Another account's name kept: 1 in 1. Taken back with what it went
in with: 1 in 1. Fourteen in all, and every failure in each run was in
the B-083 tests and the one changed. The known flaky
`LargeLetterTests.testPicturesStillComingWhenHeMovesOnAreCalledOff` also
failed in the first run of the first of these; run again, that run gave
the count above and nothing else.

The full suite, serially, with nothing undone: 1,685 tests, 5 skipped,
none failing. The release build for the iPad links.

## B-084 — FIXED 2026-10-19, found on the iPad, seen fixed in the iPadOS 18 simulator and on the iPad. After a Delete, a conversation's row in Trash named its oldest letter and its stack ran upside down; Mail's names the newest

**What he saw.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-19, in passing, during
B-080's check in the third round there, on the build of `ipad-fix2`. A
conversation of two: a letter sent at 9:45 and a reply at 9:47. Its Inbox
row was right: 9:47, the mark, the reply's subject with its "Re:", the
reply's first words. Edit, that row ticked, Delete. Trash: the row read
9:45, the mark, the subject without "Re:", the first letter's words. The
same after the app was quit and opened again. Opened, the header named
the 9:45 letter, and the stack had the 9:47 letter at the top and the
9:45 letter at the bottom. Older conversations in Trash were the same.
Mail's row names the newest letter, and its stack runs the oldest at the
top (B-074).

Over IMAP, the two were UIDs 251 (9:45) and 252 (9:47) in the Inbox, and
199 (9:45) and 198 (9:47) in Trash: the newest had the lower UID. Gmail
kept each letter's INTERNALDATE through the move.

**What it was.** Two things together.

- *The app's own batch.* Edit mode's Delete gathered the ticked rows'
  letters in the list's order, each conversation newest first
  (`ListBatch.letters`), and sent them one at a time, a UID MOVE each
  (`ListBatch.run`, B-062). Gmail gives each letter moved in the next UID
  in the folder it goes to. So the newest letter had the lowest UID in
  Trash. Move out of a folder in Edit mode did the same.
- *The order of a conversation.* The list is in UID order, newest first.
  `MessageThread.group` kept that order, and a conversation's newest was
  the first of it. So the row, the order of its names, the pane's header
  and the stack (`ConversationDocument.stack`, the order turned over) all
  came from the letter the folder took last. That is the newest only when
  the letters came into the folder in the order they were written. After
  the app's own Delete it was the oldest, every time. Letters put in a
  folder out of turn any other way do the same: moved by another mail
  program, a reply deleted before the letter it answers, a letter put
  back.

**Changed.**

1. *The batch goes the oldest first* (`ListBatch.letters`). The ticked
   rows' letters go in the list's order turned over: the bottom row
   first, each conversation's letters oldest first, each letter once. The
   folder they go to takes them in the order they came, so their new UIDs
   follow their times, and the rows keep their order there. Edit mode's
   Delete and Move both. Every row still leaves at the tap, and nothing
   he sees changes.
2. *A conversation goes in the order its letters came*
   (`MessageThread.byArrival`). Each row now carries when the server took
   its letter, its INTERNALDATE (`MessageSummary.arrived`), from the FETCH
   it is drawn with already (`IMAPMailRepository.rows`): nothing more is
   asked. A conversation's letters go by it, the newest first, and by UID
   where two came in the same second. The row, its names, the pane's
   header and the stack then stand for the newest, whatever order the
   letters are in the folder. Not by the letter's Date, which its
   sender's clock wrote: a letter dated wrong keeps the place its arrival
   gives it, as B-074 has it.
3. *The kept copy* (D-016, `MailShelf`). The time is kept with each row
   and read back, so a launch draws the same row before the folder is
   listed. A page kept by a build before has none: its rows read as not
   knowing it, and a conversation with such a row keeps the folder's
   order, as before. No new format. The same for a letter kept on the
   iPad, which has none.
4. *The row's id* (`MessageThread.id`). It was the newest letter's. It is
   now the letter the list has first in the conversation, the last the
   folder took. A page appended below can bring a letter that came later,
   a reply deleted before its letter, and the newest then changes; the
   letter listed first does not. So his place, his tick, the letter open
   and VoiceOver's row (B-079) find the row again as before. The two are
   the same letter but for a conversation put in its folder out of turn.

**Every way several letters go at once,** looked at:

- Edit mode's Delete and Move, in a folder and in a search's hits:
  changed, as above.
- Edit mode's Delete inside Trash erases each letter: the order changes
  nothing there, and they go in the same order as the rest.
- Edit mode's Mark moves nothing. Its writes go in the order Delete's
  do; nothing he sees changes.
- The reading pane's Delete and Move act on one letter, the one it shows,
  in a conversation too: nothing to order.
- The Outbox already sends its letters oldest first, in the order he sent
  them (`LocalDrafts.uploadWaiting`).
- The copies of a draft a save leaves in Drafts are erased, not moved to
  a folder he reads. A letter kept on the iPad goes from the iPad.

**Still as it was.** B-074: the stack runs the oldest at the top and the
newest open at the bottom, opens at the oldest letter he has not read,
and puts a letter that comes while it is open at the bottom. B-075 and
B-080: one mark after the date, no count, the names newest first, the To
in Sent Mail, Drafts and the Outbox. B-079: VoiceOver's row is found again
by its id and its letters, and reads the names, how many and the
subject of the newest. Their tests are unchanged and pass. A search's rows
are one letter each, as before. In Drafts a tap opens the newest; Gmail
takes a draft's INTERNALDATE as it is saved, so that is the one saved
last, as before.

**What he sees.** After a Delete, a conversation's row in Trash names its
newest letter, its time, its subject and its sender first, as in the
Inbox, and its stack runs the oldest at the top. The same for a
conversation whose letters came into a folder out of turn. No new words.

**Tests.** Eleven new and two changed: `ArrivalOrderTests.swift`, nine;
one in `MailShelfTests` and one in `ListBatchTests`.

- *The batch:* a conversation of three in the Inbox, ticked and deleted,
  goes the oldest first, one UID MOVE each, and reaches Trash in the
  order it came; its row there names the last reply by the folder's order
  alone, as a build without the times groups it, and with them; the stack
  runs the first letter to the last. The same for another conversation
  moved out in Edit mode.
- *By arrival:* Trash after the old Delete, the newest with the lower UID:
  the row's subject, time, preview, names and VoiceOver's words from the
  newest, the rows in their places, the stack the oldest first, where it
  opens, and what a tap marks read. Two letters in one second: the higher
  UID first, in either order listed; from two folders or two
  UIDVALIDITYs, the list's order.
- *A letter dated wrong* keeps its arrival's place: dated 2023 and taken
  last, the newest, at the bottom, open; dated 2037 and taken first, at
  the top.
- *Without the time:* no letter with one, or one without among them, the
  folder's order; one letter, and none.
- *The row's id* across a page that brings a letter that came later: the
  same rows by id, the newest the later letter, his place, his tick and
  VoiceOver's row found again.
- *A letter that comes while the stack is open* still goes in at the
  bottom.
- *The repository:* each row carries the INTERNALDATE the page's FETCH
  asked for, and its own Date. Trash with a conversation put there newest
  first: the row from the last to come, listed and from the kept copy
  after a launch.
- *The kept copy:* the time kept and read back; a page kept without it
  reads, its rows without it, and its conversation in the folder's order.

`testEveryRowGoesAtTheTapAndEachLetterIsMovedToTrashInTurn` takes its
letters as Edit mode does, and the four go the oldest first.
`testTickedRowsGoInListOrderWhateverOrderHeTickedThem` is now
`testTickedRowsGoInTheListsOrderTurnedOverWhateverOrderHeTickedThem`.

With both parts undone, the new field left in so the tests build: 9 of
the 13 failed, 58 failures. The four that passed hold what was right
already or helpers written with them: the tie broken by UID, a letter
dated wrong in a conversation that came in order, a conversation with no
times, and a letter that comes while the stack is open.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run

The tie broken by the list's order alone: 1 in 1. The letter's Date in

## B-085 — FIXED 2026-10-19, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. A Save in Settings with no connection was followed by "Can't connect to mail server."

**What he saw.** Seen on the iPad on 2026-10-19, during B-083's check,
with Airplane Mode on. Blackmail's Settings, the name changed, Save:
Settings closed and "Can't connect to mail server." came up. It came after
every Save made with no connection that day: the name, the name put back,
and "Send my signature as plain text instead". Each save had worked:
Settings opened again showed what was saved, and the next letters went
with it. Nothing he asked for needed the connection, and the alert reads
as if the save had failed.

**What it was.** Save hands the list the account saved (`onSaved`). The
list took his addresses and drew its rows again (B-076), then asked the
container for the folder counts (`onRefreshRequested`), as his Refresh
does. That sweep is a LIST and a STATUS per folder. With no connection it
failed, and a sweep asked for that way is not a quiet one (B-049), so it
put up the alert.

The sweep was there from the first version, when a new password was
saved this way too. Since B-056 a new password goes by `onPasswordSaved`,
which builds the screens again over a repository that signs in with it;
that fetches what it needs for itself. B-076 kept the sweep and put the
rows drawn again in front of it. What Save keeps now is the name, the
signature with its formatted twin and its pictures, and his other
addresses. None of it is on the server, and no count changes with it.
B-076 needed only the rows drawn again, which Save already does.

**Changed.** Save asks the server for nothing
(`MessageListViewController.showSettings`). The sweep is gone, not made
quiet: there was nothing for it to fetch. The rows are drawn again with
his addresses, as before. The rest of the save is as it was: the account
written, the share sheet and the book handed it, the pictures of a
restored signature saved. The list's `onRefreshRequested` is called in
one place now, his Refresh. Edit mode's Delete and Move still ask for
the counts by `requestSweep`, when one may have changed (B-062).

**Not changed.** His Refresh fetches the page and sweeps the counts, and
with no connection says "Can't connect to mail server." and "No
Connection", as before. The password path is not touched: a new password
is checked with Gmail before it is kept, and with no connection Settings
says "Could not reach Gmail. Your old password is still in place."

**Other places that speak of the connection when he did not ask.** Every
alert about the connection was looked at, with what sets it off. None
other is the same case, and none was changed.

- *Organize by Thread:* the rows drawn again, nothing fetched. *Bring
  Back Set-Aside Letters:* Drafts and the Outbox drawn from the iPad,
  nothing fetched. *Save Draft:* the letter kept on the iPad and Drafts
  drawn from it, no alert.
- *Coming back within fifteen minutes:* nothing fetched for the list. The
  connection is probed, the letters waiting go if they can, and the watch
  starts, all with nothing said.
- *Coming back after fifteen minutes or more* is a new sitting (B-003):
  the Inbox's newest page is fetched, as at launch, and with no connection
  one "Can't connect to mail server." comes up, as at launch and at each
  folder opened (B-053, seen on the iPad). The page is what he has come
  back to read, and the alert says it is not fresh. Not the same case.
- *The watch:* its checks, its sweeps and its fetches say nothing when
  they fail (B-049).
- *After a Delete, Move or Flag the server took,* from the reading pane
  or Edit mode: the counts are swept, and that sweep is his (B-049,
  B-062). It fails only if the line goes in the moment after a write that
  went.
- *A letter opened that the server says is another one now* (D-016): it
  comes off the list and the counts are swept (`onMessagesChanged`). He
  opened it, and the server had answered.
- *Delete Draft on a draft opened from Drafts:* Drafts is fetched again
  after it, and with no connection says so. He asked for something on the
  server, and the copy in Drafts did not go.
- *A letter opened, a date jump, Move's list of folders, Send:* each is
  something he asked for.

**What he sees.** With no connection, Save closes Settings and nothing
more is said. Refresh after it says "Can't connect to mail server." as
before. No new words.

**Tests.** Six, all new, in `QuietSaveTests.swift`.

- *Save:* what it runs in the list takes his addresses and draws the rows
  again, and asks for no sweep, no page and no pass. Drawing the rows
  again (`regroup()`) asks for none either, and the container, told of
  it, only hands the reading pane its new letters.
- *The counts:* the hook Save used, `onRefreshRequested`, is called in
  one place, his Refresh.
- *The other ways to the counts:* `requestSweep` is called in one place,
  Edit mode's Delete and Move, and `onMessagesChanged` in one, a letter
  opened that is another one now.
- *His Refresh:* its page is not quiet and puts up the alert when it
  fails; the counts it asks for are swept as his, and a sweep of his that
  fails puts up the alert.
- *A sweep asked for* with nothing said of quiet is not quiet.
- *The password path:* checked, saved, and the screens built again once
  the sheet has gone, not by `onSaved`, which Settings calls in one
  place, a save with no new password.

Five read the source: the controllers are UIKit and are not built on
the machine the suite runs on. The one on a sweep asked for runs the
sweeps.

Against the code as it was, with the sweep after Save: 2 of the 6
failed, 3 failures. The four that passed hold what was right already:
his Refresh, the other ways to the counts, a sweep asked for, and the
password path.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. The sweep after Save
put back: 3 in 2. A sweep after Save by the way Edit mode asks for one:
3 in 2. His Refresh's counts made quiet: 1 in 1. His Refresh's page made
quiet: 2 in 2. A failed sweep never saying so: 1 in 1. A sweep quiet
unless said otherwise: 2 in 2. A new password handed to `onSaved` as
well, before the screens are built again: 1 in 1. A sweep by Edit mode's
way at the end of `regroup()`, which Save runs: 3 in 3. A sweep by
`onMessagesChanged` at the start of the rows' rebuild, which `regroup()`
runs: 1 in 1. The container sweeping when told the rows were drawn
again: 2 in 2. Ten in all. Every failure was in the new tests but four,
one in `RefreshTapTests`, one in `NewMailTests` and two in
`ConversationOrderTests`, which hold the same code. The known flaky
`LargeLetterTests.testPicturesStillComingWhenHeMovesOnAreCalledOff` also
failed in the first run of the sweep quiet unless said otherwise; run
again, that run gave the count above and nothing else.

The full suite, serially, with nothing undone: 1,691 tests, 5 skipped,
none failing. The release build for the iPad links.

## B-086 — FIXED 2026-10-20, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. A folder tapped in the first seconds after launch lost its highlight to the Inbox

**What he saw.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20,
three panes. He opens Blackmail and, while the line under the list
still says "Checking for Mail...", taps Trash. Trash's letters come,
and Trash is highlighted. Then, as the folders' names come from the
server, the highlight goes back to the Inbox, beside Trash's letters,
and stays there until Refresh. It happened in each run where the tap
came before the server had answered for the folders: from half a
second to almost six seconds after the launch, as Gmail was quick or
slow. In two panes the folders are behind the list at launch, and no
tap came early enough.

**What it was.** At launch the app shows the folders kept on the iPad
and highlights the Inbox, then asks the server for the folders and,
once they come, highlighted the Inbox again, whatever was open. A
folder tapped in between was opened and highlighted, and that second
highlight took it back to the Inbox. Every redraw after kept it there.

**Changed.** When the folders come, the folder that is open is
highlighted: the Inbox, unless he has tapped another. The first frame's
Inbox, before anything can be tapped, is as it was. The other places
that highlight a folder already followed the folder that is open.

**Tests.** `PaneArrangementTests`, one new test, read from the source:
after the wait for the folders, the next line highlights the folder
that is open; the Inbox is named only once, before the wait. The old
line put back, the whole file run: 2 failures in that test, nothing
else failing. The full suite, serially: 1,729 tests, 5 skipped, none
failing. The release build for the iPad links.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-20**, three panes: Blackmail ended and
opened again, Trash tapped 0.4 s after the launch, the screen watched to
4 s, three times. Each time Trash stayed highlighted beside its letters
through the folders' coming, the line's "Updated Just Now" and the
counts. The build before, with the same tap, put the highlight back on
the Inbox each time.

## B-087 — FIXED 2026-10-20, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. Save Draft with no connection left the old copy's row in Drafts for some eight seconds

**What he saw.** Seen on the iPad on 2026-09-30, Drafts open in the
list, with no connection. A draft reopened from its row, changed, Cancel,
Save Draft: the sheet went, and the list kept the row of the copy in
Gmail, as it was before he changed it. Some eight seconds later the new
row, "On this iPad only", took its place. Nothing was lost: the letter
had been kept on the iPad before the sheet went. Mail's Drafts shows a
draft saved at once.

**What it was.** Save Draft keeps the letter on the iPad at the tap,
before the sheet goes, and the list is told (`ComposeActions.saveAndClose`).
But Drafts lists only the letters kept here that no composer has open,
and hides only the copies those stand for (`LocalDrafts.waiting`,
`replacedInDrafts`). The sheet had the letter open until it let go of
it, and it let go only once the save had been answered, so the list drew
nothing new at the keep. With no connection the save is answered when
the connect fails, some eight seconds on the iPad; then the sheet let
go, and the row came. A new letter had no row at all until then. With a
connection the wait was the second the save takes to land, and the copy
it became came in the old one's place, so it was hardly seen.

The sheet held the letter for one thing. No pass takes a letter open in
the composer to the server, and the save has to be the only one taking
it up, or the pass and the save would each take a version of it. Hiding
it from the list came with that.

**Changed.** As the sheet goes, Save Draft puts the letter away
(`DraftKeeping.putAway`): the sheet is done with it as far as Drafts
goes, and Drafts lists it at once, "On this iPad only", in place of the
copy it was reopened from, or at the top for a new letter. The hold on
the passes stays until the save has been answered (`LocalDrafts.saving`),
and that hold is all the sheet lets go of then. Listed, the letter can
be opened from its row while its save is still out; it is then the new
composer's, and the first sheet letting go leaves it open. Letting go
used to close it outright, which would have let a pass take it from
under the composer it was open in.

When the save lands, the letter leaves the iPad at once, as one nobody
has open does, and the list draws the copy it became in its place: one
row for the letter at every redraw. A letter open in the sheet that
landed used to stay on the iPad until the sheet let go, unlisted; listed
now, that would have been two rows for the moment between.

With a photo still on its way in, it is put away once the photos are
in, kept again with them first. The letter kept at the tap is not then
the one saved: opened or deleted from its row meanwhile, it would have
been kept again by the save over what he had done there.

Listed while its save is out, the letter can also be opened from its row
and that save land while the new composer has it, as it could already
while a pass took it up. The copy it became is then its row for as long
as that composer is open. But the letter still names the copy it was
first reopened from, and the list hid only that one. Changed and saved
again, its row came beside the copy that had landed: two rows for the
letter until that save landed, and with no connection until a pass. Sent
instead, that copy was still listed as the sheet closed, Send naming
only the copy it was reopened from, until the tidying after the send
removed it; tapped, it opened the letter just sent, to be sent a second
time. Now a letter kept here also stands in for the copy an upload of it
put up in this launch (`LocalDrafts.landed`, in `replacedInDrafts`),
which its next upload replaces, and so does one sent or deleted until
the tidying has removed it. Not under a password saved since that upload
set off (`landedUnder`): the copy's folder and UID may then be another
mailbox's draft, and it stays listed, as a copy the letter names by UID
alone does.

**Not changed.** What is sent, and when: the save's APPEND and the old
copy's removal after it. A save that fails leaves the letter on the
iPad, to go with the next pass. Send, Delete Draft, a sheet swiped away,
Cancel on a letter as it opened, and the Outbox are as they were, but
for the copy that landed, above: Drafts no longer lists it while the
letter is kept, in the Outbox too, nor once it is sent or deleted, until
it is tidied away.

**What he sees.** Save Draft with Drafts open: as the sheet slides away,
the letter's row is at the top of Drafts with "On this iPad only" on it,
and the old copy's row has gone. With no connection it stays so. With
one, about a second later the mark goes, and the row is Gmail's copy.
Opened again from its row at once and saved again, one row as that
sheet goes too; sent from there, none. No new words.

**Tests.** Eleven new: ten in `DraftRowAtOnceTests.swift` and one in
`ComposeActionsTests`, whose Save Draft test now has the putting away in
its order.

- *No connection:* a draft reopened from Drafts, Save Draft. As the
  sheet goes its row is in place of the copy's, and so after the save
  has failed, one row for the letter at every redraw. A new letter's row
  is there as its sheet goes.
- *A connection:* its row as the sheet goes and while the APPEND is
  held, and no pass takes it meanwhile. Once it lands, its copy in its
  place and the old copy gone, one row for the letter at every redraw,
  one APPEND, nothing left on the iPad.
- *Opened from its row while the save is out:* the save answered, the
  letter stays the new composer's, not listed and taken by no pass while
  it is open. Once that composer is done, listed again, and up once: one
  copy on the server.
- *The hold:* put away, listed, and no pass takes it, the pass as he
  leaves included, until the sheet lets go; then the next pass does.
- *The order:* kept and put away before `dismiss`. With a photo coming,
  not put away until it is in, then kept with it, put away and saved,
  the letter taken once.
- *Saved again from its row, its save landed there:* its row in place
  of the copy that landed as that sheet goes and while the second save
  is out, then the copy that save became; one row for the letter at
  every redraw, one copy on the server.
- *The same with no connection for the second save:* its row in place
  of that copy, and so once the save has failed, until a pass replaces
  it; one row at every redraw.
- *Sent from there:* no row for the letter as the sheet closes, the copy
  that landed included, though Send names only the copy it was reopened
  from; then that copy removed, and the letter sent once.
- *Sent from there with no connection:* it waits in the Outbox, the copy
  that landed still kept as its own and still in Drafts, and Drafts has
  no row for the letter as the sheet closes nor while it waits, though
  the letter in the Outbox names only the copy it was reopened from.
  With the line back, the pass sends it once and removes that copy, and
  nothing is left on the iPad.
- *Opened while a pass takes it up, then saved:* its row in place of the
  copy the pass put up as the sheet goes, then its own copy; one row at
  every redraw.
- *A password saved since:* a copy that landed before it, and one whose
  upload went before it and landed after it, stand in for the letter no
  more, and are listed.

The tests draw Drafts as the list draws it from what `LocalDrafts`
posts, `MessageListViewController.keptChanged`'s two steps over
`ListLetters`; the controller is UIKit and is not built on the machine
the suite runs on.

Against the code as it was, the change undone by hand with its new names
left in place: the first 5 new tests all failed, 15 failures, and the
Save Draft test with the putting away in its order 3 more. Then each
part undone alone, the new and changed tests run each time, counted as
failures in tests. The first sheet letting go closing the letter as
well: 5 in 1, the test of a letter opened from its row, which ended with
two copies on the server. The passes not held: 5 in 2. A letter that
landed while its save was out left on the iPad: 5 in 1, two rows at the
landing.

Then the copy that landed: the change to `LocalDrafts` for it undone,
its tests kept. The 5 tests for it all failed, 11 failures: two rows at
each second save, the copy's row as the sent letter's sheet closed, and
the password test at its first check, since nothing was hidden at all.
Then each part undone alone. A sent or deleted letter's copy not hidden:
2 in 1, the Send test. No check of the password: 2 in 1, the password
test. The count of saves taken as the upload landed rather than as it
set off: 1 in 1, the copy whose upload went before the save.

The Outbox test came after, for the claim above that the copy that
landed is not listed while the letter waits in the Outbox. The copy
hidden for a letter in Drafts only, not for one in the Outbox
(`replacedInDrafts` taking the landed copies of the letters with no
`outbox` alone): 2 failures in 1, the Outbox test, the copy's row there
as the sheet closed and while the letter waited. Every other test of
`DraftRowAtOnceTests`, `ComposeActionsTests`, `OutboxTests` and
`LocalDraftsTests` passed, 158, so nothing else stood for it.

The full suite, serially, with nothing undone: 1,762 tests, 5 skipped,
none failing. The release build for the iPad links.

## B-088 — FIXED 2026-10-20, found on the iPad and seen there fixed but for another letter under the original's UID. A forward whose original had moved looked for it in All Mail once for each file

**What was seen.** On the iPad on 2026-09-30, in B-051's check: a forward
of a letter with two PDFs, sent with no connection, its files' UID written
in the store as another Inbox letter's. In the next launch it went from the
Outbox with both PDFs, at their own sizes. The connection log had `UID
SEARCH X-GM-MSGID …` in All Mail before each part: the same letter looked
for twice. He sees nothing of it but the wait. Each search is a round trip
to Gmail's search, on the line his taps go on, before the part is asked
for, and a letter with ten files looked for its original ten times.

**What it was.** A letter being built fetches each file and each quoted
picture it carries on its own (`fetchCarried`, once for each part, from
`letterFiles`, `loadAttachments` and `loadPictures`). A part whose letter
is not under the UID it names is looked for in All Mail by Gmail's id for
it (`carriedPartElsewhere`, B-051), and where it was found was kept
nowhere. The next part of the same letter tried the UID it names, as each
part does, then searched All Mail again.

**Changed.** Where the search finds a letter in All Mail is kept for the
launch, by Gmail's id for it (`foundInAllMail`): the folder's name, its
UIDVALIDITY and the UID. Every part of the original asked for after that is
fetched from there first, for the letter being built and for any other
built in the launch that carries the same original, after the letter on
screen only and before the folder and UID it names
(`carriedPartFoundBefore`), as any part a letter carries is
(`carriedPart`): by the FETCH that describes the letter, which names it
before the part's bytes are asked for. No search goes, and with All Mail
still selected no SELECT either; nothing is asked again of the folder the
part names, where a part before did not find it. Not there any more,
another letter under that UID or none, or All Mail renumbered or refused,
and the log says so as it does for the folder the part names (`CARRIED-PART
folder=[Gmail]/All Mail reason=another-letter`, or `gone`, or `folder`).
What was kept is dropped and the part goes as the first did: the folder and
UID it names, then one search, and the parts after it come from where that
finds it. Not found, nothing of the letter goes, as before (`CARRIED-PART
not-found nothing-sent`).

What a forward of three files costs now, in its later launch. The original
archived since, as when he archives it while the forward waits in the
Outbox or in Drafts, so that its Inbox UID holds nothing: the first file a
SELECT of the Inbox, a FETCH there answered with nothing, a SELECT of All
Mail, the search and the part's two FETCHes; each file after it the two
FETCHes. Ten commands where there were eighteen, and one SELECT of All
Mail, which Gmail answers only once it has counted All Mail, where there
were three. With another letter under the UID, as on the iPad, the Inbox
was not asked again after the first file before either, this launch having
had the other letter there: ten commands where there were twelve, the two
searches gone. Both are counted as the tests count them, in a launch that
has listed only Sent before the pass. On the iPad the pass goes after the
Inbox's first page (the TODO's step 4). Where that page lists the other
letter under the UID, as it will for a letter as new as the original, the
first file asks nothing of the Inbox either: eight commands where there
were ten. With the Inbox still selected from that page, the archived
original's first file goes without its SELECT of the Inbox: one command
fewer, now and before.

**Not changed.** The first part of a letter not yet found in this launch
goes as before: the folder and UID it names, then a search of All Mail.
A part that names no letter goes by folder and UID alone. A line that
goes while a part is fetched leaves the letter waiting for the
connection, as before. Where a letter was found is kept for the launch,
not for one letter, so a letter built again goes there first from its
first part: an Outbox pass tried again after the line went during a
file, Save Draft and then Send, a later forward of the same original.
The letter on screen still goes before it, and its FETCH, naming the
letter, decides.

**What he sees.** Nothing new. A forward like it goes a little sooner.

**Tests.** Seven, all new, in `KeptReferencesTests.swift`: the shipping
`LocalDrafts` and repository over the scripted server, and a scripted
submission server. The first six count `UID SEARCH X-GM-MSGID` in All
Mail and pin the parts fetched there, by UID and section; the seventh
pins that nothing is asked.

- *Three files, the Outbox:* a forward of a letter with three files, sent
  with no connection; in a later launch the Inbox is renumbered so that
  the original's UID holds another letter. One search, the three parts
  from the UID it gave, each file its own and none the other letter's.
- *Three files, Drafts:* the same forward kept as a draft and taken to
  Drafts in a later launch: one search, and the copy carries the three.
- *A picture and a file:* a forward whose quote shows a picture and which
  carries a file, both of one original. The picture, fetched first, finds
  it, and the file comes from there: one search.
- *Renumbered between two files:* All Mail renumbered under the
  UIDVALIDITY it had once the first file's bytes are fetched, so that the
  UID it was found under holds a letter with three files at the same
  sections. The second file is not taken from it, the log says
  `reason=another-letter` for All Mail, the original is looked for once
  more, and the second and third files come from its new UID: two
  searches for three files.
- *Three files, the original archived:* the first forward's, the original
  taken out of the Inbox by another client before the later launch, so
  that its UID there holds nothing. Two SELECTs in all, the Inbox's and
  All Mail's, both for the first file; one FETCH asked of the Inbox; one
  search; the three parts from the UID it gave, two FETCHes each.
- *All Mail renumbered for the next connection:* the same, and the line
  goes as the second file's first FETCH is out. The connection made again
  finds All Mail under a new UIDVALIDITY, numbered from 1. The log says
  `reason=folder` for All Mail, then `reason=gone` for the Inbox; the
  original is looked for once more, and the second and third files come
  from its new UID: two searches, the three files sent, nothing left in
  the Outbox. RFC 3501 lets UIDs change between sessions only, under a new
  UIDVALIDITY, so the renumbering is met here as it would be: on the new
  connection's SELECT.
- *The original on screen:* the archived original's forward goes from
  the Outbox and finds it in All Mail, which the launch keeps. Put back
  in the Inbox under a new UID, opened there and forwarded again in the
  same launch, its three files come from the letter on screen: no
  command at all, and no `CARRIED-PART` in the log.

For the renumberings, the scripted server can change its mail between two
commands (`change(after:_:)`): the moment the command named has been
carried out, before its reply goes. For the last, it holds the second
file's answer (`holdReplies`) until All Mail is renumbered and the line
cut.

Against the code as it was: the first six all failed, 18 failures. Three
searches for three files, two for the picture and the file, three in place
of two after the renumbering; with the original archived, six SELECTs,
three of them All Mail's. All Mail renumbered for the next connection,
nothing was sent: the search found the letter under its old UID, and the
FETCH there met the renumbering and took it for the letter not found, the
forward left in the Outbox saying its attachment could not be downloaded.
Then parts of the change undone one at a time, the six run each time. The
refusal of the UID kept caught only when it is another letter or none, and
taken for the connection when its folder is renumbered: the last test
failed, 9 failures, nothing sent, the forward left in the Outbox as one
waiting for the connection; the other five passed. No second look after a
refused UID: both renumbering tests failed, 7 and 9 failures, nothing sent;
the other four passed. The UID kept used without the FETCH naming the
letter: the first renumbering test failed, 7 failures, two of the other
letter's files sent as the second and third, and the last failed on its
log. The UID kept tried after the folder and UID the part names: the
archived test failed on its SELECTs, the FETCHes asked of the Inbox and its
log, and the last on the order of its log.

The seventh came after, for the order "after the letter on screen only":
in the other six the forward is sent by a repository that has opened
nothing. The letter on screen not asked before the UID kept
(`fetchCarried`): it failed, 2 failures, a SELECT of All Mail, then the
two FETCHes for each file, and the log saying each was found there. The
other 33 tests of `KeptReferencesTests` passed.

The full suite, serially: 1,762 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

The photos were small so that the forward, 749 KB with the quoted

2. *The forward, offline.* Sent at 14:51 with Airplane Mode on: in the
   Outbox, with four parts in the store, the quoted signature's picture

   app ended at 14:52.
3. *Its UID another letter's:* not made, as above.
4. *Back, without the edit.* Airplane Mode off, the app opened at
   14:52:24. After the Inbox's first page the forward went by itself, each
   of its four parts by the letter's FETCH and its `BODY.PEEK` at UID 301

5. *Arrived:* "Fwd: R6 B-088 three", its three photos at the original's

6. *The original archived instead,* in the app, the store not edited. The
