## B-089 — FIXED 2026-10-20, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. A letter read from its All Mailboxes hit kept its unread dot in the Inbox

**What he saw.** Seen on the iPad on 2026-10-03, during B-062's check. In
the Inbox he searches All Mailboxes and taps an unread hit: its dot goes,
and the Inbox's count goes down by one. He cancels the search, and the
Inbox's row for the same letter still has its dot. It kept it until the
Inbox was fetched again.

**What it was.** An All Mailboxes hit is All Mail's row of the letter,
under All Mail's id. The Inbox's row under the search is the same letter
under the Inbox's id. The tap's read mark took the dot off by id
(`ListLetters.reading`, from `markReadIfNeeded`), so off the hit alone.
The STORE went on All Mail's UID, and Gmail had the letter as read, since
`\Seen` is the letter's and not the label's. The counts came off every
folder the hit is counted in, the Inbox among them. Cancelling the search
puts the Inbox's rows back as they were, with no round trip
(`endSearch`), so the Inbox's row kept the dot it had before the tap. A
tap on that row then would have sent a second STORE, and taken one off
the counts a second time: one too low until the next sweep. Edit mode's
Mark on a hit, both ways, and the reading pane's read mark of a letter
in a conversation went by the same id.

The kept copy did the same. A read mark or a flag the server took changes
every kept row of the letter (`MailShelf.read`, `MailShelf.flagged`), but
the letter was found from the row the write named on its own folder's
kept page. All Mail's page is kept only once All Mail has been opened,
and holds only its newest letters. A hit found on neither changed
nothing, and the next launch drew the Inbox's kept row with its dot, or
without its flag, until the first page came.

The watch's news did the same, found once the rest was fixed. A letter
that comes while he is scrolled down is held as the watch fetched it, to
go on at the top when he is back there (`ListLetters.hold`, `showNews`),
and the read mark changed only the list's letters and the hits. A new
letter came while he was down the Inbox, and was held, unread; he
searched All Mailboxes for it and read its hit, and the count went down
by one; he cancelled and went to the top, and the held row went on with
its dot. A check asked before the STORE and come after it did the same
without his scrolling, a check that set off just before the search
landing during it: it brought the Inbox's copy as the server had it when
asked, unread, and that copy went on as it came. A tap on the row then
sent a second STORE.

And the kept copy of a Delete or a Spam from a hit, older than B-089: the
letter was found from the row the MOVE named on its own folder's kept page
(`MailShelf.gone`), so a hit binned or marked as spam with All Mail never
opened left the Inbox's kept row of it, which the next launch drew in his
Inbox until the first page came.

The flag on the list's rows was already right: Flag goes on the letter's
twins under other mailboxes' ids (`ListLetters.setFlagged`), seen on the
iPad. Not on the watch's news held; see Not covered.

**Changed.**

- A read mark goes on the letter wherever the list holds it: under its own
  id, and under every other id the list holds with the same Gmail message
  id (`ListEdit.copies`), the watch's news held to go on among them. A row
  with no Gmail id is matched as a twin, as Flag's are. Two rows whose
  Gmail ids differ are two letters. Each copy is held over a listing asked
  before the server took the mark, as the row's own is, a listing asked
  after has the say on each, and a refusal puts each back. The list's copy
  of the letter is used, or the letter itself when the list has no row
  under its id, as for a letter the reading pane opened from a hit after
  the search had ended.
- The tap, Edit mode's Mark as Read and Mark as Unread, and the reading
  pane's read mark all go this way: each hands the list the letter now,
  not its id.
- A letter the watch brings takes his read mark on a copy of it as it is
  held (`ListLetters.withHisRead`), while the mark is on its way or taken
  and not yet seen by a listing asked after: under its own id, as a
  listing's row does, or by the same Gmail message id. The last mark he
  made, where there are two. Taken, it is held over a listing as the
  rest are; refused, it goes back with them, whether the copy was held
  before the mark or came while the STORE was out.
- A listing's rows take it the same way, once the marks that listing has
  seen are gone: the Inbox's page asked before the STORE and come after
  it, over the kept page after a launch or under the search, can bring
  the letter's Inbox copy the list did not have when he read the hit, as
  the server had it then, unread. It goes on read.
- The kept copy: a read mark or a flag on a row that is not on its
  folder's kept page goes by the Gmail id the write named, onto every
  kept row of that letter (`MailShelf.changeLetter`). A row that is there
  goes as before. A Delete or a Spam goes the same way: the letter is
  found from its row on the folder's kept page or, with none there, by
  the Gmail id the MOVE named, and leaves every kept page but the
  Trash's or Spam's (`MailShelf.gone`).
- The counts go by the letter, not the row (`ReadBilling`): by its Gmail
  message id, or by the row's id where the row has none. With the dot now
  on every copy, he can read the letter on one copy and mark it unread on
  the other, and billed by row the unread forgot only its own row. Read
  in the Inbox, Mark as Unread on its hit, and the Inbox's row, dotted
  again once the search was cancelled, tapped: nothing came off the
  second time. Read from the hit, Mark as Unread on the Inbox's row, and
  the hit read again in a new search: the same. Either way the counts
  ended one too high, a count with no dot to go with it, until the next
  sweep, which with the Inbox showing comes only with news or a Refresh.
  Now an unread on any copy forgets the billing for all of them, and a
  read on another copy of a letter billed already takes nothing off.

**Not changed.** One STORE, on the hit's own UID, as before, and the
counts are billed once per letter, on whichever copy. On the list, Delete
and Move already took the twins (B-062); the kept copy of a Delete or a
Spam is above. Flag on the list is still matched as twins. Nothing more is
fetched.

**What he sees.** A letter read from its All Mailboxes hit has no dot on
its Inbox row when the search is cancelled, and the Inbox's count is one
lower, once. Mark as Unread on a hit puts the dot back on the Inbox's
row too. Read, marked unread and read again, on either copy, the count
ends one lower than it began. A letter that came while he was scrolled
down, read from its hit, goes on at the top without its dot. A launch
draws the Inbox's kept page the same way, and without a letter he
binned or marked as spam from its hit. No new words.

**Tests.** `ReadOnEveryCopyTests`, seventeen, over the shipping repository
and the scripted server where there is a server to ask, with the list's
own letters: a hit read at the tap, the Inbox's row without its dot at
once, over a listing asked before the STORE landed and after the search
ended, one STORE on the hit's UID, billed once, and a listing asked after
has the say; a refused mark, the dot back on both and nothing billed; Edit
mode's Mark as Unread and Mark as Read on a hit, each reaching the Inbox's
row; a read mark made after the search ended, found from the letter; the
copies found by the Gmail id, by twins only without one, never a letter
with another Gmail id; the wiring of Edit mode's Mark, read from the
source; and the kept copy, a read mark and a flag on a hit changing the
Inbox's kept row with All Mail never opened, and with All Mail's page kept
without the letter, and a launch drawing both; and a letter binned and
another marked as spam from their hits with All Mail never opened, off the
Inbox's kept page and not drawn by a launch, the Inbox's other kept rows
left. Four on the watch's news, with the list's letters alone: a letter
read from its hit while the watch holds the Inbox's copy goes on read,
billed once, and Mark as Unread on a hit reaches a held copy; a check
asked before the STORE that lands after it brings it read, and so does one
that lands while the STORE is out, and once a listing asked after the
STORE has come the server has the say; a refused mark puts the held copy's
dot back, held before the mark or come while the STORE was out, and
nothing is billed; and of two marks on the letter, read and then unread on
two hits, the news takes the last. Two on a listing, with the list's letters
alone: the Inbox's page asked before the STORE brings the letter's copy
the list did not have, and it goes on read, billed once; and the same
page landing while the STORE is out takes the mark, and the dot comes back
when the server refuses it. Three on the counts, with the list's
letters alone: read in the Inbox, marked unread on its hit and read in the
Inbox again; read from its hit, marked unread in the Inbox and read from
its hit again, each one off the Inbox's count and All Mail's, as the
letter ends read; and the billing itself, a read on one copy refused on
another, an unread on one forgotten for both, rows with no Gmail id billed
by their own ids, and a binned row with none not billed again when its
copy was. `KeptPlaceTests`, `KeptCopyTests` and `ConversationOrderTests`
hand `reading` the row rather than its id. `PaneActionsTests`' two B-062
tests of what the list does at the tap and as the read mark is answered
call `reading` and `readAnswered`, as the tap does; they called
`ListLetters.setRead`, which nothing in the app called any more, and which
is gone.

Each part undone in the worktree, one at a time, the new tests run: the
copies left out of `reading`, 5 failures in 3 tests; the answer going
back on the letter's own id alone, 2 in 2; the copies not held over a
listing, 3 in 2; the kept copy found by the folder's kept row alone, 4
in 1; the copies matched as twins only, 1 in 1. The list and the kept
copy both as they were: 9 failures in 4 tests. The counts billed by row
id, as before: 7 failures in the three tests on them, and the two on the
list found the counts back where they began, not one lower.

Then the watch's news and the kept copy of a Delete, each undone alone
and the fifteen run. `ListLetters` as it was before them: 6 failures in
3 tests; the refusal test passed, there being nothing put on to put
back. The news left out of `reading`: 3 in 1. The news not taking his
mark as it is held: 3 in 2. The news left out of the list's changes, so
of the mark and of its refusal: 4 in 2. A mark taken on as the news is
held not put back when refused: 1 in 1. The first mark found taken in
place of the last: 1 in 1. The kept copy of a Delete or a Spam found by
the folder's kept row alone: 5 in 1. The listing's rows taking his mark by their own
id alone, as before: 2 failures in the two tests on a listing.

The full suite, serially: 1,764 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-20**, the same build as B-087's, the same
day, three panes, on the test account. Three letters To A with `+b089`,
subjects beginning "R6 B-089". All Mail was opened before the steps, in
B-088's put-back, and not during them; its kept page held no B-089 letter.
Times are the iPad's clock, and the count is the Inbox's. Every step of
the TODO check passed. In 5 and 7 the app was ended once the Home Screen
was up; the swipe into the app switcher was not made.

1. *Two letters,* "R6 B-089 one" and "two", both in with the dot: the
   count from 13 to 15.
2. *Read from a hit.* "R6 B-089 one" tapped on its All Mailboxes hit: the
   dot went, 15 to 14. Cancel: the Inbox's row had no dot. Tapped: still

3. *Mark from a hit.* Mark as Unread on the hit: its dot back, 15, and the

4. *Flag from a hit.* Flag on the hit, Cancel: the Inbox's row flagged.

5. *The kept copy.* "R6 B-089 two" read from its hit, 14 to 13. The

6. *News held.* Scrolled two screens down, "R6 B-089 three" sent. The
   watch's next check logged `NEWS folder=INBOX arrived=1`, 13 to 14, and
   a minute on the list was still down. Read from its hit: 14 to 13.

7. *Binned from a hit.* "R6 B-089 two" from its hit, Delete in the reading

The B-087 to B-089 letters are in Trash only, and every other folder is as

Seen in passing:

**Not covered.**

## B-090 — FIXED 2026-10-20, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. A screenshot shared from its editor could not be attached

**What he saw.** Seen on the test iPad (iPadOS 16.5.1) on 2026-10-20,
three times of three. A screenshot taken, its floating thumbnail tapped
within a second to open the editor, then Share, Blackmail: the sheet came
up with Cancel and "The photo could not be attached." and nothing else. With
two screenshots in the editor, "The photos could not be attached.". There
was no letter to send. The same screenshot shared from Photos goes, as the
PNG it is (B-036). This is the TODO's share check 7, a picture with no
name, which expects it to go named as Mail names one: "image0.png", or
"image0.jpeg".

**What it was.** Not confirmed on the iPad. The words are
`ShareItems.leftOut`'s for a share of pictures alone of which none came. So
the provider was counted as a picture, by a picture type it offered
(`SharedPhoto.fileType`) or by what `UIImage` could read, and
`ShareItems.picture` staged nothing. It asked for one type only, the one
chosen, as a file and then as bytes, and neither gave anything ImageIO
opens. By the look of it the editor hands its picture over as a `UIImage`,
an object, and not as a file or as bytes under the type it names; or under
another type, which was never asked for.

Or the type gave a file or bytes that are no picture. Only a source ImageIO
did not make was taken as not opened, and ImageIO makes one of what is no
picture at all, with nothing in it: on a Mac (macOS 26.3, 2026-10-20) a
keyed archive, words and no bytes at all each opened with a count of
nought and no type. Such a source went on to `stage`, which found no
picture at its index and left it out there, `way=left out, no picture in
it`, as one that could not be made a picture, and tried nothing else. Both
readings give the same words.

Which of these, the log would have said: each picture's `SHARE-PICTURE`
line has what the provider offered and how it went. But the log was written
to a file only at a send's end (`CaptureProbe.dumpTranscript`), and a sheet
with no letter has no Send. The line was never where a check could read it.

**Changed.**

- *Every picture type it offers.* A picture is read as the type chosen, as
  before, its file and then its bytes. Where neither gives what ImageIO
  opens, it is read the same way as each other type the provider offers
  that `UTType` says is a picture, in the provider's own order, each once
  (`SharedPhoto.typesToRead`). Not another app's private types, Photos'
  thumbnails among them: a photo whose own file gave nothing is left out,
  and said, never sent as a small copy of itself. Only a type not opened
  goes on to the next. A picture opened and not made one, or left out for
  the room or the memory, is the same picture whatever type it is read as,
  and is answered there, as before.
- *Not opened is no picture in it.* A file or bytes are opened only when
  ImageIO finds a picture in them, a count of one or more (`read`). One it
  makes a source of and finds nothing in, as it does of what is no
  picture, is as one not given: the file goes on to its bytes, the bytes
  to the next type, and the last to the object. A picture in it that
  cannot be made one is left out there, as before; its line says `no
  picture at its index`, or `not made a JPEG`. A photo from Photos opens
  with its one picture, and goes as it did.
- *Then the object.* With no type left, the provider is asked for a
  `UIImage` (`loadObject`), and failing that for its own item, which is the
  `UIImage` itself where the sharing app put one there (`loadItem`). It is
  made a file by ImageIO, written straight onto the disk where it is staged
  and measured there (`ShareItems.object`, in `SharedPhotoObject.swift`): a
  PNG where the provider says it is one, as a picture of the screen is, or
  where the picture has a clear part, which a JPEG has not got; otherwise a
  JPEG at the JPEG's quality, as any picture not kept whole is made one
  (`SharedPhoto.objectWay`). Its bytes, their MIME type and its name's
  extension all come from that one way (`SharedPhoto.objectFile`), so an
  image0.png is a PNG and goes as image/png. At its own size and never
  turned; its orientation, where it is not upright, goes as a tag
  (`SharedPhoto.exifOrientation`), as a photo sent as its own bytes keeps
  its.
- *An item that is a file or bytes.* The provider's own item may be a file
  on the iPad or bytes rather than a `UIImage`. Then it is read by ImageIO,
  inside the item's callback, as a type's file or bytes are, by the same
  rules and bounds, and never as a `UIImage`; a file is named by its own
  name, as one handed over any other way is (`ShareItems.picture(item:)`).
  Anything else is left out, not opened.
- *Bounded.* This is the one place the extension decodes a picture whole: a
  `UIImage` cannot be read at a half, a quarter or an eighth. Decoded, a
  picture is four bytes a pixel, and it is taken at three times that while
  it is made a file, as every decoder nobody measured is: twelve bytes a
  pixel. Its size is the `CGImage`'s, read before a pixel of it is decoded.
  It may take three fifths of the memory left, read right before, or of the
  80 MB assumed where the iPad does not say; and never more than 9 million
  pixels, whatever the memory says (`SharedPhoto.objectRefused`). The most a
  share extension is known to be given is the test iPad's 180 MB; three
  fifths of that is 108 MB, and 108 MB at twelve bytes a pixel is 9
  million. His iPad's screen, 2160 by 1620, is 3.5 million pixels, 42 MB at
  the peak; the test iPad's, 2388 by 1668, 4 million and 48 MB, inside the
  80 MB assumed; the largest iPad screen, 2752 by 2064, 68 MB. A
  48-megapixel object would need 576 MB: it is left out, and said, and
  never decoded.
- *Named as Mail names a picture with no name* (B-036): the sharing app's
  suggestion where it has one, and with none "image0.png" or "image0.jpeg",
  counted on across the share with the other pictures with no name
  (`ShareItems.Staging.unnamed`). Two from the editor go as image0.png and
  image1.png.
- *No location.* A `UIImage` carries no metadata at all: no GPS, no EXIF,
  only its pixels, their colour profile and its orientation. Nothing but
  the orientation, and for a JPEG its quality, is written into the file
  (`SharedPhoto.write`), so there is nothing to strip.
- *The log.* A picture's line says every type tried, in order, the last the
  one that decided: `read=public.png,public.jpeg`, `read=public.png,object`
  for the `UIImage`, `…,item` for the provider's own item, with `(public.png
  inside)` where the item was a file or bytes; and for the object `way=PNG
  made of the object, N MB available`, or `JPEG`. An object written larger
  than what is left of the letter's room is taken away again and its line
  says `left out, no room`, as a JPEG made here does; one ImageIO did not
  write, `not written` (`SharedPhoto.objectLeftOut`, from what
  `Staging.written` measured, `lastMeasured`). When the sheet says a
  picture or a video could not be attached, in place of the letter or in a
  line over it, the log so far is written out as a send's end writes it,
  `blackmail-send-<time>-left-out.txt` in the extension's tmp, among the
  newest ten kept (`ShareItems.keepLog`), under its own time rather than
  the last send's. So the next check can read why.

**Not changed.** A picture that opens as its first type goes as before: as
its own bytes, whole, or a JPEG made here. A photo from Photos still goes
as its own bytes, and its line is as it was. A picture is still what the
provider offers by a picture type, or what `UIImage` could read; a page,
words, a file and a video go as they did. The sheet's words, and when it
says them, are as they were. A letter's send writes its transcript as
before.

**What he sees.** A screenshot shared from its editor, marked up or not,
comes into the sheet as "image0.png" (or "image0.jpeg"), two of them as
image0.png and image1.png, and Send sends them. No new words.

**Tests.** `SharePictureFallbackTests`, twenty-one. The types tried: the one
chosen first, then the provider's other picture types in its order, each
once, never one that is not a picture or a private one. The object's
bound: twelve bytes a pixel; never more than 9 million pixels with a
terabyte to spare, 9 million exactly allowed; under it, the memory left or
the 80 MB assumed, three fifths exactly allowed, a byte less refused; the
screens of his iPad, the test iPad and the largest iPad; none with no
size; and the line for one left out for the memory. A PNG or a JPEG, by
what is offered and a clear part; its name, the suggestion's or image0,
image1; its bytes, its MIME type and its name from the one way, for every
offer with and without a clear part; two staged straight onto the disk as
image0.png and image1.png, nothing through memory; one written larger
than the room left taken away, measured and said `no room`, one not

- Twelve bytes a pixel is not measured, only taken as every format nobody
  measured is (B-036). Whether ImageIO holds the file it makes in memory
  before it writes it is not known; the three times leaves room for it.
- An object longer than 4096 px on a side within the 9 million, a long thin
  one, goes at its own size, not made 4096 as a JPEG made from a file is.
  It is never more pixels than the 16 million that rule allows at 4:3.
- An object not upright goes with an orientation tag, its pixels as they
  are, and fewer mail programs read a PNG's tag than a JPEG's. A picture of
  the screen is upright.

## B-091 — FIXED 2026-10-20, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. With Airplane Mode on, Flag in the reading pane went back with "Can't connect to mail server." only some 19 s later, and a letter tapped meanwhile said "Loading…" as long

**What he saw.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-20, during the reading
pane's B-041 check ("Flag with Wi-Fi turned off"), with Airplane Mode in
place of Wi-Fi, twice. A letter open in the reading pane, its FETCH
answered 10 and 24 s before. Airplane Mode on, from Control
Centre, and four seconds later Flag in the pane, then a tap on another
row: the flag came on at the tap, and the pane said "Loading…" for the
other letter. Then nothing. Timed the second time: 19 s, and then in the
same frame the flag went back, one "Can't connect to mail server." came
up, and the pane said the letter could not be downloaded. The first time
it was somewhere between 11 and 38 s, with no frames taken between. In
an earlier run that was stopped, the Flag waited behind the watch's
NOOP, already written onto the cut connection, and came back after 41 to
43 s. A Flag made after that, with the connection gone, was refused
within a fifth of a second, the flag never drawn. Gmail had neither
letter flagged afterwards, so the screen ended as the server had it.

Not by design. Nothing is kept to go when the network is back (D-016): a
refused Flag goes back and he is told (B-041). But TODO's check has that
with Wi-Fi off at once, or after the 30 s read deadline on a socket left
half open, and Airplane Mode is neither: the iPad knew the network had
gone.

**What it was.** The STORE was written onto the connection already open,
`UID STORE 324 +FLAGS.SILENT (\Flagged)`, with no probe in front of it,
the connection having been used within ninety seconds (B-024), and
nothing answered. No DEADLINE line came: the stack gave the connection
up first, at about 19 s. The letter's FETCH waited behind the STORE at
the client's gate and failed with it.

Nothing told the client the network had gone. Once a connection is up,
`TLSConnection` hands every later state to the connect's report, which
takes only the first (`LinkOpening`), and nothing listened to the
connection's viability, which is how `NWConnection` says a connection
that is up has no path. So the client went on writing onto it, and each
command waited for the stack, or for its deadline. B-024's probe would
not have helped had it gone: its NOOP would have been written onto the
same connection and waited the same.

**Changed.**

- The device's link listens: `TLSConnection` sets `NWConnection`'s
  `viabilityUpdateHandler` before the connection starts, on the queue the
  states come on, and hands what it says to the transport's
  `LinkViability` (`LinkTransport.swift`). It is heard only while the
  link is up: from the connect's report that it is, on the link's own
  queue and before the connect is settled, to `close()`. Up is a path,
  so the LOGIN after it is never refused for a word said while it was
  being made, and nothing a link says once it has been let go of is kept.
  The handler is let go of with the connection. Each change while the
  link is up is one line in the connection log, naming the link by its
  port, never an address: `LINK port=993 viable=false` or `LINK port=993
  viable=true` for the mail's connection, `port=465` for a Send's, which
  listens too and is never asked. None comes from a try to connect, nor
  from a link already closed.
- `MailTransport.pathIsGone`: the system has said there is no path, and
  not that it is back.
- `IMAPClient` writes no command onto a connection whose path is gone.
  Each command is asked about before it is written (`performCommand`):
  with no path the connection is let go of, the command is not written,
  `NO-PATH UID FETCH not-sent` goes in the log, and it fails as a dropped
  connection does. So a read goes once more, on a new connection, which
  with no network fails at once, a new connection's `.waiting` being a
  failure (`TLSConnection`). The probe in front of a write, the watch's
  NOOP and the LOGOUT go the same way.
- A write is asked about first, at its turn at the gate and before its
  SELECT (`throwUnsentIfDisconnected`): the connection let go of the same
  way, `NO-PATH UID STORE nothing-sent` (`UID MOVE`, `UID EXPUNGE`,
  `APPEND`), and the write turned away as `Unsent`, not a byte of it
  written. So it goes once, on a new connection, if there is a network
  for one, and with none it fails at once (`sendingOnce`, B-049). Written
  onto the cut connection, it could never have been sent again, since
  nothing could say it had not gone.
- A command kept off the link inside a write, once the write has begun,
  is a plain failure, never `Unsent`, and its line is the command's own,
  `not-sent`: the EXPUNGE of a Delete in the Trash whose `\Deleted` STORE
  went and was answered as the path went is `NO-PATH UID EXPUNGE
  not-sent`, and the Delete fails and is not sent again, the letter left
  marked for the next Delete. Sent again on a new connection the STORE
  would have gone twice, and through `move`'s fallback, on a server
  without MOVE, the COPY twice: on a server other than Gmail, a second
  letter in the Trash. So `nothing-sent` says nothing of the write went,
  and `not-sent` that this one command was kept back, perhaps after
  another of the same write.

**Not changed.**

- A command already written is not asked about. Its answer is read when
  it comes, and if the path went with it on the wire it waits as before,
  for the stack or its deadline, with whatever he taps meanwhile waiting
  behind it at the gate. Closing the connection the moment the path goes
  would end that wait too, and was not done: at every brief drop it would
  cut off a command with its answer on the way, and a write cut off can
  never be sent again.
- Nothing is kept to go later (D-016). A Flag, Delete or Move refused
  goes back and he is told, as before, only at once.
- A good path: the question is one more hop to the transport for each
  command, and nothing else. A path lost and found again on the same
  connection, with nothing written meanwhile, leaves the connection in
  use.
- **Sending, checked: not the same defect, not changed.** `SMTPClient`
  makes a connection for each letter and ends it with the letter, so a
  Send never writes onto a connection made earlier, which is where this
  came from. With Airplane Mode on, a Send's connect goes `.waiting` and
  fails at once, and the letter waits in the Outbox at once
  (`Outbox.waits(after:)`). A Send waits only if the path goes during the
  letter's own few seconds, mostly its upload, which is on the wire.
  Asking before each line would gain at most the seconds between two of
  them, and a wrong word of no path would put in the Outbox a letter that
  would have gone.

**What he sees.** With Airplane Mode on or Wi-Fi off and the connection
still open, Flag in the pane: the flag comes off again and "Can't connect
to mail server." is up within a fraction of a second, so quickly that the
flag may never be drawn. A letter tapped says at once that it could not
be downloaded. A Delete or a Move: the row back and the alert, at once.
With the network back, the next Flag goes once. No new words.

**Tests.** `NoPathTests`, fourteen, over the shipping repository and
client and the scripted server, whose `hasNoPath` is Airplane Mode: each
open link told it has no path, as the device's viability tells it, bytes
written onto such a link going nowhere and never answered, and a new
connection failing at once. `losePathOfOpenLinks` cuts the open links
alone, a new connection made as usual. The deadline is five seconds, and
each call is given one.

- *Refused at once, nothing written:* a Flag with the path gone, within
  half a second, the flag not set, `LINK port=993 viable=false` and
  `NO-PATH UID STORE nothing-sent` in the log, and one new connection
  tried and not made;
  the same after ninety seconds of quiet, its probe kept off the link; a
  letter opened, `NO-PATH UID FETCH not-sent`; a Flag and a letter tapped
  behind it, as on the iPad, both; and the watch's check, its NOOP kept
  off the link.
- *Once:* the open link with no path and a network for a new one, a
  Delete goes once on the new connection, LOGIN, SELECT and UID MOVE, and
  nothing on the old; the path gone, a Flag refused, and with the path
  back the next Flag connects and goes once, one STORE in all.
- *A write that went in part:* a Delete in the Trash whose STORE was
  answered as the path went: the EXPUNGE kept off the link, `NO-PATH UID
  EXPUNGE not-sent`, the Delete failed, one STORE in all and no new
  connection, the letter in the Trash still, marked; and a Delete on a
  server without MOVE whose COPY was answered as the path went: the STORE
  kept off, one COPY in all, the letter in the Inbox still, unmarked.
- *Left alone:* a STORE already written as the path goes is answered and
  lands, once, and only the letter tapped behind it is kept off the link,
  and opens on a new connection.
- *A good path:* a Flag, a letter and a Delete, each its one command on
  the connection open, nothing in the log about the path; a path lost and
  found on the same link leaves it in use, with no reconnect.
- *The link:* a line for each change, naming the link by its port, none
  for a word that changes nothing, and a link never told anything has a
  path. It hears only while it is up: a word of no path said while it is
  being made is not kept, and the link comes up with a path; one said
  after its close is neither kept nor logged; and a link closed before
  its connect said it was up never hears.
- *The device's half,* read from `TLSConnection`'s source, which does
  not build on the host: the handler set before the start, `.ready` the
  report and nothing else, the link named by its port, the handler let go
  of before the cancel.

The scripted server's link has the model above, and the scripted
submission server says it always has a path.

Against the code as it was, `pathIsGone` false whatever the link is
told: 9 of the 11 failed, 41 failures. The two that passed hold what was
right already, a good path, and the device's half, which the next ones
undo. Each part undone in the worktree, one at a time, the eleven run,
counted as failures in tests: the command's question left out of
`performCommand`, 19 in 4; the write's left out, 3 in 3, the write
refused and never tried on a new connection; an answer read after the
path went thrown away, or a read cut off once it had, the rejected way,
1 in 1 each, the command left alone; no path never coming back, 6 in 2;
in the source, the handler not set, 3 in 1, up not told, 2 in 1, the
handler kept at the close, 2 in 1.

The three tests added since, with the changes to the log's lines, each
undone the same way, the fourteen run: the command's refusal thrown as
`Unsent`, 11 in the two writes that went in part, each sent again on a
second connection, LOGIN, SELECT, then STORE and EXPUNGE, or COPY, STORE
and EXPUNGE, and each reported done; the write's line back to
`not-sent`, 3 in 3; the link not named, 13 in 13; a word heard while the
link is being made, 4 in 1; after its close, 2 in 1; `close()` not
telling the link, 2 in 1; the connect's report not telling it it is up,
54 in 8, every command written onto the cut link and waiting there; a
link closed before it came up hearing all the same, 2 in 1; in the
source, the link named port 0, 1 in 1, and `.ready` telling the link as
well, 2 in 1.

The full suite, serially: 1,778 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-20**, a build of master with B-090 and
B-091 (cba64fa), three panes, on the test account. Two letters To A with
`+b091` before the "@", "R6 B-091 one" and "R6 B-091 two". The
connection was cut with Airplane Mode, which turned Wi-Fi off with it,
the iPad reached by its cable; frames were taken some 0.07 s apart for
nearly 3 s after each tap, then to 25 s. Every step of the TODO check
passed, 2 twice, but for one part not possible on this iPad: the tap on
"B-091 two" straight after the Flag.

1. *Two letters,* both in the Inbox after Refresh.
2. *Flag, the connection open.* "R6 B-091 one" open, Airplane Mode on,
   and some six seconds later Flag in the pane. iPadOS said the link had
   no network, `LINK port=993 viable=false`, a third of a second after
   Airplane Mode went on. At the Flag, 0.1 s after the tap, `NO-PATH UID
   STORE nothing-sent`, and nothing written after it until the LOGIN once
   Airplane Mode was off. The first time the flag was never drawn; the
   second, the next tap 0.05 s behind it, it showed at 0.14 s and was gone
   at 0.21 s. Each time "Can't connect to mail server." was coming up by
   0.21 s, one alert, the same to 25 s, and no "Loading…" anywhere. The
   build before held the flag 19 s. The tap on "R6 B-091 two" fell on the
   alert both times and opened nothing: a tap takes some 0.1 s here, and
   the alert was up first. The TODO's step now says so.
3. *A letter, the connection open.* Back online, and Airplane Mode on
   again with "R6 B-091 one" open: `viable=false` 0.34 s on, then the
   watch's check, `NO-PATH NOOP not-sent`. "R6 B-091 two" tapped: at
   0.19 s the pane had its header and "This message could not be
   downloaded.", and the alert was coming up.
4. *Back.* Airplane Mode off, a new connection, one LOGIN. Flag: one `UID
   STORE … +FLAGS.SILENT (\Flagged)`, answered OK, Gmail had it flagged,
   and the flag stayed through a Refresh. Flag again: one
   `-FLAGS.SILENT`, and Gmail had it unflagged.
5. *The log.* Only `port=993` lines. Three `viable=false`, 0.32 to 0.34 s
   after Airplane Mode went on, before the switch had finished, and never
   a `viable=true`: each link was let go of at its first command after
   the word. The watch's NOOP never went just before the word, and there
   was no DEADLINE line.
6. *Put back.* The two letters to Trash with Edit and Delete; Airplane
   Mode off, Wi-Fi on.

Gmail never had a letter flagged by an offline Flag.

**Not covered.**

- Wi-Fi turned off alone, Airplane Mode left off, was not tried on the
  iPad. Airplane Mode, which turned Wi-Fi off with it, was said within a
  third of a second each time (above).
- A command already on the wire as the network goes still waits for the
  stack or its deadline, and what he taps meanwhile behind it: the
  stopped run's 41 to 43 s behind the watch's NOOP. See Not changed.
- A word of no path while the network is in fact fine costs the next
  command a new connection, a LOGIN and a SELECT; a write then goes on it,
  once, and a read is answered there.
- A real drop of a second or two, a Wi-Fi reassociation or a moment's
  roam, behaves differently now. A command he makes in it used to be
  written, and could ride the drop out on TCP's retransmissions, its
  answer coming a moment late; now it is refused at once, "Can't connect
  to mail server.", since the one new connection it is allowed goes
  `.waiting` while the network is down, and that is a failure. Not seen
  on the iPad. If it is, the way to do better is a short wait at the
  gate, a second or two at most, for the path to come back before the
  connection is let go of; Airplane Mode's refusal would still come far
  inside the old 19 s.
- The path gone during a write's SELECT, or after it and before the
  write's first command: the write is kept off the link, as a plain
  failure, and is not tried on a new connection, though nothing of it was
  written. Kept so on purpose: the command's refusal cannot tell a write's
  first command from its second, which may follow one that went (see
  Changed), and `Unsent` there sends that one twice. `NoPathTests` holds
  it.
- Mail on the iPad keeps a change made offline and sends it later, as far
  as is known without trying it here. D-016 keeps no such queue, so the
  Flag is refused, at once now, where Mail would keep it.

## B-092 — FIXED 2026-10-21, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. A letter Gmail answered OK for and did not move went from the list, and came back only at a Refresh

**What he saw.** Seen once on the test iPad on 2026-10-21, and not again
when the same three letters were deleted the same way twice more, twelve
MOVEs in all. Edit, three Inbox rows ticked, Delete: all three rows went.
Gmail had moved two. The third, the first of the three sent, was in the
Inbox still, read, and not in the Trash. Its row came back only with a
Refresh more than two minutes later, and a second Delete took it. The
letter was never lost; for those minutes the list showed as deleted a
letter the Inbox still held.

Not by design. A Delete or Move the server did not take puts the row
back and says so (B-062).

**What it was.** Gmail's answer, and the client's reading of it. With
INBOX selected, `UID MOVE 343 "[Gmail]/Trash"` was answered in 0.89 s
with `OK [COPYUID 2 343 0] (Success)`: no EXPUNGE, and 0 for the
letter's UID in the Trash, which is no UID (RFC 4315). The two after it
had `* 68 EXPUNGE` and a COPYUID with a UID in it. Of about 116 MOVEs in
the connection logs kept, 112 had a COPYUID with a UID in it, one sent
in the wrong mailbox on 2026-09-28 (B-039) was answered `OK Success`
with no COPYUID, and one is this. Why Gmail answered so is not known.

`IMAPClient.move` took any tagged OK for a move done, and read neither
the COPYUID nor whether an EXPUNGE came. So the batch was told the
letter had gone, the row taken off at the tap stayed off, and the
repository took the letter off the kept pages. The watch did not bring
it back: the row was still in the folder's list and the letter still in
the folder, no newer than the newest, which is neither news nor gone.
Only Refresh, which has the say, did.

**Changed.**

- A MOVE answered OK counts as done only if its answer shows it: a
  COPYUID whose source holds the letter, with as many UIDs in the
  destination and none of them 0; or, from a server without UIDPLUS,
  which gives no COPYUID, an EXPUNGE (`IMAPMoveAnswer`, new). The
  COPYUID is read on the tagged OK, where Gmail puts it, or on an
  untagged OK before the EXPUNGEs, where RFC 6851 puts it.
- An EXPUNGE names a sequence number, not a UID, and one for a letter
  taken out of the folder elsewhere at that moment, on another device,
  by a Gmail filter, can ride on any answer, a Delete's MOVE among them
  (RFC 3501 §7.4.1). So it is never taken for the letter's against the
  answer's own COPYUID, a 0 as on the iPad or another letter's: that
  answer with such an EXPUNGE on it would be this bug again. Nor where
  a server with UIDPLUS, as Gmail is, gave no COPYUID at all: every
  MOVE Gmail did had one, and its `OK Success` with none moved nothing.
  Either is looked into as below. A normal Gmail MOVE, with its COPYUID,
  is its one command as before.
- An answer that shows nothing is followed, in the same hold of the
  connection, by a look in the folder the letter was in: a NOOP, then
  `UID SEARCH UID n`. Gone, the move is done, and nothing is sent again.
  Still there, the same MOVE goes once more, and its answer is read the
  same way; showing nothing again, the folder is asked again. Still there
  after that, the move is refused: the letter is where it was, unmarked,
  its row back where it stood with "Can't connect to mail server.", and
  the kept copy keeps it. So too with the second MOVE refused, or the
  NOOP or the SEARCH. Nothing else is sent: no COPY, no `\Deleted`, no
  EXPUNGE.
- Never a COPY after a MOVE answered OK. A MOVE refused still falls back
  to COPY, `\Deleted` and UID EXPUNGE, as before; one answered OK with
  nothing to show does not, and neither does the second MOVE refused. The
  COPY would make a second letter in the Trash wherever the MOVE had
  landed. The second MOVE goes only once the folder has said it holds
  the letter still, and on Gmail a letter is in one place, the Trash
  excluding every other folder, so it has no second copy to make.
- The NOOP first because a server that has moved a letter and not told
  the connection can go on listing it in a SEARCH until it does (RFC
  2180 §4.1). Asked without it, such a letter would be sent again and
  refused, its row put back though it had gone; on a server that keeps
  what it has not told of, the second MOVE could copy it again.
- On a server without MOVE, the fallback's COPY is read for its COPYUID
  before anything is marked. One with 0 for the letter's UID, or naming
  another letter: nothing is marked or expunged, which would leave the
  letter in neither folder, the COPY is not sent again, and the move is
  refused, the letter where it was, unmarked. A COPY answered OK with no
  COPYUID, from a server without UIDPLUS, goes on as before: the server
  can say no more.
- The connection log names each step in numbers, never the letter:
  `MOVE-HOLLOW folder=INBOX uid=343 copyuid=dest-0 no-expunge`
  (`copyuid=none` for no COPYUID, `other` for one naming another letter
  or unreadable), then `MOVE-CHECKED folder=INBOX uid=343` with `gone`,
  `there sending-again`, `moved` (the second MOVE's answer showed it),
  `there not-moved`, `refused not-moved`, `unanswered not-moved` or
  `lost not-moved`, and those below for a letter staying in All
  Mail; `expunge` in place of `no-expunge` when an EXPUNGE came with
  the answer and was not taken for the letter's; for the fallback,
  `MOVE-HOLLOW … UID COPY copyuid=dest-0` and
  `MOVE-CHECKED … nothing-marked not-moved`.
- Filed from All Mail in a label, a letter stays in All Mail, so it is
  looked for there by its labels: `UID FETCH n (X-GM-LABELS)` in the same
  hold, and the destination's label on it (`\Inbox`, a system folder's
  by its LIST attribute as `\Starred` for `\Flagged`, a user label's by
  its name), done. Without it, the same MOVE goes once more, a label
  given twice on Gmail being one label and a MOVE out of All Mail taking
  nothing out; its answer showing nothing again and the label not on,
  refused: `MOVE-CHECKED … labelled`, `unlabelled sending-again`,
  `unlabelled not-moved`. Its row stays on the list either way (B-041),
  so a refusal there is the alert alone, and the folder is not counted
  for it. A server without Gmail's labels is not asked:
  `stays-in-folder not-asked`, taken as before.
- The connection dropping, or its path going (B-091), during the NOOP,
  the SEARCH, the FETCH or the second MOVE fails the move as on any
  dropped connection, and the MOVE, having gone, is not sent again on a
  new one: refused as not moved, the row back where it stood, the kept
  copy keeping it, and the log closing `MOVE-CHECKED … lost not-moved`,
  after the `NO-PATH` line where it was the path.
- The same for every Delete and Move from Edit mode and from the reading
  pane, which all go through `IMAPMailRepository.move`: to the Trash, to
  Spam, to a folder, and out of the Trash or Spam.

**Not changed.**

- A normal MOVE: its one command, as before, and nothing in the log.
- Delete inside the Trash is no MOVE: it is `\Deleted` and a UID EXPUNGE
  of the letter (B-062), as it was. Its UID EXPUNGE is rightly answered
  OK with no EXPUNGE when Gmail's Auto-Expunge has taken the letter at
  the STORE, so an answer showing nothing says nothing there.
- Edit mode's rule that the first refusal stops the rest (B-062): a
  letter refused as not moved stops the ones after it, which come back
  unsent with it, as for any refusal. A letter whose second MOVE lands
  stops nothing.
- No new words. "Can't connect to mail server." is what a Delete or Move
  the server would not do has always said.

**What he sees.** A Delete or Move that Gmail answers so and takes at
the second MOVE: the row goes at the tap and stays gone, three more
round trips behind it. One Gmail will not take: the row back where it
stood and "Can't connect to mail server.", as for any Delete the server
refused; the letter is in its folder still, and the next Delete is his.
A Move out of All Mail answered so: the row stays, as ever, and the
letter is in the folder, or, refused, "Can't connect to mail server."
with the letter not filed. Every other Delete and Move as before.

**Tests.** `HollowMoveTests`, twenty-six, over the answer's reading on
Gmail's own strings, and over the shipping repository and client, the
list's own letters, the kept copy and the scripted server, whose
`hollowMoves` answer the next MOVEs as Gmail answered that one, tagged
`OK [COPYUID <validity> <uid> 0] (Success)` and no EXPUNGE, with nothing
moved (`.nothingMoved`) or with the letter moved and the connection not
told until its next NOOP (`.movedUntold`), or `OK Success` with no
COPYUID and nothing moved (`.nothingMovedUnsaid`), whose `hollowCopies`
answer a COPY so, and whose `newsRidesOnMoves` puts on a MOVE's answer
the EXPUNGE of a letter taken out elsewhere (`removeElsewhere`), which
otherwise comes only on a NOOP. Without UIDPLUS it gives no COPYUID.
A MOVE into a folder that holds the letter already, as All Mail holds
every letter, is answered with the UID the letter has there, as Gmail
answers an Archive from the Inbox, so an Archive is pinned at its one
command too.

- *The answer:* Gmail's MOVE done, its EXPUNGE and the tagged COPYUID,
  shows it; the iPad's does not, nor does 2026-09-28's `OK Success`; RFC
  6851's untagged COPYUID is read; the COPYUID alone is enough, the
  EXPUNGE alone only without UIDPLUS, and an EXPUNGE never against a
  COPYUID with a 0 or another letter's, with or without; an EXISTS is
  not. A COPYUID for another letter, with fewer UIDs in the destination,
  `*`, too many digits or unreadable names nothing; ranges either way
  round; a 0 anywhere is a 0; one on an untagged NO is none; of two, the
  one naming the letter. A COPY's answer is read for its COPYUID alone,
  none at all having nothing against it.
- *Once:* the iPad's answer with the letter still there, a Delete: MOVE,
  NOOP, `UID SEARCH UID n`, MOVE, on the one connection, then none in
  the Inbox, one in the Trash, none on the kept Inbox, and the three log
  lines; a Move to a folder from the pane the same, its row staying off.
- *Twice:* from the pane, refused, the alert's words, the row back where
  it stood, the kept copy keeping it, the letter in the Inbox unmarked
  and not in the Trash, two MOVEs and two questions and nothing else;
  the second MOVE refused, with no COPY after it; the SEARCH refused,
  nothing sent again.
- *It did go:* the answer with the letter moved, the NOOP's EXPUNGE, the
  SEARCH finding nothing, done, nothing sent again, one copy in the
  Trash; and the same at the second MOVE.
- *An EXPUNGE not the letter's:* the iPad's answer, and the `OK Success`
  with no COPYUID, each with another letter's EXPUNGE on it: the Inbox
  asked, the MOVE sent again and landing, `copyuid=dest-0 expunge` and
  `copyuid=none expunge` in the log, the row off from the pane. Without
  UIDPLUS, the EXPUNGE with no COPYUID is the answer's word: one MOVE.
- *Lost:* the path going with the hollow answer on its way, the NOOP
  kept off the link: one MOVE on the one connection, none lost, no new
  connection, refused, the row back, kept, the letter in the Inbox, and
  `NO-PATH NOOP not-sent` then `lost not-moved`; the same with the
  socket dropping with the NOOP on the wire, and with the path going
  before the second MOVE.
- *All Mail:* a hollow answer filing a letter in the Inbox: the FETCH of
  its labels, the MOVE again, landing, the row staying, counted in the
  Inbox; the same answer with the letter filed all the same, in Sent
  Mail and in the Inbox: the FETCH only, done; hollow twice: refused,
  the row staying, not counted in the Inbox, the letter in All Mail
  alone; on a server without Gmail's labels, one MOVE, not asked.
- *As before:* a Delete and a Move to a folder, one MOVE each, and a
  Move out of All Mail, whose answer has no EXPUNGE, one MOVE, none
  noted; Delete inside the Trash, the STORE and UID EXPUNGE, the hollow
  MOVE waiting not met.
- *Without MOVE:* COPY, STORE and UID EXPUNGE as before; a hollow COPY,
  nothing marked, no STORE, no EXPUNGE, no second COPY, refused, the
  letter in the Inbox and on the kept Inbox.
- *Edit mode:* three rows deleted, the second sent answered hollow: it
  goes again and lands, the others one MOVE each, every row off, each
  letter once in the Trash. The first sent answered hollow twice, the
  iPad's first: refused, and by the rule above the others unsent, all
  three rows back where they stood, every letter in the Inbox and kept.

Each part undone in the worktree, one at a time, the seventeen run,
counted as failures in tests. The code as it was, a tagged OK taken for
done, 41 in 10, and in the whole suite those 10 alone: nothing else held
it. A hollow OK falling back to the old COPY, `\Deleted` and EXPUNGE, 37
in 10. A 0 among the destinations not seen, 52 in 14. The COPYUID not
read, 2 in 2; the EXPUNGE not read, 2 in 1; the untagged COPYUID not
read, 3 in 3; the source set not asked for the letter, 2 in 2; the
counts not compared, 1 in 1. No NOOP before the SEARCH, 9 in 9, among
them the letter that did go found still there, sent again and refused.
No second MOVE, 23 in 7; the second sent as a COPY, 28 in 7; a second
hollow answer refused unasked, 4 in 3; the second MOVE refused falling
back to the COPY, 2 in 1; the question unanswered taken for gone, 3 in
1. The client not heeding `leavesSource`, 2 in 1; the repository saying
every letter stays, 40 in 9. The COPY's COPYUID not read, 5 in 1, the
letter marked and expunged with no copy anywhere; a COPY with no
COPYUID taken as hollow, 1 in 1. Every MOVE checked, 3 in 2, and in the
whole suite 23 in 21, nineteen of them tests that were there before,
each pinning a Delete's or a Move's commands.

Then, with the EXPUNGE, All Mail and a connection lost looked into, each
part undone again, the twenty-six run. An EXPUNGE taken for the letter's
whatever the COPYUID says, as it was, 13 in 3, among them the hollow
answer with another letter's EXPUNGE on it; an EXPUNGE with no COPYUID
taken from a server with UIDPLUS, 5 in 2. The client taking every server
for one with UIDPLUS, 2 in 1; for one without, 4 in 1. The connection
lost taken for a write not sent, so sent again on a new connection, 13
in 2, and at the second MOVE 7 in 1; taken for done, 7 in 2; its log
line left out, 2 in 2. All Mail not asked, 11 in 3; the label never seen
on the letter, 1 in 1, the MOVE sent again and refused though the letter
was filed; compared without case, 1 in 1; the repository naming a system
folder's label by its folder's name, or not giving the Inbox `\Inbox`, 1
in 1 each; the repository giving no labels, 7 in 4; a server without
Gmail's labels asked all the same, 1 in 1.

The full suite, serially: 1,825 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-21**, a build of master with B-092
(1233252), three panes, on the test account, three letters To A with
`+jane` before the "@", "R6 B-092 one", "two" and "three". Every step of
the TODO check passed, the letters going from the Inbox rather than out
of the Trash, one row ticked in Edit mode, not three; two ticked at once
went the same way in B-042's check that morning. The hollow answer came
once the same morning, in another check, and was taken at the second
MOVE.

- *Deleted in the pane:* "one", `UID MOVE 363 "[Gmail]/Trash"`, an
  EXPUNGE and `OK [COPYUID 2 363 308]` 0.17 s on, and nothing after it
  but the watch's NOOP 11.6 s later. The row gone at 0.3 s and still
  gone 37 s on; Trash held it once, as 308.
- *Moved to All Mail* from the pane's Move sheet: "two", an EXPUNGE and
  `OK [COPYUID 12 364 438]`, 438 being the UID it had in All Mail
  already, as Gmail answers an Archive. The row gone, the letter out of
  the Inbox and in All Mail once.
- *Deleted in Edit mode:* "three", its MOVE answered with an EXPUNGE and
  a COPYUID, then the sweep of the counts, the letter being unread.
- *Out of All Mail:* "two" moved to the Inbox, answered
  `OK [COPYUID 1 438 366]` with no EXPUNGE, the letter staying in All
  Mail: a COPYUID all the same, as on 2026-10-20, so no `MOVE-HOLLOW`
  line and no `X-GM-LABELS` FETCH. Its All Mail row stayed (B-041), and
  the Inbox held it once after a Refresh. Deleted there: one MOVE again.
- *The log:* five MOVEs, each answered OK with a COPYUID naming its
  letter and no 0, in 0.16 to 1.04 s; no `MOVE-HOLLOW` or
  `MOVE-CHECKED` line, no `UID SEARCH UID n`, no COPY and no label
  FETCH.
- *The hollow answer:* a Delete in the pane of a letter in All Mail, at
  04:33 by the iPad's clock, in B-042's check. Its row, just above the
  list, went at the tap and did not come back, with no alert; Trash held
  one copy, as 314, and nothing more was sent for it. The hollow answer
  came 0.36 s after the MOVE, and the second MOVE's answer 0.43 s after
  it went:

```
→ a365 UID MOVE 173 "[Gmail]/Trash"
← a365 OK [COPYUID 2 173 0] (Success)
· MOVE-HOLLOW folder=[Gmail]/All Mail uid=173 copyuid=dest-0 no-expunge
→ a366 NOOP
← a366 OK Success
→ a367 UID SEARCH UID 173
← * SEARCH {1 uids}
← a367 OK SEARCH completed (Success)
· MOVE-CHECKED folder=[Gmail]/All Mail uid=173 there sending-again
→ a368 UID MOVE 173 "[Gmail]/Trash"
← * 36 EXPUNGE
← * 75 EXISTS
← a368 OK [COPYUID 2 173 314] (Success)
· MOVE-CHECKED folder=[Gmail]/All Mail uid=173 moved
```

So the fix did on the iPad what the host tests hold: the hollow answer
read as nothing shown, the folder asked, the MOVE sent once more, and
the letter moved, 1.07 s from the first MOVE, where before it had been a
row gone and a letter left behind. Both hollow answers seen were to a
Delete, a MOVE into the Trash, the first from the Inbox and this one
from All Mail.

**Not covered.**

- Seen on the iPad once, above, and taken at the second MOVE. Not seen
  there, as none can be made to come: a second hollow answer to the
  same letter and its refusal, a hollow answer to a Move out of All
  Mail and its `X-GM-LABELS` FETCH, and a connection lost during the
  check. Each is held by the host tests, the scripted server's answer
  being the iPad's word for word.
- Why Gmail answered so is not known. If it is Gmail not ready to file
  the letter, the second MOVE, a round trip or two later, may meet the
  same; then the row comes back with the alert, and the next Delete is
  his. On the iPad the second MOVE, sent 0.28 s after the hollow
  answer, landed.
- A server without UIDPLUS gives no COPYUID, so an EXPUNGE in its
  MOVE's answer is still taken for the letter's: one for another letter
  riding on an answer with nothing moved would be taken so. Gmail has
  UIDPLUS.
- A hollow answer for a letter filed from All Mail on a server without
  Gmail's labels is not looked into. On Gmail a label is looked for as
  the folder is named; one Gmail named otherwise, none known, would be
  missed, and the move sent again and, answered so again, refused with
  the letter filed all the same.
- The connection lost during the check refuses the move whether or not
  the letter had gone. Gone, its row is back until the next Refresh,
  and a second Delete of it is answered with nothing moved, looked into,
  found gone and done.
- A server other than Gmail that moved a letter, kept it in the source
  as well, and answered with no COPYUID and no EXPUNGE, which RFC 6851
  says it should not, would get a second copy from the second MOVE.
- On a server without MOVE, a hollow COPY's letter may have reached the
  Trash all the same: the COPY is not sent again, but his next Delete's
  would put a second copy there.

## B-093 — FIXED 2026-10-21, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. A Delete in the reading pane, the letter's row just above the top of the list, moved every row in view up by one

**What he saw.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-21, in B-042's check of
paging upward, and again when the check was made a second time on a fresh
launch. All Mail after Go to Date, three panes. A letter open in the
reading pane, the list scrolled slowly up until the letter's row was just
above the top of the list, hidden under the search field, with the row
above it under the status and navigation bars. Delete in the pane: in the
first shot after the tap, at 0.22 s, every row in view had moved up by
exactly one row, the top row he could see had gone up out of sight, and it
stayed so. The server side was right, one `UID MOVE` and no list fetch.

Not by design. A row binned from the reading pane above the top of the
pane is not to shift the rows he is looking at (B-042).

**What it was.** The place the list holds while its rows are drawn again.
The pane's Delete takes the letter's row off at the tap (`PaneActions.start`,
`ListLetters.take`), and the list draws its rows again keeping his place
(`regroup`, `ListPlace`): the rows he can see are taken first, by their
letters and how far down the pane each sits, and the first of them still
listed is put back where it was. "The rows he can see" were the table's
visible rows, which are every row in its bounds. The table runs on under
the status and navigation bars, and the search band is pinned over the
next 43 points, so one or two of those rows were under them. The first,
the row under the status bar, was the row held; the letter's row, under the
band, went from between it and the rows he could see, and they closed up
under it by one row. Had the first row he could see been held, nothing in
view would have moved. With the letter's row in view, as in Edit mode's
Delete the same day, the row held was above it and nothing he could see
moved, which is why it had not been seen.

The same row was held by every move that keeps his place: a page of newer
mail put on above after a date jump, where a newer letter in the
conversation of the row under the band takes that row up the list; a Move
the server refused, its row put back above the list; a search's Cancel,
the folder coming back by the row under the bar.

**Changed.**

- The rows he can see are the ones with a point or more of them between
  the bars, below the search band (`ListPlace.inSight`), by the sums
  VoiceOver's rows go by (`TableSight`, B-079): the table's offset, its
  height, its adjusted insets and the band's height, which the table hands
  over as `sight` (it was `voiceOverSight`, private to VoiceOver). The
  first of them still listed is held. A row taken out above it, under the
  bars and the band, closes out of sight: the rows above it come down one
  row, still under the bars, and every row in view stays where it was.
- Their offsets are still from the top of the table's bounds, so the list
  is put back as before.
- The same for every move that keeps his place, which all take it in
  `place()`: the regroup after a Delete or a Move from the pane or Edit
  mode, a Mark, a Flag, a page above or below, the grouping switch, a Save
  in Settings and a Move put back; a search's Cancel, by the place taken as
  its results replaced the folder; the newest page fetched afresh after an
  edit of his own; and the fresh page over the kept one (D-016).
- With no row in sight, a pane too short for one below the band, every row
  on screen is taken, as before.
- When the row taken out is the first he can see, the rows below close up
  into its place, as in Mail. The row on screen just above it, under the
  bars or the band, is taken with the rows he can see (`ListPlace.above`,
  `justAbove`), and it is the row held (`closingUp`): it stays where it
  was, out of sight, and the list is not scrolled. The first change of
  this entry held the next row he could see instead, as `landing`'s rule
  had it: the rows below stayed, and the row above came down into the gap.
  That was with less than a point of the row above in sight; with a point
  or more, that row was the first he could see and was held, and the rows
  below closed up. Which way it closed turned on a point of the row
  above. It closes up now whatever of the row above shows. It still turns
  on a point, of the letter's own row: with less than a point of it below
  the search field, it is the row just above the first he can see, and
  closes out of sight, nothing in view moving; with a point or more, it is
  the first he can see, the row above it is held, and the rows below close
  up into it, every row in view a row up, as in Mail.
- With no row on screen above it, the list's first row, or with that row
  taken out too, as Edit mode's Delete of several rows can take it, the
  first of the rows he could see as they stand now goes where the first
  was, and again the list is not scrolled. The list's first row taken out
  a little way down, most of it under the search field, used to put the
  list back at its top.
- The same when the first row he can see goes down the list: a
  conversation whose newest letter is taken out, its next letter further
  down. One whose next letter is next on the list keeps its row where it
  was, headed by that letter, and nothing moves.
- The same for every move that keeps his place: Edit mode's Delete or Move
  of several rows at once, the rows below closing up into the first one's
  place; a search's Cancel, the top row he could see deleted while the
  results showed; the newest page fetched afresh without it. One edge of
  that last: with the newest page ending at the row above the first he
  could see, that row is held and the list goes to the end of the page,
  its last row above the toolbar, where it used to go to the top
  (`ListPlaces.refetched` says so).
- A row put back, its Delete or Move refused, offline or by the server
  (B-062, B-092), with the list as the tap left it: back where it stood,
  the rows below it down a row, every row as before the tap. The place
  from before the tap is kept (`TakenRows`), told which row went and which
  came back by the letters (`ListChange`), and the row is put back by it
  (`ListPlaces.Move.putBack`, `regroup(for:)`). Edit mode's Delete or Move
  keeps one place for every row it took, from before the first, until the
  last is back. With the close-up alone, the top row he could see went
  back in above the rows that had closed up into its place, out of sight
  under the search field: the reading pane emptied at the tap, the alert
  up, offline "Can't connect to mail server.", no letter in sight, and
  every row in view one up from where it had been. By the screen alone
  that row cannot be told from one that was out of sight above the list
  when it went, which is to stay there; the place from before the tap
  tells them apart. Once what he sees has moved since the tap, the list
  scrolled or a row in view joined by newer mail, the rows he can see
  then are held, as before, and the place is dropped. A page put on above
  meanwhile moves nothing in view, and the row still goes back where it
  was.

**Not changed.**

- A Delete of a row in view below the top one: the rows above it stay and
  the rows below close up, as before.
- At the top of the list, a Delete of the top row: the list stays at the
  top and the rows below close up, as before.
- Otherwise which row is put back is still `ListPlace.landing`'s rule:
  the first row he could see still headed by the same letter, else the
  next, else one holding any of its letters. A row newer mail has joined,
  on a page put on above, has gone up the list and is passed over, as
  before (list-8): taken from the top row he can see, the next row he
  could see stays where it was and the row above comes down into the
  place. The grouping switch merging the top row into another the same.

**What he sees.** A Delete or a Move from the pane, the letter's row out of
sight just above the list: nothing in view moves. A row put back above the
list, a page of newer mail put on above it, a search cancelled: the rows
he could see stay where they were. A Delete or a Move of the top row he
