## B-094 — RECORDED 2026-10-21, found on the iPad, not changed. Go to Date from a list at its top fetches the page above as the day lands

**What was seen.** Nothing on screen; the connection log shows it. Seen on
the test iPad on 2026-10-21, in B-042's check of paging upward, three
times, and again when the check was made a second time on a fresh launch.
All Mail just opened, at its top, Go to Date, Current Mailbox, 5 Oct, Go,
and nothing touched after. The FETCH of the page above went out 0.14 s
after the window's `UID FETCH`, with no scroll; the first slow scroll up
then had nothing left to bring. The same from the Inbox with All Mailboxes,
to 4 Oct: the page above 0.45 s after Go. And from the Inbox just opened,
to 5 Oct: the window's FETCH and the page above's 0.17 s apart. On the
fresh launch, All Mail opened at its top, Go to 5 Oct: the window's FETCH
was answered, and 44 ms later the FETCH of the page above went out, before
the window's first preview fetch, which `show(_ window:)` starts on its
last line. Each time the day's letter was the top row, and the line said
"Showing October 5" ("Showing October 4" for the All Mailboxes jump):
nothing moved. Go to the same day from part-way down the list, twice and
once more on the fresh launch, fetched the window and its previews only;
the first two times the page above came with the slow scroll up to it,
within a second of the drag that brought it.

Not by design. The page above a day waits for him to move the list up to
it: the lead above (`willDisplay`, ten rows of a page of fifty) is the same
share of a page as the letters the jump keeps above the day, so the
landing is inside it, not at its edge.

**What it is.** Two ways, one seen.

- *Laid out where the old list was.* `show(_ window:)` reloads the table
  and lays it out (`layoutIfNeeded`) before it scrolls to the day, so that
  the scroll is worked out on the new rows. That layout is at the offset
  the old list had. From a list at its top it puts the window's first rows
  on screen, rows 0 to 8, and `willDisplay` starts the page above for any
  of the first ten. From part-way down, the rows laid out there are past
  the first ten, which is why nothing was fetched then. The same layout
  could start the page below, with the old offset near the end of the new
  window; not seen.
- *In a deep folder, the rows above the day under the bars.* Not seen: in
  the test account's All Mail the older side is short, the window kept 21
  newer letters above the day, and it landed at row 20. With a page of
  older mail below it, the jump keeps ten newer letters above the day
  (`PageWindow.newerRowsAboveAnchor`), so it lands at row 10, or higher
  when two of the ten share a conversation, or when the landing moves up
  past letters of the evening before, west of Greenwich (B-058). The table
  runs on under its bars (B-093), so the one or two rows above the day are
  on screen under the bars and the search band as it lands, and they are
  among the first ten: the page above starts as the day lands, wherever
  the list had been. *Since B-117 a jump's window has the page above it
  in it too, sixty letters above the day, so it lands at row 60, and
  this way no longer starts a page; the first way still does, the page
  above the one in the window. With those letters sharing conversations
  it can land higher, and above row 12 this way starts that page too.*

**What it costs.** One envelope FETCH of a page, up to fifty letters, and
its previews, as the day lands, on the connection the day's own previews
wait behind: the first of them went out 80 ms after it on the fresh
launch. Nothing was seen to move on screen, then or later, and nothing
was taken to: the page goes on above the day, out of sight, the rows he
can see held where they are (B-042). *Wrong with Organize by Thread on,
seen on the iPad on 2026-10-23 (B-117): a reply on that page to the
letter the jump landed on joined its row and took it up the list, out of
sight, 0.14 s after it was drawn, and the day's next letter came down
into its place. Since B-117 the window has that page in it, fetched in
its one FETCH, and the row the jump landed on is held where it is, by its
letter, as the pages above come, until he moves the list; the page asked
for as the day lands is the one above it, fifty letters more, and its
previews.* And the check that the page above comes as he scrolls up to it
cannot be made from such a landing; TODO's B-042 check of paging upward
says so.

**Why it is left.** A fix has to keep the page above loading whenever he
scrolls up to it, wherever the day lands, at row 20 or at row 1, and from
any list. The one tried had to hold off paging while the rows were laid
out, then look at the rows on screen once, keep the row the day landed on
until the page above came or the list was fetched afresh, and look at the
edge again at every move of the list, since at a day landed at row 1 or 2
every row above it is on screen already and none comes on screen as he
moves up to it. It grew a tracker of the day's row and a hook on the list's
scrolling, each with its own ways to go wrong: a row taken out above the
day, or the grouping switched, left the day's row a row off. A page above
that never came, and the list stopped at the top of a day with newer mail
above it, would be worse than one fetched a second early. For an app
nobody can update, it is left as it is.

## B-095 — FIXED 2026-10-21, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. A finger held on a conversation's line never lit it, and began WebKit's selection of a word in it, and its Copy menu

**What he saw.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-21, in B-055's check of a
conversation's lines, and again when the check was made a second time on a
fresh launch, with a tap on a link to show the shots could catch a
highlight. A conversation of three letters, all read, each closed to its
line. One finger held still on a closed line for a second: the line did not
lighten in any frame, and at about 0.6 to 0.7 s WebKit began to select a
word in it, the loupe and its handles, and at about 1.4 s showed its Copy,
Look Up, Translate, Search Web and Share menu. A tap off it put the menu
away, and nothing else changed. A plain tap opened the line, and closed it,
as it should, with no lightening in any frame either. The link in the
control darkened under the finger at 0.13 s: WebKit's own tap highlight,
caught at the same pace.

Not by design. A line is lit under the finger while he presses it, and it
is not text: Mail's message headers in a conversation are not text to
select. His taps are slow.

**What it was.** Two things.

- *No light.* The line's only press feedback was WebKit's tap highlight,
  `-webkit-tap-highlight-color`. WebKit on the iPad paints it for a link, a
  label, a form control and the like, and for anything else only when it
  is no wider and no taller than 30% of the page in view
  (`_showTapHighlight` in `WKContentViewInteraction.mm`, `WebPageIOS.mm`,
  WebKit 7615.2.9.11.4, the iPadOS 16.5 one). A line is a `<div>` with a
  click listener, as wide as the pane, so its highlight was asked for and
  dropped, on a tap and on a hold. It had never lit: the `<div onclick>`
  before B-055 was the same size, and the B-055 check's "greys under the
  finger as it did" was wrong.
- *A selection.* Nothing made the line unselectable, so a still finger
  became WebKit's long press for text: the loupe, a word, the edit menu.

**Changed.**

- A line, and everything in it, is not text to select and has no callout
  (`-webkit-user-select: none`, `-webkit-touch-callout: none`): the stack's
  own lines only, the letters' bodies selectable as before. WebKit's tap
  highlight on a line is off. The two rules and the light below are
  `!important`, as the pictures' width in a body already is: a sender's
  own style sheet applies to the whole stack, and an important rule of
  its own on `*` or `div`, an email's reset, would beat them otherwise.
  Among important rules the line's selectors outrank such a one.
- The stack's script lights the line itself, a class with the same faint
  white, 8%, from the touch until the finger lifts. The light goes at the
  lift, at a touch WebKit cancels, a finger moved more than 10 px, a second
  finger, a scroll of the page, and at 1.2 s, when lifting would no longer
  open it.
- The lift is the tap, the script's: one finger, still to 10 px, lifted
  within 1.2 s, the line where it was under it, opens or closes the letter
  and tells the pane, as a tap did. WebKit's own tap on the line is
  stopped, by `preventDefault` on the touchend, which WebKit's tap waits
  for (`_touchEndDeferringGestureRecognizerForSyntheticTapGestures`); the
  listener is not passive, so WebKit waits on it
  (`WebPageProxy::handlePreventableTouchEvent`).
- Whether WebKit clicks on its own at the lift of a touch held a second,
  the line no longer selectable, is not in its source. The long press that
  clicks at its lift, the highlight long press, is off in this web view:
  WebKit turns it off when it uses context menus with link previews on
  (`_updateLongPressAndHighlightLongPressGestures`), which is so here, as
  a link held in B-055's check showed, with its context menu. A click would
  come from WebKit's tap recogniser, which is UIKit's, and how long UIKit
  lets a tap be held is not in WebKit. So nothing counts on it: the script
  acts at the lift and stops WebKit's tap.
- If WebKit clicked anyway, the tap would open and close the letter at
  once. So after a touch the script took, one click is let pass: the
  first click on a line, if it is on that touch's line, within a second of
  the lift, and before another touch lands. The first click on any line
  ends it, and so does the next touch. A click on another line, or on the
  same one after the next touch, toggles as it did.
- A selection he made in a letter's body, with a finger held on a word
  there, goes at a tap on a line, with its Copy menu, as it went at
  WebKit's tap: the `preventDefault` that stops WebKit's tap stops its
  clearing too, so the script clears it before it toggles the letter.
- Past 1.2 s, the light gone, the lift does nothing, and WebKit's tap is
  stopped the same way. A line that moved from under the still finger,
  a letter above it grown, the same: nothing.
- A finger that moves, a scroll, does nothing, and nothing is stopped:
  WebKit takes no tap after a scroll. A touch that lands within 0.2 s of a
  scroll, on a stack still moving from a flick, only stops it, as WebKit
  takes no tap then: no light, and WebKit decides. The script's own
  scroll, keeping his place as a letter above him grows, is told from his
  (`bmMine`) and ends nothing. In each of these WebKit's tap is what it
  was before, the click let pass above included: a touch the script left
  to WebKit is never the one whose click is let pass.
- As first written, before the iPad saw it, the click let pass was tied to
  the clock alone: the first click on any line within a second of a touch
  the script took. Each touch left to WebKit in that second lost its tap:
  a line pressed slowly while the one tapped before it opened, its body
  in and the header grown, the pane's scroll to keep his place cutting
  the press, never opened at the lift. Run in a DOM, a touch near a
  scroll, a finger drifted 15 px, a press cut by a scroll, and a click
  after a hold past the bound each lost their click. Now it is the
  touch's line's, until the next touch.
- The touches are heard on the window, as the hold's are, not on the
  lines. VoiceOver's activation sends an element a touch in place of its
  click when it or a node above it has a touch listener
  (`AccessibilityObject::press`, `hasTouchEventListener`, the same WebKit),
  and the window is not a node: VoiceOver's activation of a line is the
  click it was, as is a pointer's.
- Lines put in at the bottom later (`bmAppend`) are lit and tapped the
  same: a line is one `bmWire` wired. A line drawn by a letter's own markup
  is neither.

**Not changed.**

- A quick tap opens and closes a line as before, now by the script at the
  lift rather than by WebKit's click.
- VoiceOver's activation of a line, the click.
- A letter's text, selectable; a held link's menu and preview, WebKit's
  own.
- How a line looks unpressed, and what it holds.

**What he sees.** A finger on a closed line: it lightens at once, and stays
light while he holds it still. Lifted within about a second, the letter
opens, as at a quick tap; on an open letter's line, it closes. No word is
selected and no menu comes, however long he holds it. A word he selected
in a letter, and its menu, go when he taps a line, as they did. Held past
about 1.2 s, the light goes, and lifting does nothing. A finger that
scrolls the stack: the line lights for the moment before the stack moves,
goes as it moves, and nothing opens.

**Tests.** In `LinePressTests`, nine, reading the document and the script
as the stack's other tests do: a line not text to select and without a
callout, important, and nothing else in the document so, WebKit's
highlight off; the light, its class, important, and what puts it out; the
tap, its bound, its 10 px, its `preventDefault` in a touchend listener
that is not passive; the click let pass, the touch's line's, within the
second, ended by the first click on a line and by the next touch; the
selection cleared at the tap and only there; a touch on a scrolling page
and a second finger; the script's own scroll; the touches on the window
alone, and the click alone on a line; lines put in later, and a letter's
own not. One older test changed with it:
`testTheScriptKeepsHisPlaceAsLettersAboveHimGrow` reads `bmKeep` with its
new line.

Each part undone in the worktree, one at a time, the tests run, counted as
failures in tests. No selection rule, 3 in 1. The rule on the line and not
what is in it, 1 in 1; on every element, 1 in 1. No callout rule, 2 in 1.
WebKit's highlight as it was, 2 in 1. No lit class, 1 in 1. The touch not
lighting it, 1 in 1. A scroll not putting it out, 1 in 1; a cancel not,
2 in 2. The light not out at the bound, 1 in 1. The touchend passive, 1 in
1. No `preventDefault`, 2 in 1. No bound, 1 in 1; a bound of 3 s, 1
in 1. The line's place not checked, 1 in 1. A moved finger a tap, 1 in 1.
The touches heard on the line, 3 in 1; on the document, 3 in 2. No lines
known, 2 in 1; any `.bm-head` pressed, a letter's own among them, 1 in 1.
A touch on a scrolling page a press, 1 in 1; a second finger, 1 in 1. The
script's own scroll ending a press, 2 in 2. The click let pass: tied to the
clock alone, any line's, as first written, 1 in 1; not ended by a click on
another line, 1 in 1; not ended by the next touch, 3 in 2; with no second,
1 in 1; for a minute, 2 in 2; none let pass, 1 in 1; none set at the lift,
3 in 2; the first version's number, 2 in 2. No selection cleared, 3 in 2;
cleared at every lift the script takes, 1 in 1. Each of the four
`!important`s taken off, 1 in 1 each.

Checked outside the suite and not kept: the stack's script run in a DOM
(jsdom) on a stack of three letters, the touches and clicks made by hand,
27 cases: taps of 0.1 and 1 s, lit while held, each opening once, WebKit's
tap stopped and a click after it let pass; a hold of 1.5 s, lit to 1.2 s,
nothing at the lift; a moved finger, a scroll, a touch on a stack still
scrolling, a second finger and a cancel, nothing and nothing stopped; a
click alone, as VoiceOver's, toggling; a line put in later; a letter's own
line; a line moved under the finger; two quick taps, open and closed; and
the script's own scroll during a hold, the tap still taken. Then 20 more.
Within a second of a tap the script took: a touch near a scroll, a finger
drifted 15 px, on another line and on the same one, and a press cut by a
scroll, each left to WebKit and its click toggling; a click on the same
line at once swallowed, and after the second toggling; a click on another
line, then on the first, both toggling; two taps and a click after them,
open and closed. A click on another line within a second of a hold past
the bound, toggling. The light out after the bound with no lift, and the
next touch lit. A word selected in a body, gone at a tap on a line and
kept for a moved finger. All 47 pass; the first version failed 8 of them.

The full suite, serially: 1,856 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The release
build for the iPad links.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-21**, a build of the `line-press`
worktree (a6a6c7c), master with B-092, B-093 and B-095, three panes, on

Seen in passing, as in B-055's check: a header that gains a Cc line at a
tap leaves the stack's first line half under it until the stack is
scrolled.

**Not covered.**

- Seen on the iPad, above, but for two things. VoiceOver's activation of
  a line, the click, was not tried on this build. A finger held still and
  then dragged, in one touch, was not made, a touch made here moving at
  one pace from touch to lift; a drag, a slow drift and a touch on a
  moving stack stood in, each lit only while still and opening nothing.
- The host has no WebKit. That WebKit stops its tap at the `preventDefault`
  and sends no click after it is from its source, not seen: on the iPad
  each tap the script took, lifted within the bound, opened or closed its
  letter once, as it does either way, the click let pass covering one
  that comes. That the selection's handles and its menu go when the
  script clears it was seen there: WebKit tells UIKit's text interaction
  that the selection changed (`_updateChangedSelection`,
  `selectionChanged`), and the handles were gone by 0.20 s, the menu by

  the finger on whatever comes under it. On the iPad that was the
  signature's logo, a link, and WebKit put up its menu and preview at
  about 1 s; nothing opened, and a tap off the menu put it away.

  while WebKit lays out a large one waits as long. Not measured.

  WebKit's tap did (`_singleTapRecognized`). Nothing in the pane is known
  to need it, but a keyboard up for the list's search field may stay up
  when he taps a line, where WebKit's tap would have taken it away. Not

  moves; a row of UIKit's in a scroll view waits a moment before it lights.

  longer is not known. Past it the light goes while the finger is still

  WebKit's page hands the script the touch, so a busy page can stretch a
  tap of about a second past it, the margin 0.2 s. The bound stays: a
  finger resting on the glass must not open a letter at its lift.

## B-096 — RECORDED 2026-10-21, found on the iPad, not changed. A switch of the panes in the middle of a bounce ends the bounce

**What was seen.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-21, in B-066's check,
step 3, and again on a fresh launch with the Layout button off and on,
each run against the same gesture made with no tap. Three panes, the
Inbox at its top, pulled down past its top and let go, and the view button
tapped as it sprang back: the switch was made at once, with
`pane motion: bouncing; switched at once`, as built. In the first frame in
two panes the list was almost at its rest, 26 to 45 pt nearer it than the
bounce left alone; the last 6 to 10 pt then sprang back, first a point or
two away from the rest. Important flicked past its bottom, the same: 66 to
72 pt of the bounce gone in the one frame. In two panes, "< Mailboxes" and
the Inbox tapped at once after a pull, a change with no new width for the
list: the bounce went on as it would have.

Not by design. A switch made at once leaves the bounce to finish (B-066),
and the list keeps its place across a switch.

**What it is.** The switch made at once only looks at the bouncing list. It
then lays out the new arrangement in the same moment, and the list's column
goes from 330 to 375 pt wide. UIKit's scroll view, given a new size while
past its end, takes its offset almost to the end at once and springs back
only the last few points. With no new size the bounce is kept: the resize
is what ends it.

**What it costs.** A fraction of a second of a bounce. The list comes to
rest some 30 to 70 pt sooner, in the frame the arrangement changes, when
everything on the screen moves at once anyway, then springs the last few
points with no jump. The rows end where they would have, and nothing is
fetched or lost.

**Why it is left.** The fix is the app's own spring-back across the resize:
the overshoot read before the new layout, put back after it, and run down
to rest frame by frame by the app in place of UIKit, given up the moment
his finger takes the list. That is new scroll physics for a fraction of a
second, at a switch already made at once, and not worth it in an app that
is never updated. Left as it is.

## B-097 — RECORDED 2026-10-21, found on the iPad, not changed. A file of a letter too large to fetch whole is fetched again each time it is opened

**What was seen.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-21, in B-043's check,
the 5 MB PDF, and again on a fresh launch. A letter of 6.1 MB on the
server, a PDF of 4.4 MB shared from Files, so over the 5 MB above which a
letter is opened in parts (B-054). Its file's row tapped:
`UID FETCH n (UID BODY.PEEK[2])`, the whole part, 6 MB as it is on the
wire, and Quick Look 2.6 s after the tap. Done, and the row tapped again:
the same FETCH and the same 6 MB, and Quick Look 2.3 s on, 2.0 s on the
fresh launch. A letter of 93 KB, fetched whole, with a PDF: tapped twice,
nothing fetched either time.

Not by design. A file of a letter fetched whole opens again from what the
app holds, and nothing in B-054 has a file of a letter opened in parts
fetched again at every tap.

**What it is.** A file is served without the wire only from the last letter
fetched whole. A letter opened in parts keeps its structure and none of its
files, so every tap on one of its files fetches the part again. The copy
made for Quick Look at the first tap is still on the iPad at the second, as
the pane keeps the last file opened until the next is written (B-063), but
nothing says which letter and part it is, so it is not used.

**What it costs.** The file again at every open after the first: its
megabytes over the connection, and about 2 s, much as the first open took.
Only for letters over 5 MB; a file of a letter fetched whole opens from
what the app holds.

**Why it is left.** Only a file of a letter over 5 MB is fetched again, and
the second open costs what the first did. A kept copy that ever answered
for another letter or part would show him the wrong file, which is worse
than a second wait. For an app that is never updated, it is left as it is.

## B-098 — RECORDED 2026-10-21, found on the iPad, not changed. A letter tapped shows its header over the previous letter's body for one frame

**What was seen.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-21, in B-041's check of
the reading pane at the tap, from screen recordings at 60 frames a second,
stepped through frame by frame. The new letter's header, its sender,
subject and date, came in the frame the selection moved, and under it, for
one frame, some 17 ms, was the previous letter's body, moved down with the
new header; then "Loading…". It was so in 5 taps of 7. For the first letter
after a launch, two frames of an empty pane, every time. The same first
frame showed in passing in two more checks that day.

Not by design. The TODO's check has the previous letter never on screen
beside the new selection, not even for a frame (B-041).

**What it is.** The header is UIKit's and goes out with the selection.
"Loading…" is a page the web view paints in WebKit's own process a frame or
two later; until then it shows what it painted last, or nothing before its
first letter.

**What it costs.** One frame, some 17 ms, of the letter he has left under
the new one's header, or two of an empty pane after a launch. Between
"Loading…" and the letter no white or blank frame came.

**Why it is left.** The fix is a cover over the web view from the tap, in
the pane's own colour, lifted when WebKit has painted "Loading…". If it
ever failed to lift, a letter would stay hidden under it, which is worse
than one frame of the letter before. For a frame, it is left as it is.

## B-099 — RECORDED 2026-10-21, found on the iPad, not changed. A letter that comes while a search shows goes on at the check after Cancel, up to some 32 s later

**What was seen.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-21, in B-049's check,
under a search. A letter sent to the account itself while a search showed
over the Inbox, and Cancel tapped as one of the watch's checks began: the
letter went on the list 32.2 s after Cancel, and 31.7 s at a second try.
While the search showed, the Inbox's count went up at the check, as built.

Not by design. The TODO's check has it at the top within half a minute of
Cancel (B-049).

**What it is.** Cancel sends the Inbox's SELECT, whose answer has the new
EXISTS, but starts no check, so what came during the search waits for the
next timed one: a whole interval, and the sleep's lateness, at worst.

**What it costs.** A letter that came while he searched is on the list up
to some 32 s after Cancel, the Inbox back and its count already up
meanwhile. Nothing is lost.

**Why it is left.** After Cancel the letter waits for the next check as
any new letter does, an interval and the sleep's lateness at worst, and
the Inbox's count is up meanwhile. A check started at Cancel would be a
second way into the watch, beside its timer, in an app nobody can update.
It is left as it is.

## B-100 — BUILT 2026-10-22, seen on the iPad 2026-10-22. Send made no sound; Mail's swoosh plays as the sheet goes, for a letter put in the Outbox too

**What Mail does.** Mail's composer plays its sent sound as its sheet
goes. Read from iOS 18.6's MessageUI in the simulator's runtime on the
Mac, with high confidence: `-[MFMailComposeController viewDidDisappear:]`
calls `+[MFSoundController playSentMailSound]` when the sheet's result is
1, 'sent', and it has no Send Later date, and that plays ToneLibrary's
alert type 6, the tone chosen at Settings, Sounds, Sent Mail. So it plays
as the sheet goes, without waiting for the server, not for Send Later, and
not when the Outbox sends a letter later. Apple's words for 'sent' are
"The email message was queued in the user's outbox. It is ready to send
the next time the user connects to email." (`MFMailComposeResult.sent`,
and the MessageUI header's comment on `MFMailComposeResultSent`). A Send
online and a Send offline are one result, so a letter put in Mail's
Outbox plays it too: medium-high confidence, read from the code and the
documentation, not tried with Mail on a device offline. The tone is
Settings, Sounds, Sent Mail, Swoosh by default, and it can be None
(Apple's iPad guide, "Change or turn off sounds"): high confidence. Mail's
share sheet is the same composer, so a shared page plays it too: inferred,
medium.

The call is public: `AudioServicesPlaySystemSound`. The id is not. Apple's
page says to get a sound from `AudioServicesCreateSystemSoundID`, and
documents no number. 1001 is mail-sent.caf in iOS 18.6's AudioToolbox,
whose built-in table runs new-mail.caf, mail-sent.caf at 1000, 1001, and
the file is in the runtime; lists of the system sounds have given the same
since iPhone OS 2. Medium-high, and unverified until the iPad's checks 1
and 9. Apple says such a sound plays "at the current system audio volume,
with no programmatic volume control available"; nothing of Apple's says
how it meets Silent mode, the Ringer and Alerts volume, headphones or
Bluetooth, which checks 2 and 10 are for. That it needs no entitlement and
plays from an extension is inferred, until check 5.

**What it was.** Nothing in the app made a sound. Send closed the sheet at
Gmail's 250, or with the Outbox's notice, in silence, from the composer
and from the share sheet.

**Changed.**

1. *The hook.* `ComposeActions` takes `sent`, beside `queued`, and calls it
   once per letter, just before it tells the sheet to close, on the two
   ways Send closes it: after `sendLetter` has returned, Gmail's 250,
   `sent` then `dismiss`; after `Outbox.Waiting`, `sent`, then `queued`,
   then `dismiss`. Never on a refusal, which keeps the sheet, nor for
   Cancel, Save Draft, Delete Draft, an autosave, his leaving the app, a
   sheet swiped away, or a second tap, which sends nothing. The composer's
   `ComposeActions(letter:…)` hands it through. `ShareSheet` takes the
   same and hands it to its `ComposeActions`, so it is called just before
   `finish`, never before `cancel`, and never for a send refused, an
   offline one included: the share sheet has no Outbox.
2. *The call.* `AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(ComposeViewController.
   sentMailSound)`, from the composer's `ComposeActions` and the share
   sheet's `ShareSheet`. `sentMailSound` is 1001, named once, in
   `ComposeViewController`, its comment saying it is mail-sent.caf in
   AudioToolbox's built-in table and undocumented. `import AudioToolbox`
   is in those two files alone, `UI/ComposeViewController.swift` and
   `Share/ShareViewController.swift`, each inside its `canImport(UIKit)`
   guard; nothing that builds on this host has it.
3. *The link.* AudioToolbox came in by the module's own autolink, and no
   linker setting was added. In the release build both executables load
   `/System/Library/Frameworks/AudioToolbox.framework/AudioToolbox`, the
   one load command new against master, and each binds
   `_AudioServicesPlaySystemSound` from it.

**Not changed.** No sound when a later pass sends a letter from the
Outbox, as in Mail. No setting. A refusal is silent, the sheet staying
with the alert, as before. The Outbox's notice says what it said. The
sound starts as the sheet is told to close; Mail's starts from the sheet's
`viewDidDisappear:`, once it has gone, a few tenths of a second later. In
the share sheet that later moment comes after the share has completed,
when the extension may already be ended, so both sheets play it at the
start of the close.

**What he sees.** One swoosh as the sheet closes after Send, from the
composer and from the share sheet. With Airplane Mode on, the swoosh and
the Outbox's notice, and nothing more when the letter goes later. None in
Silent mode (once seen). Nothing when Gmail refuses a letter: the sheet
stays with the alert, as before. No new words.

**Tests.** `ComposeActionsTests`, six new, the sound and the send's return
written into the log. A send held on its way, no sound; let go, the 250,
the letter taken off the iPad, the sound, then the sheet told to close,
then Drafts tidied, the sound once and nothing at a tap after.
`Outbox.Waiting`: the sound, then the notice, then the close, once. A
refusal for the letter's size and one for any other reason: silent, the
sheet put back each time; then a Send that goes, one sound. Save Draft,
Delete Draft, an autosave, leaving the app, Cancel on a letter as it
opened and a swipe: no sound, each read on its own, nor at a Send after
them. Two quick taps and a third on the wire: one sound. A Send waiting
for a photo: no sound while the photo is awaited or while the letter
goes, then the sound once it has gone. `ShareSheetTests`, two new, over
the scripted submission server: nothing while the letter's 250 is held,
then the sound just before the share ends, once, however many taps; a
letter Gmail refuses as too big and one sent with no connection, no sound
and the sheet staying, and Cancel after them and before any Send, no
sound. `OutboxTests`, one new, through the composer's own wiring over the
scripted servers: a letter put in the Outbox, one sound as the sheet
closes with the notice, none when a later pass sends it, and one for a
letter that goes at Send; and `testALettersOwnFailureKeepsTheSheet` now
says its three refusals, a recipient, a letter too big and a password,
play nothing. `SentSoundTests`, three, read from the source: AudioToolbox
imported by the two sheets' files alone, once each and inside the guard,
nothing under `Mail/` and not `ShareSheet.swift`; one call in each, of the
sound by its name, 1001 named once, `SystemSoundID` in the composer alone,
and no alert sound anywhere; and each sheet handing the call to its own
hook.

Each part undone in the worktree, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. The sound moved before
`sendLetter` returns: 19 in 7. Played on a refusal too: 12 in 3. Left off
the Outbox's close: 6 in 2. Played after the sheet is told to close: 4 in
4. In the Outbox, after the notice: 1 in 1. Played at a second tap: 11 in
5. Played at Save Draft: 1 in 1; at Delete Draft: 4 in 2, the share
sheet's Cancel among them; at an autosave: 3 in 1; as he leaves the app:
2 in 1; at Cancel on a letter as it opened: 1 in 1; at a swipe: 1 in 1.
Not handed through by the composer's `ComposeActions(letter:…)`: 3 in 1.
Not handed on by `ShareSheet`: 2 in 1. And, read from the source: the
composer not handing the sound to its hook, 2 in 2; the share sheet
calling 1001 by its number, 3 in 2; `ShareSheet.swift` importing
AudioToolbox behind a guard of its own, 3 in 1; the alert sound in place
of the system sound, 3 in 2. Nothing else failed in any run. Played at
Save Draft first passed: the test read the count after setting it back
for the next way. It reads it after each way now, and the six ways it
covers were each undone again with it as it is.

The full suite, serially: 1,868 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links. `llvm-objdump --macho --dylibs-used`,
`otool -L`'s listing (no `llvm-otool` on this host), on the release
build's BlackmailApp, which is the app's `Blackmail`, and BlackmailShare,
the extension's executable, each:
`/System/Library/Frameworks/AudioToolbox.framework/AudioToolbox
(compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 1000.0.0)`.

**Not covered.**

- A tone other than Swoosh, or None. The app cannot read his choice and
  plays Swoosh whatever it is. None drops this batch (D-019).
- 1001 itself: seen on the iPad (below); on the simulator, check 9, not.
- Which volume governs the sound, the media volume included, and
  headphones and Bluetooth (checks 2 and 10): a person's ear. On the iPad
  the log gave each swoosh the system sounds' volume, 1.0, with the media
  volume at nought, but the level after the iPad's processing read
  silence for every swoosh, as it did for the music. Silent Mode silences
  it, seen there.
- The extension's sound cut short as the share completes: not, seen on
  the iPad, played its whole length.
- A letter whose 250 comes after he has left the app or locked the iPad,
  its sheet still up behind: the sound is asked for then, from the
  background, which Mail's sheet, gone at the tap, never does. iOS played
  it on the locked test iPad (check 12, below).
- The two sheets' wiring is read from the source on the host, not run.
  The hook under it runs.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-22**, iPadOS 16.5.1, a build of
`featA-int` (7eefcb4), three panes, the test account; letters To A with
`+jane` before the "@", subjects beginning "R6 B-100". The sound was read
from the iPad's system log, which names each system sound asked for and
what iOS's audio server did with it; the app logs nothing of its own.
Steps 1, 2's Silent Mode, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11 and 12 of the TODO check passed.

- *1001 is mail-sent.caf on the iPad.* Each Send that went or was put in
  the Outbox asked for 1001 once, 2 to 43 ms after Gmail's 250 or the
  Outbox's word, never before it, and iOS played mail-sent.caf, category
  MailSent, to the speaker, for 1.5 to 1.65 s. Eight such Sends, eight
  requests; none at the second of two quick taps, at the Outbox's later
  send, at a refusal, at Delete Draft or at the share sheet's Cancel.
- *Silent Mode on:* the app asked for it, and iOS played nothing.
- *The volume:* the log gave each swoosh the system sounds' volume, 1.0,
  while the media volume was at nought. The level after the iPad's own
  processing read silence for every swoosh, as it did for the music, so
  which volume governs it, the media volume included, is left for a
  person's ear.
- *The share sheet:* its whole 1.65 s, as the composer's, though the
  extension was ended 36 ms after asking; the sheet gone by 1.4 s and
  Safari live by 2.4 s, the sound still playing. Offline, "Can't connect
  to mail server.", the sheet kept, no sound.
- *Music playing:* no interruption and no ducking asked; the music went on.
- *Locked at once after Send:* the 250 came on the locked iPad and the
  swoosh was played there; unlocked, the sheet had gone.

Not done there. Whether any of it is heard needs a person's ear: the
log's level meter read silence after the iPad's own processing for every
swoosh, as for the music with the media volume at nought. So do 2's Ringer
and Alerts slider and the volume buttons, 6's two heard together and 7,
VoiceOver's speech beside it. 3 was not made on that build: its composer
took photos alone, five at a time, and those came in at 0.8 MB or less,
and the share sheet left out a 114 MB video as past its 25 MB room, so no

## B-101 — BUILT 2026-10-22, seen on the iPad 2026-10-22. Quoted text had no bar, and a file sent inline, as Apple Mail sends a PDF, had no row and no paperclip

**What Mail does.** (A) *A bar beside quoted text.* Mail's reading pane
lays a style sheet of its own over every letter: in iOS 18.6, read from
the simulator's runtime, MobileMailUI's `MFMessageContentView` loads
MessageUI's `_MFUserStyleSheetCSS`, and its `_MFUserStyleSheetDictionary`
styles `BLOCKQUOTE[type=cite]` and `BLOCKQUOTE[CLASS=gmail_quote]` at
one, two and three levels. Each has `padding-left: 5px`, `margin: 0`,
`border-left: 1px solid` and `color`, in one colour, all `!important`:
the quoted words take the colour as well as the bar. The colours are in
MessageUI's asset catalog: rgb(88, 86, 214), violet, for the first
level, rgb(0, 175, 205), teal, for the second, and rgb(18, 192, 14),
green, for the third and deeper; in Dark Mode rgb(191, 90, 242),
rgb(0, 200, 250) and rgb(87, 217, 119). High confidence: Mail's own
code, read; not compared on a screen. Apple's guide mentions only
Increase Quote Level
(https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/reply-to-and-forward-emails-ipad45e27452/18.0/ipados/18.0);
a bar of its own colour at each level:
https://www.idownloadblog.com/2021/04/02/block-quote-levels-mail/. Mail
also draws bars beside plain text quoted with "> " (medium confidence);
not in this change.

(B) *A file sent inline.* Apple Mail on an iPhone or an iPad sends a PDF
with `Content-Disposition: inline`, no `Content-ID`, and no mention of it
in the letter's HTML: seen in his own Sent Mail. 5 of the 100 letters with
files he received this year carried such a part. Mail lists them as files
(high).

**What it was.** (A) Neither of the pane's pages had a rule for a quote:
the page of a letter on its own (`PanePage.letter`) or a conversation's
stack (`ConversationDocument.html`). Mail's bare `<blockquote
type="cite">` was WebKit's own, 40 px in and no bar. Gmail's quote has
its own bar written on it, 1 px of `#ccc`, which under the pane's invert
is `#333` on black, all but gone (B-050: "draws no blue bar").

(B) The header listed every part of a letter but those sent inline
(`Message.listedAttachments` and `MIMEDecoder.listedAttachments(in:)`,
both `!isInline`), a rule made for a signature's logo, which the body
shows by `cid:`. A PDF sent inline went with them: no row, so nothing
could open it, and the body does not show it. The paperclip on its list
row went by `MIMEPart.isAttachment`, which says no to anything inline: no
paperclip either. A Forward carried it, as it carries every part.

**Changed.**

1. *Mail's rules, in both pages* (`QuoteBars`, one place for both): on a
   letter's own page inside `#bm`, after the invert, and in the stack
   inside `.bm-html`, a letter's HTML, after the signature's rules. The
   selectors are `blockquote[type=cite i]` and
   `blockquote[class~=gmail_quote]`, the class matched as a word so the
   bar stays if Gmail gives the quote a second class, and their two-deep
   and three-deep descendants in any mix of the two, by `:is()` (WebKit
   since iOS 14). Each rule is `padding-left: 5px; margin: 0;
   border-left: 1px solid C; color: C`, all `!important`, so Gmail's own
   margin and bar, written on the quote without it, give way. Mail's
   light colours, as they are: a letter's HTML is drawn on white and
   inverted with its hue turned back, and in Chromium, the pages as the
   app builds them, they came out rgb(152, 150, 255), rgb(0, 150, 180)
   and rgb(0, 163, 0) on the black: the second and third about Mail's
   dark teal and green, if darker, and the first bluer than Mail's dark
   violet, rgb(191, 90, 242). Inside a signature's white sheet in the
   stack, inverted a second time, they come out near Mail's light
   colours on white (the teal measured rgb(15, 165, 195)). The sheet's
   own words keep their black: the colour is the quote's, and the sheet
   sets its own. Rendered: a reply from Mail three deep, a reply from
   Gmail's web page, and a quote holding a signature's sheet with a
   quote inside it, on a letter's page and in the stack.
2. *One rule for a part the body shows* (`Attachment.isShownInBody`):
   sent inline, a picture, with a `Content-ID`. The header lists every
   other part (`Message.listedAttachments`,
   `MIMEDecoder.listedAttachments(in:)`). `Attachment.isInline` stays the
   sender's word as it came, so the copy kept on the iPad needs no new
   field: `MailShelf.FileRecord` keeps `inline` as it did, and the format
   is unchanged.
3. *The paperclip* (`IMAPMailRepository.hasAttachment`) goes by
   `MIMEPart.isListedFile`: an attachment is a file; a message/rfc822
   part answers as `isAttachment` does, so a forwarded letter sent inline
   is words in the body and never a file, its own parts looked at in
   their turn, as before; a part sent inline is a file unless it is a
   multipart, a picture with a `Content-ID`, or a text part with no name
   (named as `collectAttachments` names it); with no disposition,
   `isAttachment`'s answer. And the walk leaves out the parts the pane
   shows as the letter's words (`MIMEDecoder.bodyParts(of:)`, every one
   of them in `bodyPlan(of:)` since B-113), as the
   header does: a text part sent inline can carry a name and be the
   letter's only words, and a paperclip with no row under it would send
   him looking for a file. That last is beyond the plan, which had the
   paperclip go by `isListedFile` alone.
4. The new rows open as every row does, by `openAttachment` and Quick
   Look. Nothing new goes on the wire.

**Not changed.** `MIMEPart.isAttachment`, `chooseBodies` and
`collectAttachments`: what the body is made of, and which parts are kept,
are as they were. (Changed since by B-113 and B-114: a body is every part
of its words, in order, `MIMEDecoder.bodyPlan(of:)` in place of
`chooseBodies`.) Plain text quoted with ">", which has no bar. Signature
logos: no row and no paperclip. Send, Reply and Forward.

**What he sees.** In an HTML letter quoted text has a thin bar down its
left, its words 5 pt from it and in its colour: violet, teal one level
in, green deeper. A reply from Gmail the same, its grey bar gone. A quote
sits 5 pt in where it sat 40, so a long one takes fewer lines. A PDF from
Apple Mail on an iPhone or an iPad has its row in the header from the
tap, and opens in Quick Look; its row in the list has the paperclip. A
picture sent inline with no `Content-ID`, which nothing showed, is listed
too, and so is a file sent inline with one that is not a picture. A
signature's logo is not. No new words.

**Tests.** `PanePageTests`, two new and one changed: the rules for `#bm`
written out in full, both selectors three deep, 5 px, margin 0, a 1 px
bar, Mail's three colours and every declaration important, after the
invert in an HTML letter's page and in a plain one's not at all; a reply
from Mail three deep and a reply from Gmail's web page, their markup
byte for byte on the page and in the stack's body; and every letter's
page byte for byte as before with the rules taken out, found once in an
HTML letter's page and never in a plain one's.
`ConversationDocumentTests`, three: the rules for `.bm-html` written
out, once, after the signature's rules, none for `#bm`; the signature's
rules as they were; and the two replies' markup into their sections as
it came, at first draw and by `bmFill`. `MIMEDecoderTests`, three: a
table of thirteen shapes, each its header's rows from the structure and
from the downloaded letter, the parts kept, the paperclip over the same
structure, the body's words, and the part's `isAttachment` as before and
its `isListedFile`: a PDF inline with no `Content-ID`, listed with a
paperclip, and a PDF inline with one, the same; a logo inline with one,
neither; a JPEG inline with none, listed with a paperclip; a PNG
attached with one, listed with a paperclip; an unnamed text part inline,
neither; `notes.txt` inline, listed with a paperclip, and the same as
the letter's only words, neither; a message/rfc822 inline and unnamed
holding words and a PDF, its words the body, no row and no paperclip of
its own, the PDF listed with a paperclip; one holding words alone, its
words the body, neither; a message/rfc822 attached as `forwarded.eml`,
listed with a paperclip, as before; a multipart/related sent inline,
holding the HTML and a logo with a `Content-ID`, neither, the multipart
no file of its own; and Apple Mail's own shape, the plain words and an
HTML split around a PDF, the PDF listed with a paperclip; that the body
shows a part (`isShownInBody`) only when it is a picture sent inline
with a `Content-ID`: not a PDF or a text part sent inline with one, nor
a picture sent inline with none, nor one sent as an attachment with one;
and that the HTML of the logo's letter and of Apple Mail's shape is the
part it was. (No longer so for Apple Mail's shape since B-113: its HTML
is both parts, the PDF's mark between them, and the test is
`testTheBodyOfALetterWithAFileSentInlineHasEveryPart`.)
`OutgoingMailTests`, one changed: the logo, inline with its
`Content-ID`, raises no paperclip (`isListedFile`), and a picture sent
inline is still no attachment to the body's walk. `PaneDocumentTests`,
one, over the shipping repository and the scripted server: a letter with
a PDF sent inline and a logo, the paperclip on its row, the PDF's row in
the header from the row and once the letter has come, and its bytes at
the tap; and a letter with the logo alone, no paperclip and no row. The
scripted server can send a file inline with no `Content-ID`.
`MailShelfTests`, one: a row kept with a PDF whose record says inline
and a logo, the record in the fields it always had and the format 1, and
the header drawn from it after a launch listing the PDF and not the
logo. `BoundedLetterTests`' fingerprints of the pane's pages are taken
with the rules out, and are as they were. The tests that already had
signature logos, in `LargeLetterTests` and `PaneDocumentTests`, pass
unchanged.

Each rule for the files undone in the worktree, one at a time, the full
suite run: `isShownInBody` without its `Content-ID` test, 3 failures in
2 tests, and without its picture test, 4 in 2; `isAttachment` made to
answer an inline part as `isListedFile` does, one rule for the body and
the paperclip, 21 in 3, the table, the decoding of the ordinary letters,
whose forwards sent inline lost their words, and a picture sent inline
taken for an attachment; `isListedFile` in place of `isAttachment` in
`chooseBodies` and `collectAttachments`, none, by construction, since
it answers as `isAttachment` for message/rfc822, the one part those two
ask about; the message/rfc822 case taken out of `isListedFile`, 3 in 1;
`Message.listedAttachments` by `isInline` as before, 13 in 3;
`MIMEDecoder.listedAttachments(in:)` by `isInline`, 12 in 2; the
paperclip by `isAttachment` as before, 6 in 2; the paperclip not leaving
out the letter's words, 1 in 1; `isListedFile` without its unnamed text
test, 2 in 1, without its picture with a `Content-ID` test, 5 in 3,
with that test asking a `Content-ID` of any part, not only a picture, 2
in 1, and without its multipart test, 2 in 1; and `isShownInBody` and
`isListedFile` both asking a `Content-ID` of any part, not only a
picture, 6 in 2. Each rule for the bars undone, the touched classes run:
the rules left off a letter's page, 18 in 2; left out of the stack, 3 in
1; the third colour Mail's dark green, 5 in 2; not important, 7 in 2;
the bar only, the words not coloured, 7 in 2; not scoped, 8 in 2;
Gmail's class matched whole, 5 in 2.

The full suite, serially: 1,866 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-22**, twice, three panes and two (TODO,
B-101's check): steps 1 to 6, 8 and 9 passed, and 7's first part, the PDF
sent inline listed from the tap, with its paperclip, opening in Quick
Look. 7's second part failed as the host tests said it would, the words
after the PDF nowhere: B-113. A shape beyond 9's, a note and the letter it
forwards inline, showed the note alone: B-114. The first time the replies
were the app's own, in Mail's markup, the test account holding no letter
from Mail; the second, the letters were made on the host and put in its
Inbox. Seen again the same day on a build of int11 (e739d2c), with B-113
and B-114, the same letters under new headers: 7's second part passed,
the words after the PDF and "Sent from my iPad" under its blue row, in
three panes and two, and the note's forwarded letter was drawn under it
with its header lines. Not tried: the iOS 18.6 simulator, and Mail's own
bars beside these, there being no device with Mail at hand.

**Not covered.**

- Bars beside plain text quoted with "> ", as Mail draws them: left to
  the owner.
- The words in the bar's colour, as Mail has them: the owner may want
  the bar alone. That is the `color` declaration out of `QuoteBars.css`,
  one line, and its two tests.
- A row kept from before. A letter listed by an earlier build has no
  paperclip for its PDF sent inline, and its kept files leave the PDF
  out, as that listing did, so its header gains the row only when the
  letter has come. Both until that folder is next listed from the top.
  A row listed by this build keeps the PDF with its inline mark, and a
  launch draws it.
- A part with no `Content-Disposition` has its row and no paperclip, as
  before, if it is not text and has no name, a picture say, or is text
  with a name (`text/calendar; name="invite.ics"`, `text/plain;
  name="notes.txt"`), unless the pane takes it for the letter's words:
  with no disposition the paperclip goes by `isAttachment`, which asks a
  name of a file and takes no text part for one.
- A picture sent inline with a `Content-ID` that the body does not show,
  in a plain-text letter or beside HTML that names no such `cid:`: no
  row, no paperclip and nothing that opens it, as before. The rule goes
  by the letter's structure alone (`isShownInBody`, `isListedFile`) and
  does not read the HTML to see whether the picture is in it, so it takes
  every such picture for one the body shows. Whatever uses the rule
  later has the same limit.
- Words after a file in the middle. Apple Mail can split a letter's HTML
  around a file (multipart/alternative: the plain words, then
  multipart/mixed of HTML, the PDF, HTML), and the pane shows the first
  HTML part only (`chooseBodies`): the words after the file are not
  shown, though the plain words have them all. The host tests have it so

  recorded under its own number if seen. Seen so on the test iPad

  fixed the same day.
- A text file sent inline in a letter whose HTML comes first, or in
  Apple Mail's shape above, is taken for the letter's plain words
  (`chooseBodies`), as before: the list's preview and the plain words are
  the file's, and it has no row and no paperclip. Found on the host while
  building this; not changed, as the body is not this change's. Fixed by
  B-113: beside other words such a file is a file, with its row and its
  paperclip, and a reply quotes the letter.
- A note, then the letter it forwards sent inline as message/rfc822: the
  note alone, the forwarded letter nowhere. Seen on the test iPad

## B-102 — BUILT 2026-10-22, seen on the iPad 2026-10-22. Rows had no reply or forward arrow; Mail's show one in the gutter

**What Mail does.** A letter he has answered has a small grey arrow on its
row, filled, turning up and back, in the leading gutter on the sender's
line: the column of the unread dot. A letter forwarded has the same arrow
turning the other way. Apple's iPadOS 16 guide shows one ("Flag emails",
the row "Park Photos": the arrow left of the name, the paperclip at the
end of the subject's line), and iCloud Mail's guide names
the "Reply Arrow" and the "Forward Arrow". Measured on that picture, at its
3 pixels a point (the name's capitals 35 pixels, for 17 pt semibold's 12),
the arrow is 12 to 12.7 points wide and 10 high, a light grey, centred on
the name's capitals as the dot is. iPadOS 18's is taken to be the same,
from that picture and from 18.6's Mail code, which knows `\Answered`,
`$Forwarded` and `Forwarded`; read from that code, less surely, it sets the
mark as the letter goes, not as it is written. Not known, and chosen here (D-020): an unread letter that is
answered shows its dot; a letter both answered and forwarded shows the
reply arrow; a conversation's row shows its newest letter's mark.

**What it was.** Every row's FETCH asks for FLAGS (`IMAPClient`), and Gmail
sends `\Answered` and `$Forwarded` with them, but only `\Seen` and
`\Flagged` were read. No row carried either mark, and the gutter held the
dot or the paperclip. "Did I answer this?" could be told only in Sent
Mail, or from a later letter that quotes him: an Inbox conversation's
stack holds only the Inbox's letters, not his replies in Sent Mail (Mail's
Complete Threads, still open in the TODO), so opening it did not show them.

**Changed.**

1. *Read off the FLAGS the row is fetched with* (`IMAPFetchResult.isAnswered`,
   `isForwarded`): `\Answered`, and `$Forwarded` or `Forwarded`, in any
   case, each a whole flag, so `$ForwardedTo` or `\Forwarded` is neither.
2. *Carried on the row* (`MessageSummary.isAnswered`, `isForwarded`),
   filled where the read mark and the flag are (`IMAPMailRepository.rows(from:)`):
   every folder's listing, a page further down, Go to Date, a search's
   hits and a new letter from the watch. False for a letter kept on the
   iPad and for the Outbox's.
3. *Kept with the row on the iPad* (`MailShelf`, D-016): `answered` and
   `forwarded`, written only for a row with the mark. Absent reads as none,
   so a page kept by the build before reads as it did, its rows without
   arrows until the folder is listed again: no new format.
   `MailShelf.answered` and `forwarded` put a mark on every kept row of a
   letter by its Gmail id, as `flagged` does, and write one taken off as
   nothing. Nothing calls them yet; they are for the marks written after
   a reply or forward goes, which wait for the owner.
4. *What the row shows* (`RowArrow`, new, and `MessageThread.arrow`). On a
   read row, the reply arrow for a letter answered, the forward arrow for
   one forwarded, the reply arrow for one both. Nothing on an unread row,
   whose dot has the gutter. A conversation takes its newest letter's
   marks, the letter whose time and preview the row shows (B-084's newest,
   the last to come); the row the list draws carries them
   (`displayRow`), so the cell draws the conversation's arrow. An older
   letter's mark alone shows nothing.
5. *The cell* (`MessageCell`): one image view, grey as the preview's words
   (`Theme.secondaryText`), in a 12-point square centred where the dot is
   (`Theme.rowArrowBox`), the arrow scaled to fit its width. The symbols
   are `arrowshape.turn.up.left.fill` and `arrowshape.turn.up.right.fill`,
   in iOS since 13, each made once at a size of its own
   (`Theme.rowArrowSymbol`), so no text size in Settings changes them
   (B-071). The gutter holds one thing, in this order: the spinner, which
   fades what is under it; the dot; the arrow; the paperclip (D-020). So
   the paperclip goes to the end of the subject's line whenever the dot or
   the arrow has the gutter, as it did beside the dot. Every other number
   in the row is as it was.
6. *VoiceOver* reads "Replied" or "Forwarded" where the row shows the
   arrow, in the place it reads "Unread" for the dot: "Replied, Carlo,
   Lunch on Sunday", then the time. An unread row reads "Unread" and no
   "Replied". New words, so the owner's to approve, and held from his iPad
   until he does (the TODO's question under "Blocked on the owner"); a
   changed word is one line, `RowArrow.spoken`, pinned by its test.

The plan had the arrow in a 16-point box, as the paperclip in the gutter
is. Measured on Apple's picture that draws it 16 points wide, a quarter
larger than Mail's. The 12-point square draws it 12 wide and about 10
high, as Mail's, and as wide as the dot whose place it takes.

Its grey is not Mail's. Measured on the same picture, Mail's arrow is
filled at about 196 on white, iOS's tertiary grey, lighter than the
preview's words at 126 at most, its secondary grey. Here it is drawn in
the preview's grey, 142 on black, as the plan asked: the inversion of
Mail's, about 59 on black, would be too dim for him to see (D-020).
Device step 6 sets it beside Mail's in that picture, on the simulator.

**Not changed.**

- Nothing is written to Gmail. No STORE and no new command: the listing's
  FETCH is the one it was, and the arrows cost nothing on the wire.
- The new-mail watch fetches only the new letters' summaries, never the
  flags of letters already listed (PERFORMANCE.md), so a mark made
  elsewhere shows at the next listing of the folder, a Refresh or opening
  it, as a flag made elsewhere does.
- The reading pane and a conversation's stack show no arrow.
- The row's metrics, the dot, the flag and the conversation's mark.

**What he sees.** A letter answered or forwarded in Apple Mail, or in any
other mail program on IMAP that sets the marks, shows its grey arrow from
the first listing, if the program set them (device step 0). An unread one
shows its dot, and its arrow once read. A read letter with a file and an
arrow: the arrow in the gutter, the paperclip at the end of the subject's
line. A conversation whose newest letter is answered has the arrow; one
whose older letter alone is has none. A letter he answers in Blackmail
gets no arrow until the marks are written (below).

**Tests.** `RowArrowsTests`, fourteen, new. The flags: `\Answered` and
`$Forwarded` together, any case, `Forwarded` without the dollar, and
neither from no flags, other flags or words that only contain them. The
arrow for each mark, both shown as the reply, the symbols and the words;
the dot winning the gutter. A conversation takes its newest letter's
marks, the last to come, and the row the list draws carries them; any
letter unread keeps the dot. VoiceOver's label with each mark, both, none,
unread, and a conversation's: newest, older, and newest answered with an
older letter unread, which reads "Unread" and no "Replied", as the row
shows the dot. Kept on the iPad: a round trip, a key written only for a
row with the mark, and a page without the keys read as none; `answered`
and `forwarded` on every kept row of the letter, from either folder and by
the Gmail id alone, and one taken off written as nothing, through a
relaunch. Over the shipping repository and client against the scripted
server: four letters with the marks, listed from the Inbox, each row as
its flags say, no STORE, and a relaunch's kept page the same. Read from
the source: the two symbols made once at `Theme.rowArrowSymbol`, grey,
scaled to fit, in the 12-point square centred on the dot; the gutter's
order, the paperclip in it only with no dot and no arrow, and the arrow
faded under the spinner and drawn below it. `SteadyChromeTests` reads the
cell's new symbols as sized.

Each rule broken in a scratch copy, one at a time, the whole suite run
serially each time, counted as failures in tests. `\Answered` never read:
12 in 3. `Forwarded` without the dollar not read: 4 in 2. A flag taken for
forwarded by a part of the word: 2 in 1. The listing leaving the marks off
the row: 13 in 1. The shelf keeping neither: 19 in 3. The shelf writing
false for no mark: 2 in 1. A mark taken off written as false: 1 in 1.
`forwarded` patching nothing: 4 in 1. An unread row showing its arrow: 11
in 4. Both shown as the forward arrow: 7 in 5. A conversation's arrow from
any letter's mark: 3 in 2. The row drawn without the newest's marks: 4 in
2. VoiceOver not reading the arrow: 4 in 1. VoiceOver reading the newest
letter's own arrow, not the row's, so "Unread, Replied" for a conversation
whose older letter is unread: 1 in 1. In the cell, read from the source:
the paperclip kept in the gutter beside the arrow, 2 in 1; the arrow not
faded under the spinner, 2 in 1; the arrow shown from its marks alone on
an unread row, 2 in 1; the paperclip's 16-point box, 2 in 1; the arrow
blue, 2 in 1; a symbol made with no size of its own, 3 in 2, one of them
`SteadyChromeTests`. Twenty in all, with nothing else failing, apart from
one test that reads `spec/`, which the scratch copy lacked in the first
thirteen runs and which was taken out of their counts. The VoiceOver case
of a conversation whose older letter is unread came after the first
nineteen; with it in place the four rules it reads were broken again, the
whole suite each time: an unread row's arrow gave one failure more,
counted above, and both as the forward arrow, a conversation's arrow from
any letter and VoiceOver reading no arrow the same. The full suite,
serially, with nothing undone: 1,870 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

**Not covered.**

- A letter he answers or forwards in Blackmail gets no arrow. Writing
  `\Answered` and `$Forwarded` after its 250, as Mail does, is the second
  half of this entry, and waits for the owner: it needs a bounded
  exception to D-016's "no queue of offline changes". If he says no, these
  arrows come out again before the install: arrows only on letters
  answered elsewhere would make a missing arrow mean nothing ("did I
  answer this?" answered wrongly), and that would stay so for years.
  The question, with VoiceOver's two words, is the TODO's under
  "Blocked on the owner".
- A letter answered on another device shows its arrow at the next listing,
  not at once, and only if the program it was answered in writes the
  mark. Gmail's own pages and its app never do, so a letter answered
  there has no mark on Gmail and no arrow here. Only a program on IMAP
  that stores the flag sets it, which is what device step 0 asks of Apple
  Mail. (Said by a mail library's notes on Gmail,
  https://www.limilabs.com/blog/search-unanswered-emails-in-gmail; not
  tried on the test account.) So a missing arrow already says nothing
  about a letter answered through Gmail itself, whatever is decided for
  the marks written after a send.
- Whether Apple Mail sets the two marks on Gmail, and so whether the
  letters he answered in Mail show arrows on install day: device step 0,
  on a device with Mail.
- Mail's own rule for a letter unread and answered, one answered and
  forwarded, and a conversation, which the choices here stand in for
  (D-020).
- Not seen on the simulator, where the check's step 6 sets the arrow
  beside Mail's picture. Seen on the iPad, below.
- The text size stays fixed (D-007). The square is `Theme.scaled`, so it
  follows `textScale` if that is ever raised.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-22**, a build of `featAB-int` (1b5d096),
three panes and two, the test account; the letters made on the host and
put in its Inbox, their marks set and taken off from the host over IMAP.
Steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6's iPad half and 7 of the TODO check passed. 3 failed
on an older fault, B-112, and passed on a build with its fix (int9,
8607083) the same day, its mark right at every Refresh and the row never
split.

- The arrow 10 to 11 pt wide, centred on the dot's column and on the
  name's capitals within half a pixel of the shots, about 0.6 pt; its
  grey the preview words' (peaks 149 to 152 against 146 to 156). Nothing
  outside the gutter changed as the marks came, and nothing new went on

- Beside a file, the paperclip at the end of the subject's line; unread,
  the dot and no arrow; read again, the arrow back. In Edit mode the arrow

- VoiceOver read "Replied, …", "Forwarded, …" and "Replied, …" for the

- Relaunched with Airplane Mode on, every row kept its mark as the server

Not done there: step 0, which needs a device with Mail, and 6's look

## B-103 — BUILT 2026-10-22, seen on the iPad; two faults found there fixed and seen fixed 2026-10-22. Pulling the list down only bounced; Mail checks for mail

**What Mail does.** Pulled down past the top of the message list and let
go, Mail's list checks for mail: a spinner turns above the first row, and
the bar under the list says "Checking for Mail…", then "Updated Just Now".
It has done so since iOS 6, which took Mail's Refresh button away for it
(Macworld's and OSXDaily's hands-on of iOS 6 Mail), and Apple Community
answers for iOS 17 still say to pull down to refresh; Apple's iPadOS 18
Mail chapter does not describe it. Less sure: the spinner stays until the
check has answered, and there is no pull in Edit mode or in a search. A
tap on the status bar takes Mail's list to its top, UIKit's scroll to top.

**What it was.** The list had no pull: pulled down past its top it bounced
back, and nothing was fetched. Refresh was the labelled button at the
bottom left, as it is (D-009), and each tap started a run of its own, with
nothing to stop a second page going beside the first (`RefreshTap`,
B-072). "Checking for Mail…" was said only over the page kept from an
earlier launch (D-016). The status bar's tap took the list to its top
already, seen for the reading pane on the iPad on 2026-10-07; nothing in
the app set it, and nothing pinned it.

**Changed.**

- A `UIRefreshControl` on the list, grey as the line under it, with no
  words. Let go past the top, it calls the function the Refresh button
  calls, `refresh(fromPull:)`, and so the same `RefreshTap`: the newest
  page, the counts, and once they have come the Outbox's pass (B-072).
  Nothing else starts the spinner.
- One page of a Refresh out at a time, the button's or the pull's
  (`RefreshTap.Gate`, `RefreshTap.start`). The gate is taken as a run
  starts, let go as its page answers, and let go again as the run ends,
  however it ends. While it is held a tap or a pull starts nothing, and
  the pull's spinner turns until the page that is out answers. Once that
  page has come, a tap or a pull starts a new run even while the first
  run's counts or Outbox letter are on their way, as a second tap did
  before; the pass keeps itself to one at a time
  (`LocalDrafts.uploadWaiting`). A run lets go of its own hold only, so a
  run that ends after the next one has taken the gate leaves that hold
  alone. The page has the connection's own deadline, so it always
  answers, and the gate cannot stay held.
- `RefreshTap.run` tells `answered` once, as soon as the page has come,
  failed, thrown or been put aside, before the counts and the pass. The
  pull's spinner ends there, and does not wait for the counts or a large
  letter going from the Outbox. It is put away too as the list goes out of
  sight (`viewWillDisappear`), as the app goes to the background, as
  another folder's list takes this one's place (`endPull`), and before the
  pull is taken off the list.
- The pull is offered only where the newest page can neither move him nor
  wipe anything (`PullRefresh.allowed`), and taken off the list and put
  back wherever that may change (`placePull`). Not in Edit mode, where the
  page would drop his ticks. Not while words are typed, results show, or
  the search field has the keyboard, all of which the page clears. Not on
  a list opened at a day, whose top is not the folder's and where
  scrolling up fetches the newer pages. Not while the panes move
  (`PaneMotion.onMoving`, told once the pictures are cut and set going,
  and as the cover goes). The Outbox has it, where Refresh sends. The
  Mailboxes and the reading pane have none. A pull that comes where none
  is offered starts nothing.
- "Checking for Mail…" is on the line under the list from the start of the
  page to its end, at a tap and at a pull, through `working`, by a `defer`
  so it cannot outstay the page; then the age the page has set, "Updated
  Just Now", or what failed. Not in the Outbox, which is on the iPad and
  has no mail to check for: its line goes on saying what waits there. The
  words are one string, `StatusLine.checking`, said over the kept page as
  well.
- The newest page sent to the top while a finger holds the list at its
  top, or pulled down past it, leaves the list where the finger has it
  (`scrollToTop`): let go, it springs back to the top, with the spinner's
  room above the first row while it turns. Set to the top under the
  finger, the rows would jump as the page lands during a pull still held.

**Not changed.**

- The Refresh button, where it was, with its alert when there is no
  connection (D-009).
- No new IMAP: the same page FETCH, the same counts and the same Outbox
  pass, whose re-sends keep the stored Message-ID and look in Sent Mail
  first (B-052, B-072).
- The status bar's tap: UIKit's, with no code of the app's. At the top the
  list lands a fresh page waiting over the kept one and puts held mail on
  (`scrollViewDidScrollToTop`), as before. Pinned now.

**What he sees.** In the Inbox at its top, he pulls the list down and lets
go: a grey spinner turns above the first row, and the line under the list
says "Checking for Mail…". The newest letters are at the top as the
spinner goes, and the line says "Updated Just Now". With no connection,
the Refresh button's alert, and the spinner goes. In Edit mode, while he
searches, and on a day's list, a pull only bounces, as before. Refresh
works as it did, but a second tap while the page is still coming does
nothing more.

**Tests.** `PullRefreshTests`, eight. Where the pull is offered, all
sixteen of Edit mode, a search, a list from the newest and the motion.
The words, one string, said over the kept page through it. The rest read
from the source, as `RefreshTapTests` reads it: one pull, grey and with
no words, its let-go and the button's tap both `refresh(fromPull:)`,
through the gate, one `RefreshTap.start` and one page, the Refresh button
in the bottom bar as it was, no `beginRefreshing` anywhere and no pull on
any other screen; "Checking for Mail…" through `working` around the page
by a `defer`, not in the Outbox; the spinner put away at the answer, at
`viewWillDisappear`, at the background notification, at the folder change
before the new list is made, and in `placePull` before the pull is taken
off, the one place `refreshControl` is set; the pull taken off and put
back at Edit and Done, as words are typed, as the band grows and shrinks,
as results come or fail, as the search ends, as a day lands, as the
newest page is reached or fetched, and as the motion starts and ends,
from `PullRefresh.allowed` over Edit mode, the search and its field, the
list's top and the motion; the top not set under a finger at or past it;
and the status bar: nothing sets `scrollsToTop` false, no
`scrollViewShouldScrollToTop` says false, and `scrollViewDidScrollToTop`

came, did not come or threw; the answer while the previews and the counts
are still out; a page that never answers and a second and third tap

answer, a new run's page while the first run's previews and counts wait;
a run whose page throws, and one cancelled while its page is out, each
letting go of the gate; a run ending while the next one's page is out,
the gate still the next one's; and thirty in a row, each tapped twice
while its page is out and its previews and counts left waiting: thirty
pages, never two out at once, and Refresh free after them. Three older
tests there have `answered` now, and the pin of the Refresh's wiring reads
`RefreshTap.start`; `QuietSaveTests`' pin of the page's closure changed
with it.

Each part undone in a scratch copy, one at a time, the 21 tests of the two
files run, counted as failures in tests. The gate let go only at the end

Not by design. A pull ends with the list at its top, as Mail's does.

**What it was.**

- The gap. The newest page goes to the top as it lands (`regroup(to:
  .top)`, `scrollToTop`), and `scrollToTop` left the list alone only under
  a finger. Let go, it set the offset to the top as the list sprang back,
  the spinner's 60 pt still counted in the top, and so stopped the
  spring-back at the spinner's rest; at once the page's answer put the
  spinner away, which takes its room away. UIKit's refresh control told to
  end while the list springs back leaves it where the spring-back was
  going: the gap formed too with the answer at the very tail of the
  spring-back, where the offset set moved almost nothing. Told to end under
  the finger it waits for the finger to lift, and told to end at rest it
  takes the list back to its top: both were seen clean.
- The pull left down. `reload` put its alert up at once, with the finger
  still on the list, and UIKit takes in no touches while an alert comes
  on. The end of the drag was lost: the list stayed where the finger had
  left it, and the spinner's end, which UIKit holds for the end of the
  drag, never came.

**Changed.**

- `scrollToTop` leaves a list past its top alone while a finger holds it
  or it coasts or springs back (`ListPlaces.setsTop`). Held, it springs
  back to the top as he lets go; springing back, it gets there itself. At
  the top, within half a point, there is nothing to set. A list left at
  rest past its top, the band, is set to the top as a list further down
  is, so the next page, mail the watch puts on at the top, or a return to
  the newest takes a band away rather than keeping it. Its callers all
  want the newest letters in sight: his Refresh and his pull, the watch's
  quiet page and the mail it puts on at the top, a search's results, the
  folder's top after a search, coming back to the newest after a while
  away, and a place to go back to that is no longer there.
- The spinner goes from the page's answer only with the list at rest
  (`PullEnd`, `endPullAtRest`): at once under a finger on the list, which
  UIKit ends as the finger lets go, and with the list still; held while it
  coasts or springs back, or is past its top, with no finger on it. A held
  end goes as UIKit says the list is at rest, at the end of its coasting
  or spring-back, at the end of a drag with none to come, at the end of
  an animated scroll, and at the status bar's tap; as a finger takes the
  list, under the finger; and, if UIKit never says so, after 2 s
  (`PullEnd.bound`), a few times the spring-back, or, with the list still
  moving and no finger on it then, after 2 s more, and then whatever it
  does (`PullEnd.rounds`). Put away at once, with nothing left held, as
  the list goes out of sight, as the app goes to the background, at
  another folder, and wherever the pull goes off the list, Edit mode, a
  search, a day's list and the panes' motion (`putPullAway`); a pull where
  none is offered, under its finger, the same. `endRefreshing` is called
  from four functions only: the answer's, the bound's, the rest's and
  `putPullAway`.
- A list come to rest past its top with no spinner turning and no finger
  on it closes up to its top, animated as a spring-back
  (`closeUpPastTop`, `PullEnd.leftPastTop`): at the end of a coasting or
  spring-back, and of an animated scroll, before a spinner held for the
  rest goes, which UIKit takes to the top itself. A spinner put away at

  again.
- His Refresh's counts after a page that did not come are asked for
  quietly (`RefreshTap.run`, `onRefreshRequested`): the page's alert says
  what failed. Asked loudly, the sweep failed at once with no connection

  from the Mailboxes while the pull's finger was still on the list, where

- The alert of every page he asked for that `reload` fetches, his Refresh
