## B-104 — BUILT 2026-10-22, seen on the iPad; one fault found there fixed and seen fixed 2026-10-22. An Inbox conversation left out his own replies; Mail brings them in from Sent

**What Mail does.** Mail on iPadOS 18 has a Threading switch, Complete
Threads, on from the factory: "Show all the messages in a thread, even if
some have been moved to other mailboxes. Moved messages will remain in the
mailboxes you moved them to." (COMPLETE_THREADS_DESC, read from the iOS
18.6 simulator runtime; the setting is kept as
ConversationViewExcludesRelatedMessages, and none kept means on.) With it
on, an Inbox conversation shows his replies from Sent among the letters
they answer, each labelled "Found in %@" or "Found in %@ Mailbox"
(MobileMailUI's Main.strings, FOUND_IN_MAILBOX_FORMAT_SHORT and _FORMAT),
%@ being Mail's name for the mailbox. Mac Mail's guide adds that the row's
number counts only the mailbox it is in, and that a conversation deleted
leaves its related letters where they are
(support.apple.com/guide/mail/view-conversations-mail35700/mac,
.../change-viewing-settings-cpmlprefview/mac); the iPad's guide only names
the setting. High confidence that it is on from the factory and that his
Sent letters join Inbox conversations with a "Found in" label; medium that
the row and its count stay the Inbox's; not known whether a single answered
Inbox letter opens as a conversation on iPadOS 18; low on the label's exact
words, which Mail fills with a name of its own, likely "Sent", where it is
drawn, and which mailboxes are left out.

**What it was.** A conversation is the folder's letters grouped by Gmail's
thread id (`MessageThread.group`), so an Inbox conversation held the
letters to him and none of his answers, which Gmail files in Sent Mail
alone. In his mailbox, 23 of 36 weekly Inbox stacks missed his side, about
three a day. B-074 recorded it as not as Mail.

**Changed.**

- An Inbox conversation of more than one letter that opens in the reading
  pane, its Gmail thread id a number and the Complete Threads switch on,
  has his letters of it looked for in Sent Mail
  (`CompleteThreads.thread(toComplete:)`, from the list's tap, and
  `IMAPMailRepository.lettersOfHis`): in one hold of the connection in the
  background line, a SELECT of the folder LIST names `\Sent`, `UID SEARCH
  X-GM-THRID n` and a `UID FETCH` of the newest twenty hits' summaries
  (`IMAPClient.search(_:across:)`), then a FETCH of their few words. Once
  the conversation's newest letter has come (`PaneRelated.lookUp`), aside
  from the line the letters settle in, and called off when the pane shows
  anything else (`PaneLoads.aside`): so it never takes the connection
  ahead of the letter he opened, and it finds the connection that letter's
  fetch made already up. Started as the stack opened, as it was first built,
  it read the connection as down after he had been away, while the
  newest letter's fetch was still making it again, and gave none, so that
  opening had none of his replies and the next had them. With Sent Mail
  already open on the connection its news is asked for first, as a
  listing asks, and not taken from a keystroke's ten seconds, so a reply
  filed a moment ago is found. The few words go in a hold of their own,
  and only while Sent Mail is still the folder open
  (`IMAPClient.fetchPartialBodiesWhileOpen`): a letter he opened in the
  Inbox in between has opened the Inbox, and they are not worth a SELECT
  of his Sent Mail and the SELECT of the Inbox after it, both in the way
  of his taps. His lines go without them then.
- Kept: hits with Gmail's id for the letter, none also in the Inbox (from
  Sent Mail, X-GM-LABELS lists `\Inbox` for those, as for a letter he sent
  himself), none of the stack's own by Gmail's id, and none whose id is one
  of the stack's, since each folder has a UIDVALIDITY of its own and
  nothing says a Sent Mail id is never an Inbox one; the newest twenty by
  when Gmail took them (`CompleteThreads.onlyInSentMail`, `shown`).
- They go into the stack closed, each before the first of the
  conversation's letters that came after it, by INTERNALDATE and by Date
  where Gmail took two in the same second, the oldest at the top
  (`ConversationDocument.stack(of:related:)`, `places`). Once the page has
  loaded, by the stack's new `bmInsert`: before the section named, or at
  the bottom, and nothing if that section is not one of the stack's; their
  lines wired as the rest are; and the letter he is reading kept where it
  is on the glass at once. When the section named begins on the glass
  with nothing above it there but closed lines (`bmReading`), it is that
  letter: the lines above give way upwards, by as much as his lines took,
  and if the stack is still holding the line it opened at, the hold
  passes to the last of his, now directly above the letter. That is the
  usual stack: opened at the line of a letter he has read, the newest
  under it, and his reply between them. Otherwise, an open letter above
  the place on the glass, or the place off it, the line held, or the
  letter at the top once he has touched the pane, stays where it is
  (`bmKeep`), and what is below the place moves down a line. Held while
  the page loads and handed back as it finishes, before the
  bodies; kept for a redraw after WebKit loses the page (`PaneDocument
  .insert`, `didFinish`). His letters after the newest go in at the bottom
  the same way, and not by the arrivals' `bmAppend`: `PaneDocument.append`
  keeps nothing while the page loads, which is right for letters the list
  offers again as it next changes, and nothing offers these again. The
  last letter is still the one that fills the pane, whatever it is.
- Each of his entries has the id "r" and its Sent Mail id, so its section,
  "mr…", is never one of the conversation's, "m" and a digit. The stack
  opens at the letter it would open at without them, with the line
  directly above that letter held at the top, his or theirs (`opensAt`):
  the picture his letters going in later leave, so the first frame and a
  late lookup look the same, the letter one line below the top. First
  built, as designed, `opensAt` counted the conversation's letters alone,
  so the stack opened at the line of the letter above, his reply went in
  under that line, and the letter he was reading dropped by a line a
  second or two after it had come.
- What the pane holds of them is `PaneRelated`'s, out of the controller,
  which the suite cannot build: which they are, by their entries' ids;
  which of them a tap on a line names; what opening one fetches, the
  letter from Sent Mail by its id and Gmail's id; the section its body
  goes into, his own; and whether the lookup is still to start. In the
  controller, which held it first, a pane where none of his letters could
  be opened, or where his body went into an Inbox letter's section, passed
  every test.
- His line is like any line: his name as the letter gives it, its first
  words and its time. Opened, a grey line over its body, "Found in Sent
  Mail": the folder's name as the Mailboxes pane shows it, the leaf of the
  `\Sent` folder's name, never written in. It is a line of its own in the
  letter's section, between its line and its body, not inside the body:
  `bmFill` replaces the body when it comes, and a letter's HTML is drawn
  inverted, which would turn the grey. VoiceOver reads it before the
  letter. The body comes from Sent Mail by its id and Gmail's id for it,
  which the fetch checks (D-016), as a `BODY.PEEK`, nothing marked; one
  that cannot be downloaded says so in its section, as the conversation's
  letters do.
- A tap on his line opens or closes it and fetches its body, and nothing
  else, before the conversation's letters are looked at (the `bmLetter`
  handler): no read mark, and no focus. The header, Reply, Flag, Move and
  Delete stay on the conversation's letter he opened last, whether the
  header follows a letter when its body lands, as now, or at the tap, if
  "Left from batch 4" is built: his load has no way to `focusLetter`.
- The answer is remembered in memory for ten minutes (`RelatedMemo`), so a
  conversation opened again draws his letters in its first frame and sends
  nothing. Forgotten when a letter he sends has gone, when the Outbox
  finds in Sent Mail a letter whose sending it could not be sure of
  (`sentMail(holds:)`), at his Refresh, and when a new password is saved,
  as the repository is retired. A lookup still out when it is forgotten
  has its answer shown and not kept (`RelatedMemo.generation`): first
  built, an answer asked before his reply was filed, and forgotten while
  its last FETCH was out, was kept after the forgetting and served without
  the reply for ten minutes, in which he might have written it again.
- Sent Mail refused, NO to its SELECT or BAD to the search: "RELATED
  refused" once in the connection log, and no conversation looks there
  again until the next launch. A lost connection is not tried again, and
  none is made where there is none. No Gmail extension, or no `\Sent`
  folder: nothing sent, and never All Mail in its place. None of these
  says anything to him; the stack is the one he had.
- Settings: "Complete Threads" under Organize by Thread, with Apple's line
  under it, "Show all the messages in a thread, even if some have been
  moved to other mailboxes." On unless he turns it off
  (`ConversationSettings.completeThreads`, read with `object(forKey:)`),
  from the next conversation opened; a safe start puts it back on
  (`SafeStart.viewSettings`).

**Not changed.** The conversation's row, its number, its dot and its few
words; Edit mode's Delete, Move and Mark; the folder counts; the read marks
at the tap; every other folder; searches; single letters. His letters are
never in the list's model, its letters or its counts, nor in the pane's
`threadSummaries`, `stackLetters` or `loaded`, so nothing done on the list
or from the toolbar reaches them. Nothing of them is kept on the iPad: not
in the copy kept (D-016), not in Local Drafts, and their few words are not
put on Sent Mail's kept page (`previewTexts`, which `previews` now calls
before it keeps what it fetched). Nothing is written: no STORE, MOVE, COPY
or APPEND. A conversation's row still opens its stack as before when the
switch is off.

**What he sees.** In an Inbox conversation, his own replies among the
letters they answer, closed to a line with his name, its first words and
its time, a moment after the newest letter has come. The letter he is
reading stays where it is as they go in: in the usual stack his reply takes
the place of the line at the top, and the letter under it does not move.
Where an open letter is above the place, that letter stays, and the letter
below the place moves down a line, as it does when a body comes. A reply
opened says "Found in Sent Mail" in grey over it, and Delete, Move, Flag
and Reply still act on the conversation's letter he opened last. Opened
again within ten minutes, his letters are there from the first frame. With
his finger on the stack as his reply's line comes, or the stack coasting
or bouncing back after it, the line goes in a moment after the stack is
still, and until then the letter he is reading moves with his finger alone
(below, 2026-10-22). In Settings, a Complete Threads switch under Organize
by Thread. New words, held from his iPad until he approves them: "Complete
Threads", the line under it, and "Found in Sent Mail" (D-021).

**Tests.** `CompleteThreadsTests`, forty-three. Pure: where his letters go,
before, between and after the conversation's, by when Gmail took them, ties
by Date, in runs that name the letter they go before; closed, read or not,
and never among what the tap marks or the stack opens with; the stack
opening at the same letter with them as without, the line directly above it
held, his or theirs, every way four letters can be read, his letters in six
placings, in the document's head too, and a letter of his opened before a
redraw passed over; his sections never the conversation's; Sent Mail's hits
in the Inbox too, or with no Gmail id, left out; the stack's own by Gmail
id and by id left out, and the newest twenty kept; the thread id a number
or nothing asked; the lookup only for an Inbox conversation of more than
one letter, grouped, the switch on; the line and its "Found in" label, from
the folder's name and escaped; what `Insert` hands `bmInsert`, and, read
from the script, its `insertBefore` and wiring, `bmReading`, the letter he
is reading kept still and the hold passed to the last of his lines; the
document holding his letters while the stack loads, handing them back
before the bodies, keeping them for a redraw, and none twice; the lookup
aside, holding up no letter opened and drawing nothing once the pane has
moved on; the memo's ten minutes, and an answer from before a forgetting
not kept; and what the pane holds of them (`PaneRelated`), found late and
remembered: his section tapped named his, his letter fetched from Sent Mail
by its id and Gmail's id, its body into his own section, once, a letter of
his under one of the stack's ids or Gmail ids left out, and the lookup due
once, after the newest letter has come. Over the scripted server, through
the shipping repository and client: the lookup's commands, `SELECT
"[Gmail]/Sent Mail"`, `UID SEARCH X-GM-THRID n` and the two FETCHes,
nothing else, and his letter opened from Sent Mail with no STORE; a letter
to himself once; no `\Sent`, nothing sent and never All Mail; a folder
named "Sent" giving "Found in Sent"; a refused SELECT and a refused SEARCH,
nothing found, one line in the log, no further lookups; a lost connection,
no retry and no reconnect; a lookup called off after its SELECT, nothing
more sent; nothing without Gmail's extension or a connection; the memo,
nothing sent within ten minutes, the stack's own left out of what is
remembered, and asked again after; a reply filed while Sent Mail is open
found, its news asked for first; a send, a Refresh and a password saved
forgetting; the kept copy as it was, Sent Mail's kept page without his
line's few words; a lookup out when the memo is forgotten, its answer shown
and not kept, and the next opening finding the reply filed meanwhile; the
Outbox finding his letter in Sent Mail forgetting, and finding none not;
and the few words not fetched once a letter of the Inbox was opened between
the search and them, nothing more sent. The switch, on until turned off;
and, read from the source, Settings' row and Apple's line under it, the
list asking and never holding his letters, the pane's lookup from the
newest letter's settling alone, his letters forgotten when the pane moves
on, put in through the document, a tap on his line, its fetch and its body
through `PaneRelated`, neither marking nor focusing and his body never
reaching the header, nothing kept, and what forgets the memo, the
generation taken before the search. `ScriptedIMAPServer` answers `UID
SEARCH X-GM-THRID`, and can add a folder. Changed, for the new wiring:
`ConversationOrderTests`' pins of the pane's `show(thread:completing:)` and

letters and the bodies, `SafeStartTests`' view settings, `LinePressTests`'

pins of Refresh's page.

The full suite, serially: 1,899 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

**Not covered.**

- A single answered letter in the Inbox, which Mail may open as a
  conversation on iPadOS 18; not known, and left as it was.
- The label's exact words and its place: Mail fills "Found in %@" with a
  name of its own and draws it in a header this pane does not have; here it
  is the folder's name as the Mailboxes pane has it, over the body.
- How long Gmail takes to SELECT his Sent Mail, which a letter he taps
  while the lookup is out waits for (PERFORMANCE.md, "What would change
  most", 4). The SLOW notes will say.
- A Sent Mail renumbered within the ten minutes an answer is remembered:
  his line is still drawn, and opening it says it could not be downloaded,
  the UIDVALIDITY check sending nothing, until the answer is forgotten or
  ten minutes pass.
- A reply sent from another device, or by the share sheet, in the ten
  minutes after a conversation was looked up: it comes in at his next
  Refresh, or when the ten minutes are up.
- A reply Gmail files in Sent Mail some seconds after the server took it:
  a conversation opened again in those seconds is remembered without it
  for ten minutes. Gmail is not known to file it late.
- Pictures in his letter's body that name parts of it (`cid:`) are not
  drawn again after WebKit loses the page: the redraw points the loader at
  the conversation's letters alone.
- Mail's other Threading switches, Collapse Read Messages and Most Recent
  Message on Top, are as B-074 built them.
- Where the script keeps the letter he is reading as his lines go in is
  read from its source by the suite, and since 2026-10-22 run on a model
  page as well (`HisLineUnderTheFingerTests`, below), which is a model and
  not WebKit. Step 1 of the check is where it is seen.
- His letter the oldest of all, found late, in a conversation that opened
  at its own first letter, unread: it goes in above that letter, out of
  sight, and the letter stays at the top. Remembered, in the first frame,
  his line is at the top over it. Nothing moves either way; the two
  pictures differ by that line.
- An open letter above the place his line goes in, on the glass, as with
  two unread letters opened together and the first of them short: that
  letter stays, and the one below the place drops by a line. Which of the
  two he is reading is not known; the one above is the one the stack
  opened at.
- His lines' few words, when he opened a letter of the Inbox while the
  search was out: left off for the ten minutes the answer is remembered.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-22**, a build of B-104 as first built,
with other work, three panes, the test account: J1, his reply A1 sent from
the app and taken out of the Inbox from the host, and J2, unread, in one
conversation. Steps 2 to 7 of the TODO check and the switch of 8 passed.
VoiceOver's reading of "Found in Sent Mail" could not be tried, the app
being on VoiceOver's Direct Touch list there, and 9, the simulator, was not
run. Step 1 passed untouched and opened again within ten minutes, and
failed with a finger on the pane.

- *Untouched:* from 0.20 to 1.07 s J1's line at y177-189 of the shots and
  J2's first line at y215-224; at 1.29 s A1's line where J1's had been,
  and J2's where it was, to 6.58 s. In the log J2's FETCH, then the SELECT
  of Sent Mail, its search and the two FETCHes. Scrolled up, J1 7:59, A1
  8:01, J2 8:01; A1 opened says "Found in Sent Mail" in grey over its
  body, and the header stayed J2's.
- *Again within ten minutes:* 66 s after the last lookup, A1's line at the
  top and J2 under it from the first frame, nothing moving, and nothing
  asked of Sent Mail.
- *With a finger on the pane:* a finger landed 0.05 s after the tap and
  dragged the stack up 100 px of the shots over 1.5 s. J2's first line
  went with it, 215, 204, 194, 183, 172 at 1.19 s; the lookup answered at
  about 1.22 s, and at 1.40 s A1's line was at the top and J2's at y198,
  where the drag had it near y161: down one line, about 37 px, and on
  with the finger from there. A slower drag did the same, A1 coming at
  about 0.6 s. Seen again twice from a fresh launch, drags of 100 and
  120 px over 1.5 and 1.8 s, A1 found at 0.55 to 0.63 s: J2 down about
  36 px, the line being 38, A1 where J2's first line should have been,
  and on with the finger. Nothing moved with A1 coming after the lift,
  the stack at rest, by more than 1 px; nor with a finger still after a
  small scroll, nor with a drag too slow to scroll, each of which became
  a text selection.

**What it was.** `bmInsert` keeps the letter he is reading where it is
with one `window.scrollBy`: its own for J2 on the glass with nothing above
it there but closed lines (`bmReading`), `bmKeep`'s otherwise. While a
finger drags the pane, the offset is the web view's scroll view's, in
WebKit's other process, set from the finger at each move, and the
script's `scrollBy` made then was replaced at the next move. The scroll
that followed was taken as his place (`bmTake`), and nothing put it back.
At rest, after the lift or under a finger held still, the same `scrollBy`
held. Nothing in the script waited for the finger. A web library for long
lists records the same on iOS, a scroll position written under a finger
ignored, and puts its corrections off while a touch has the scroll
(github.com/TanStack/virtual/pull/1318).

**Changed, 2026-10-22.** What goes into the stack is held while the stack
moves under a finger, coasts after it or bounces back, and goes in once
the stack is still, as it goes in at rest (`bmInsert`, `bmMoving`,
`bmLater`, `bmRelease`). Whether the stack moves is known two ways,
because the page alone does not hear enough. This was done in two steps
the same day: the page's own hearing first, then the pane's word, when the
model, run with a finger the stack's page never hears, showed what the
first step missed (below).

- *The pane's word* (`ConversationDocument.Motion`, the script's
  `bmPaneMoving`). UIKit's scroll view knows a finger on it (tracking), a
  drag, and a coast or the bounce back from an edge (decelerating),
  whatever page the finger first landed on, and it always ends them. With
  each of his letters it hands the page, the pane says whether its scroll
  view is moving the stack, and while it is, again every tenth of a
  second, on the main run loop in its common modes, which a drag does not
  hold up, until it has said it is still; then the ticks stop. The script
  holds for as long as the pane's last word said it moves, and a second at
  most after a word that nothing followed, as if the ticks were lost.
- *The page's own hearing.* A finger on the page, from its touch to the
  touchend or touchcancel that leaves none (`bmFinger`, heard on the
  window, as the lines' touches are), or five seconds after the last of
  its touches if WebKit never sends the lift (two seconds in the first
  step); and a scroll not the script's own in the last quarter of a
  second, as a coast's are.
- Why both. A finger put down at the tap, as on the iPad, lands on the
  page before the stack's, whose first frame came about 0.2 s after the
  tap that day, and WebKit sends the stack's page none of that finger's
  touches. A finger held still sends no scroll, and nor does a pull past
  the top or the bounce back from it, the page staying at its top. On the
  page's hearing alone, the model held a drag that never stops, by its
  scrolls, and lost the rest: with the finger held still half a second, or
  more than the five seconds of a finger that is heard, his line went in
  during the pause and the next move dropped J2 a line; a finger on J1's
  line had the line moved from under it; and the bounce at the top took
  the page back to the top as his line went in, J2 a line lower. The
  page's own hearing stays for the moment between the pane's look and the
  page's running of the insert, and for a finger that lands in it.
- Held, it is looked at again every tenth of a second. It goes in within
  about a tenth of a second of all of these at once: the pane's last word
  saying the stack is still, or a second since its last word that it
  moves; five seconds since the last touch the page heard, if a finger is
  still counted there; and a quarter of a second since the last scroll
  that was not the script's own. Each of them ends: UIKit ends the drag
  and the coast, the second and the five seconds are counted from the
  last word and the last touch, and a scroll comes only from something
  moving the stack, a coast after a lift the page never heard, VoiceOver's
  scroll or the status bar's among them. It goes into the stack as it is
  then: what is on the glass (`bmReading`), the hold the stack opened
  with, if it still holds, and the place kept, are all read at that
  moment.
- What comes while one is held waits behind it and goes in after it, in
  the order it came, so the page keeps the order of the pane's document
  (`PaneDocument`): more of his letters, letters that came into the
  conversation, for the bottom (`bmAppend`), and a body for a section not
  on the page yet (`bmFill`), which would otherwise find nothing and be
  lost, as a body for a letter that came would be. A body for a letter on
  the page goes in at once, as before. Each held change runs once, and one
  that throws takes none of the rest with it. Nothing is held in Swift:
  the pane hands the page `Insert`, `Append` and `Fill` as it did, in the
  order they come, so there is one queue, the page's.
- What is held is the page's own: a new page, another letter, another
  conversation, or the stack drawn again after WebKit lost it, starts with
  nothing held, and his letters are in the pane's document for the
  redraw, as before (`PaneDocument.insert`). None can go into another
  stack, or go in twice. The pane's word goes to whatever page is on
  screen; a page holding nothing holds nothing for it, and one that is
  handed his letters while the scroll view still moves holds them, as it
  should.
- With nothing moving nothing is held: the stack opened and left alone
  takes his line at once, as the iPad showed it right, and so does a stack
  at rest after a drag.
- A tap on a line as his line comes: the line is still under the finger at
  the lift, so the tap opens its letter, once, and his line goes in after
  it. Before, his line went in under the finger, moved the line from under
  it, and the lift opened nothing (B-095's bound for a line moved). A
  finger the page never heard keeps the line under it too, by the pane's
  word; what its lift does is WebKit's, the touch having begun on the page
  before.

In Swift, only the pane's word (`MessageDetailViewController`'s

The first step's parts undone in the worktree, one at a time, the eight

The second step's parts undone the same way, with the thirteen, the pins

The full suite, serially: 1,914 tests, 5 skipped, none failing, in five

## B-105 — BUILT 2026-10-22, seen on the iPad; two faults found there fixed and seen fixed 2026-10-22. Several words were searched as one string, and there were no recent searches; Mail asks for each word, and offers the last three

Built in the `feat-search` worktree, off master at 88ef40d.

**What Mail does.** (A) Apple's guide names only the fields searched:
From, To, Cc, Subject and the body. iOS 18.6's Message.framework, read
from the binary and not run, splits what he typed into words
(`-[MFMessageCriterion tokenizeUsingTokenizationHandler:]`, called from
`_fetchArgumentsForCriterion`): the text trimmed; a whole address one
word, each quoted part one word, each link one word; the rest by the
locale's word rules, with a shortest word of two letters, so one-letter
words are left out. Each word is asked for as `(OR FROM w (OR SUBJECT w
(OR TO w (OR CC w BODY w))))`, and the words side by side, which IMAP
reads as AND. No X-GM-RAW. That this is 18.6's code is sure; that his 18.7
takes the same path is likely; whether it takes curly quotes for quote
marks is not known.

(B) "Before you begin typing, you may see suggested recent searches", the
same guide says. MailUI's `MUISearchRecentSuggester` (18.6, read from the
binary): `recentSearches.plist`, out of backup; at most three, newest
first by the time of last use; each kept 7 days, 604,800 s, from its last
use; shown only before he types; one used again is newest again; deleted
by a swipe, probably. What keeps a search is in Mail's own binary, which
could not be read; most likely a search he ran.

**What it was.** `SearchCriteria.imap(for:)` sent the whole text, trimmed,
as one string in each of the five fields. Measured read-only on the test
account on 2026-10-22: Gmail matches several words in From, To, Cc and
Subject only next to each other and in order; BODY, which on Gmail covers
the headers too, matches them anywhere, in any order; only whole words
match. So several words already found the letters with all of them, but
through BODY alone, which is written down nowhere. A quoted phrase went
with its quote marks inside the string. And the iPad types curly quotes:
the field sets autocorrection and capitals off and leaves Smart
Punctuation on, the iPad's default, so "Plan B" typed comes as “Plan B”,
and a paste can bring them whatever the field says. Nothing of a search
was kept.

**Changed.**

(A) `SearchCriteria.words(of:)` reads the text as Mail does, and
`imap(for:)` asks for each word.

- The text trimmed. A quote mark is ", “ or ”, and the marks pair in
  order whatever their shape, so “Plan B" is a phrase too. What is
  between a pair, trimmed, each run of white space one space, is one word
  without its marks. A mark left over is read as a space. Apostrophes,
  ' and ’, are not quote marks.
- The rest is split at white space, and at the dashes Smart Punctuation
  makes of a typed -- (—), with the en dash, the figure dash and the
  horizontal bar a paste can bring, as Mail's word rules part words
  there. The hyphen of "e-mail" stays in its word. Single quotes, ' ‘ ’,
  come off the ends of a word: the iPad types 'Plan B' as ‘Plan B’. Inside
  a word, "O’Brien", they are its apostrophe and stay, unescaped. Gmail
  splits words further itself.
- A word of one character is left out, as Mail leaves out one-letter
  words: "Plan B" asks for every "plan". So is a word with no letter or
  digit in it, "--", "&&" or "...", of which Mail's word rules make no
  word. With nothing left, the whole text is the one word, its quote marks
  read as spaces, so "a b" is searched as it always was; quote marks and
  nothing else ask for nothing, and find nothing.
- A word given twice, in any case, is asked for once, and the first
  twenty are asked for.
- One word goes byte for byte as before, with no parentheses:
  `OR OR OR OR FROM "w" TO "w" CC "w" SUBJECT "w" BODY "w"`, the fold and
  the escaping unchanged. Several are each that in parentheses, side by
  side. Twenty words of a pasted letter make a line of about 1.6 KB;
  Gmail took a SEARCH of 200 groups, 17.6 KB, in 112 ms.
- The escaping goes by Unicode scalar. A quote or a backslash with an
  accent after it is one character, and a replace of the character "
  passes it by, as it did on the Linux host, so the quote went into the
  command as it was and ended the string early: a BAD, and "Could not
  search. Check the connection." Older than B-105, and found writing its
  tests; with quote marks read as marks, that is the one way a quote
  reaches a word.

(B) `RecentSearches`: his last three searches, newest first, each kept a
week from its last use, in `Application Support/Recent Searches.json`,
written whole, out of backup after every write, read leniently: a file
that cannot be read is no recent searches. The same words in any case are
one search, the newer in its place; each is kept with its runs of white
space one space, so a row is one line, and the words searched are the
same. A search over 200 characters is not kept: a paste he would not
search again, and cut short it would be a search he never made. Newest is
the order of use, not the dates kept: a clock moved back only keeps them
longer, and the search made after it is still first.

- Kept when he taps Search on the keyboard with words in the field, and
  when he opens a letter from the results, the words whose results they
  are, not words typed since and still waiting for their search. Never at
  a keystroke. Both, until the owner says otherwise, as Mail's own could
  not be read.
- Not kept, and not shown from the file, when the search asks for
  nothing (`RecentSearches.keeps`, over `SearchCriteria.words`): blank,
  or quote marks with nothing in them, “” as the keyboard types "". That
  search finds nothing, and kept it would push one he made off the three.
  One letter or a dash alone is kept, being searched as the whole text.
- Shown under the scope bar while the field is focused AND empty AND
  there are some: "Recent Searches", and a row for each, 44 pt, a clock
  and the words on one line, in the band's type, through `Theme.scaled`
  with it. The band grows for them as it does for the scope bar
  (`wantedHeight`, `onHeightChanged`), and is asked again at focus, at
  each change of the text, at its end and at the clear button. The first
  letter typed takes them away; emptied again, they are back.
- A tap puts the words in the field, takes the keyboard down and searches
  at once, in the scope the band shows, with no wait for more typing,
  through the same task a keystroke or Cancel calls off; it is newest
  again.
- VoiceOver: each row a button, "Recent search, Plan B". A row tapped is
  hidden as its words go into the field, with VoiceOver's cursor on it,
  so the band names the field with a layout change, and the cursor is
  not left on a hidden row for VoiceOver to choose where to go (B-079).
  The field does not move, and the results drawn under it do not take
  VoiceOver from it: the list holds only its rows.
- Gone with the copy of his mail when a password is saved or the account
  taken out (`CredentialStore.save` and `clear`, beside `MailShelf.wipe`),
  and at a safe start's second stage (`SafeStart`, which is handed the
  file as it is handed `Kept/`).

**Not changed.** The two scopes, the Trash and Spam merge, CHARSET, the
search's key in `SearchSession`, the 350 ms wait after typing. The field's
Smart Punctuation stays on: Mail's own field is not known to turn it off,
and a paste brings curly quotes whatever the field says. X-GM-RAW is not
used: Gmail would read his words as its operators. No suggestions as he
types: they need an index of the whole mailbox on the iPad, which D-016
does not keep. *Since B-123 the last word, typed with no space after it,
also asks for the people the app knows whose name or address starts with
it, from the address book it already keeps; still no suggestions.* No
swipe to delete a recent search: the app has no swipe,
and the week clears them. The folder's rows under the band, `ListPlace`,
`ListLetters` and B-079's VoiceOver code are as they were. The connection
log carries the longer SEARCH line; the words of a search were in it
already (D-016). D-016's "Not kept: searches" is the results; Mail keeps
the words of the last three, and so does this.

**What he sees.** Several words find the letters that have every one of
them, each in any of From, To, Cc, Subject or the body: a name only in
From and a word only in the body find the letter, in either order. *Since
B-123 the last of them, typed with no space after it, finds too the
letters from, to or copied to up to four people whose name or address
starts with it.* A part
in quotes, typed with the keyboard's curly quotes or not, is asked for as
one string, as Mail asks it. On Gmail that finds the letters with all its
words, the phrase among them, because BODY matches them anywhere: “Plan B”
finds the letters that say Plan B, and those with plan and b apart. Plan B
with no quotes finds every "plan", as Mail does. A tap in the empty field
shows his last three searches under Current Mailbox and All Mailboxes; a
tap on one searches it, and VoiceOver goes to the field, which holds its
words. New words: "Recent Searches", and VoiceOver's "Recent search,"
before the words, which are held from his iPad until the owner approves
them; a word he changes is one line in `RecentSearches`, pinned by its
test.

**Tests.** `SearchCriteriaTests`, thirteen new: two words two groups side
by side, the line whole; one word byte for byte as before, and one left
of several; a quoted phrase one word without its marks, for "Plan B",
“Plan B”, “Plan B", "Plan B” and ”Plan B“, alone and among words, two of
them, its white space one space; a mark left over a space; an apostrophe
kept in its word, straight and curly, and not escaped, and single quotes
around a word gone; the smart dashes parting words, the hyphen kept, a
dash inside a phrase kept; one-letter words and words with no letter or
digit left out, the whole text when nothing is left, nothing at all for
quote marks alone; a repeat once, in any case; the first twenty; every
group and the whole key read back by a parser of RFC 3501's grammar, four
ORs and the five fields in each group, every parenthesis closed; each
word escaped on its own, and no quote mark reaching a word; a quote or a
backslash with an accent after it escaped. Two changed: a typed quote is
now a quote mark, so the test of one ending the string early takes the
quote with an accent, the one way a quote reaches a word; and non-ASCII
words come through whole among several. `RecentSearchesTests`,
seventeen: three at most, newest first; the week, to the second, and a
search used again starting its week again; the same words in any case
replacing the older, its white space one space; the 200-character cap;
blank text not kept; a search that asks for nothing, “”, "" and the
like, not kept and not shown from the file, while one letter, a dash and
a phrase are kept, each as it is searched; a file empty, cut short, of
another shape or not JSON, no recent searches; a file outside the rules
read within them; the clock moved back; the wipe; the words; and, read
from the source, the file written whole and out of backup, the wipes at a
password saved, the account taken out and the safe start, the block shown
only while the field is focused and empty, and laid out under the scope
bar, the heading first and each row under the one before, each row a
button called "Recent search", a tap searching at once with no wait and
putting VoiceOver on the field, the band's one post, and Search on the
keyboard and a letter opened from the results keeping the search, a
keystroke not. `SafeStartTests`: one unfinished launch keeps the recent
searches, two take them away. `SafeStartTests` and `OutboxTests` hand
`SafeStart` a file of their own.

Each rule undone in the worktree, one at a time, and the three classes
run, 65 tests. Curly quotes not taken for quote marks: 19 failures in 6
tests. One word sent in parentheses: 5 in 3, one of them the old balance
test. The block shown with text typed: 2 in 1. A mark left over kept in
its word: 5 in 2. One-letter words kept: 12 in 5. Nothing searched when
nothing is left: the run ends in a crash, at the old tests' `imap(for:
"x")!`; with those two skipped, 7 failures in 1. A repeat in another case
asked for again: 3 in 1. No cap of twenty: 4 in 2. The dashes not parting
words: 2 in 1. Single quotes left on a word: 3 in 1. Words with no letter
or digit kept: 1 in 1. A phrase's white space kept: 1 in 1. The escape by
character, as before: 8 in 2. Recent searches with no cap of three: 6 in
3; with no week: 7 in 2; told apart by case: 4 in 2; with no cap of 200:
4 in 2; ordered by their dates: 3 in 1; not out of backup: 2 in 1. Left
at a safe start: 3 in 2; at a password saved: 3 in 1. A tap through the
debounce: 2 in 1. Not kept at Search on the keyboard: 3 in 1; nor at a
letter opened from the results: 3 in 1. Quote marks alone kept: 9 in 1.
The rows laid out from the top of the scope bar: 2 in 1; with no room
for the heading: 2 in 1. VoiceOver left on the hidden row: 3 in 1.

The full suite, serially: 1,886 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

**Not covered.**

- A phrase found as a phrase alone, on Gmail. A quoted part is asked for
  as one string, as Mail asks it, which is IMAP's way to ask for a
  phrase: RFC 3501 matches a string as a substring of the field. Gmail
  reads that string in BODY as all its words, anywhere, in any order, and
  takes no notice of quote marks inside it (measured on the test account,
  2026-10-22: BODY with "Tuesday garden" in quotes inside it matched), so
  the letters with the phrase come among those with all its words. What
  Mail shows for one on Gmail was not seen.
- Mail's own reading of curly quotes, of dashes and of single quotes
  around a word, which could not be read; and of addresses and links,
  which here are whole words already, as nothing splits them but white
  space and those dashes.
- Words not parted by spaces, as Japanese is written: one word here,
  which Gmail splits itself, where Mail's locale word rules split them.
- Deleting a recent search.
- The band's height with the keyboard up, in two panes and three, after
  turning the iPad and with VoiceOver on, and the clock symbol and the
  heading as drawn: the device check, under "Blocked on the iPad coming
  back". So is VoiceOver with the rows on show: the band shrinks at the
  first letter typed, as it changed only at focus before, which is
  B-079's typing with VoiceOver on, and the cursor must stay on the keys;
  where the cursor lands after a row is chosen; and whether the rows,
  in the list's section header, are read as a heading too, as the field
  is (B-071).
- A recent search read at a date past its week is not shown, and is not
  taken out of the file until the next search is kept: put the date back
  and it shows again.

**Seen on the test iPad, 2026-10-22**, on the test account, on a build of
the integration branch with this one in it (1b5d096), three panes, and
again from a fresh launch of the app for the two faults. Steps 1, 3, 4, 5,
7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 of the TODO's check passed, 9d's band, which shrank
at the first letter typed with VoiceOver on, and step 2 but for its word
with an accent: “Plan B” found the phrase among the letters with plan and
b apart, as written above, and a paragraph pasted from a letter, about 70
words of ASCII, went as 20 groups in a line of about 1.7 KB and found its
letters. Steps 6, 9b and 9c could not be run, nor 9d's VoiceOver cursor:
6 needs a password typed in Settings, not done on the test iPad, and the
state it asks for, nothing under the scope bar, was seen without it, at
the first tap in the field before any search was kept; 9b needs the iPad
turned, by a person; and with the app on VoiceOver's Direct Touch list
there, the cursor stayed on the field throughout, so where it goes from
the keys, and from a recent search, could not be seen. A recent search
tapped left it on the field, reading its words, as the results came. Two
faults:

1. *A word with an accent.* Müller typed in the field, the ü from the u
   key's accent popover, in All Mailboxes and in Current Mailbox: "Could
   not search. Check the connection.", from "mü" on, while a letter in the
   Trash said "Herr Müller". "garden" alone found that letter at once, so
   the connection was well, and "garden müller" failed as Müller did. The
   connection log had `UID SEARCH CHARSET UTF-8 OR OR OR OR FROM "müller"
   …` answered `BAD Could not parse command`, and the same without
   CHARSET answered BAD too, in the Trash, Spam and All Mail. Asked
   read-only on the test account from the host, Gmail answered BAD to any
   8-bit text in a quoted string, with CHARSET UTF-8 or without, and to
   "O’Brien" with the curly apostrophe; `CHARSET UTF-8 BODY {7}` with
   Müller after its "+" found the letter, and so did `{7+}` and the bytes
   at once, all five fields so, and the word so beside "garden" in its
   quoted strings. After ENABLE UTF8=ACCEPT a quoted word was found only
   without CHARSET.
2. *The band, emptied again.* Three recent searches kept, the Inbox at
   its top. Search: the block, the first row below it. q: the block went
   and its hit showed. The keyboard's delete: the block came back over the
   first row and most of the second, and stayed. Cancel: the Inbox was
   left scrolled down 164 points, the block's height, though nobody had
   scrolled it, and each time again it went further. With the field's
   clear button in place of the delete key nothing of it, and Cancel left
   the Inbox at its top; with q and the delete inside the 350 ms wait,
   so that no results were drawn, nothing either.

**Why.** (1) Every word goes in a quoted string (`SearchCriteria.anyField`),
and RFC 3501 keeps a quoted string to 7-bit text. CHARSET UTF-8 does not
change that, and the second try without it could not help. Older than
B-105: master's one word went in the same quoted strings. But B-105 puts
every word in one command, so one é, ü or ’ anywhere in it failed the
whole search, the ’ Smart Punctuation types in every "don’t" among them,
and a paragraph pasted from a letter typed on an iPad would have been one.
The SEARCH refused is a search that could not be run, which the list says
as "Could not search. Check the connection." (2) `editingChanged` grew
the band, and only then told the list. With the field emptied the band
grows by the block, 164 points, and the list then put the folder back from
the place it took when the results replaced it, under the band of the
field and the scope bar alone: each row where it had been on the pane
(`ListPlace`), which the grown block now covered. Cancel keeps the rows
where they are on the pane as the band shrinks, so the 164 points stayed
in the scroll. The clear button tells the list first and grows the band
after (`textFieldShouldClear`), so it was well. New with B-105: on master
the band was as tall empty as not.

**Changed.** (1) `IMAPWireCommand`, in `IMAP/IMAPLiterals.swift`: every
SEARCH goes through `IMAPClient.performSearchCommand`, so both scopes,
each mailbox of an All Mailboxes search, the second try without CHARSET,
a page's SEARCH and Go to Date's `RETURN (MIN)`. Each quoted string with
a scalar above 127 in it goes as a literal of its UTF-8 bytes, its `\\`
and `\"` taken back to what they stand for; the rest of the command goes
byte for byte as before, so a search of ASCII words is sent exactly as
it was. CHARSET UTF-8 stays.

- Where the server advertises LITERAL+ or LITERAL-, Gmail LITERAL-, the
  literal goes at once, `{7+}`, a line break and the bytes, inside the
  one command written. Over LITERAL-'s 4,096 bytes, a phrase pasted long
  between quote marks, and on a server with neither, or whose capabilities
  could not be read, it goes as `{n}`, and the rest of the command after
  the server's "+". `awaitResult` takes what goes after each "+" in turn,
  where it took one thing, an APPEND's letter, which is one of them now,
  with its wait after the upload as before. A server that answers BAD in
  place of the "+" has ended the command, and nothing more of it is sent.
- The cleaning that takes CR, LF and NUL out of the text still runs on
  all of it first, so the only line breaks in a SEARCH are its literals'.
- The connection log has the command on one line, each literal as `{7+}
  Müller`: his words as often as they were in it before, in their quoted
  strings, and in no line of their own.
- Not ENABLE UTF8=ACCEPT: Gmail then refuses CHARSET UTF-8, and it
  changes how mailbox names and envelopes come back. A SEARCH refused on
  a connection that is up still reads "Could not search. Check the
  connection.": it is still a search that could not be run, it is not "No
  results", and other words for it would be new words on his iPad.

(2) `editingChanged` tells the list first and grows the band after, the
clear button's order. Every way into and out of an empty field was gone
through:

- The delete key, a cut, an undo, dictation: each comes to the band as
  `.editingChanged`, so each now goes in that order. The clear button:
  as before.
- A recent search tapped: the block goes before the list searches, and
  its results take the folder's place under the band as it is then, the
  field and the scope bar. Emptied after, it is the delete key's way.
- Cancel: the band goes back to the field first, and the folder comes
  back where it was on the pane, as the iPad showed after the clear
  button. Unchanged.
- VoiceOver: the same delete key and the same clear button. B-079's code
  is not touched, and the list leaves VoiceOver alone while he types.
- Text the app puts in the field, a recent search's or none at Cancel,
  sends no `.editingChanged`; each of those tells the list itself.

**Tests.** `SearchLiteralTests`, seventeen, new: a command with nothing
8-bit in it byte for byte as given, in every form, his ASCII words, a
quoted phrase, escapes, a Message-ID, a date, a range of UIDs; Müller a
literal of its 7 bytes, at once on LITERAL- and LITERAL+, after "+" on
neither, and on one line in the log; a literal what its quoted string
said, a quote and a backslash raw, a quote with an accent after it too;
LITERAL-'s 4,096 bytes at once and 4,097 after "+", the rest of the
command after it, on LITERAL+ none waiting, on neither each its own "+";
a quoted string with no end left as it was; the form from the
capabilities. And over the scripted server: Müller found in Current
Mailbox and All Mailboxes, the Trash, Spam and All Mail each asked once,
each field a literal, nothing BAD; "don’t" found, alone and beside an
ASCII word quoted as before; a pasted paragraph with “ ” and five ’ found,
in one SEARCH, its four words with ’ literals and the rest quoted; a
phrase of 4,829 bytes waiting for its "+" in each field and found; a
server with neither LITERAL found on the one connection; one with LITERAL+
taking the long phrase at once; CHARSET answered BAD and the second try
found, its word still a literal; a search refused still one that could
not be run, in both scopes; a literal answered BAD before its "+", nothing
more sent, nothing of the word read as a command, and the next search on
the connection found; Go to Date's `RETURN (MIN)` with the word a literal;
and the log, on both kinds of server, the search on one line, his words
put back in quotes giving the line the build before wrote, and in no
other line. `RecentSearchesTests`, two new: read from the source, the
list told before the band grows at the delete key and at the clear
button, those two the only ones to tell it of the text, the block gone
before a recent search searches, and Cancel's band back first; and the
iPad's repro on `ListPlace` itself, each step in the order the band's code
takes it, from the top of the Inbox and from far down it, through q, a
recent search and the clear button: the rows he saw back below the block,
and Cancel leaving the Inbox where it was. One changed: the band asked
again at each change of the text, now after the list is told.
`DeadlineWireTests`, one changed: its word with an accent now a literal.
`ScriptedIMAPServer` answers BAD to 8-bit text anywhere but in a literal,
as Gmail answered it in a quoted string; takes literals anywhere in a
command, `{n}` after its "+", `{n+}` with none on LITERAL- up to 4,096
bytes and on LITERAL+ (`addedCapabilities`), and reads `{n+}` on a server
with neither as text, the stream out of step; records a literal's bytes
written before its "+" as a violation; and with `refusesLiterals` answers
BAD in place of the "+".

Each undone in the worktree, one at a time, and the three classes run,
53 tests. The SEARCH sent as before, quoted: 13 failures in 12 tests,
every search with an accent failing as on the iPad. Every literal at once
whatever the server: 11 in 5. Every literal after "+" whatever the
server: 19 in 9. LITERAL-'s limit one byte short: 1 in 1. Escapes left in

4. The APPEND's answer on the ordinary wait: 1 in 1, the existing slow

In the iPad's order the repro gave the iPad's numbers: the first row 164
points under the block, and the Inbox left 164 points down after Cancel.

The full suite, serially: 1,905 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The

**Not covered.** Gmail's answer to a literal over 4,096 bytes after its

## B-106 — BUILT 2026-10-22, seen on the iPad 2026-10-22. The Flag button flagged at once and nothing in the pane could mark a letter unread; Mail's Flag button opened Flag and Mark as Unread

Built in the `bm-flagmenu` worktree (branch `feat-flagmenu`), off
`featAB-int` at 1b5d096, which is master at 88ef40d with B-100, B-101,
B-102 part 1, B-103, B-104 and B-105.

**What Mail does.** In iOS 6 the Flag button in a letter's toolbar opened
a sheet with Mark as Unread beside the flag: "tap the flag icon and select
'Mark as Unread'" (MacStories' iOS 6 tips, which say nothing of Junk). iOS
7 kept "Flag/Unflag and Mark As Read/Unread" there and added "a Move To
Junk button that moves the current message to the Junk mailbox"
(Macworld's guide to iOS 7 Mail; AppleInsider, 2013-06-27). iPadOS 18 has
no Flag button unless one is added to the toolbar, and its More Actions
sheet holds the same items: a flag in colours or Unflag, Mark as Unread or
Read, then Move Message, Archive and, lower down, Move to Junk (Apple's
iPad guide for 18.0, "Flag or block emails" and "Organize your email in
mailboxes"; sure of the items, less of their order below Archive). Inside
Junk, Mail offers Move to Inbox, or Not Junk, less surely.

**What it was.** The Flag button flagged or unflagged the letter at the
first tap, and Mark as Unread was in Edit mode's Mark sheet alone: to keep
a letter he had opened for later, he had to leave it, tap Edit, tick its
row and mark it.

**Changed.**

1. *The sheet* (`FlagMenu`, new, and `flagTapped`): an action sheet, on the
   iPad a popover under the Flag button, the kind Reply's is, not iPadOS
   18's menu: Flag or Unflag, then Mark as Unread or Mark as Read, and
   Cancel, which UIKit leaves out of a popover, a tap outside it being its
   Cancel. For the letter the toolbar acts on, in a conversation the one
   he opened last, as Flag was. An item chosen after the pane has moved
   on to another letter does nothing; an item whose write on the letter
   is on its way as the sheet opens is greyed, the pane's own write or,
   for the read item, a read mark the list has on its way too. A draft
   kept on the iPad or a letter in the Outbox gets Flag alone, though the
   pane shows neither: their rows open the composer and the Outbox's
   sheet.
2. *Flag and Unflag* are the Flag button's write as it was (`setFlag`): at
   once in the pane and on the list, one at a time per letter, put back
   and said if refused. They set or clear the flag as the item says, where
   the button turned it over.
3. *Which item.* Mark as Unread or Mark as Read as the dot on the list's
   row says, as Mail's item follows the letter (`ListLetters.dot(on:)`,
   handed to the pane by `RootViewController` as `dotOnList`), while the
   list's row under the letter's id is that letter (`ListEdit.sameLetter`).
   The list's dot goes at the tap that opens the letter, comes back at
   Edit mode's Mark as Unread, which leaves the pane as it was, and when
   the server refuses either, and the pane is told of none of it: read
   off the pane, the sheet offered the item that changed nothing in each
   of those, a dead tap. Where the list has no row that is the letter, a
   hit after its search ended or a kept row a listing has put another
   letter under, the pane's own: read, since opening it marked it read,
   unless the pane marked it unread itself (`markedUnreadHere`, the
   letter's id), which is forgotten when the pane shows another letter or
   empties, and when his tap on the letter's line in a stack marks it read
   again. Never the pane's own `summary.isRead`, which it was handed
   before the tap that opened the letter marked it read.
4. *Mark as Unread and Mark as Read* are a new `PaneAction.read(Bool)`
   through `PaneActions.run`, as Flag is. Its effect keeps the row, leaves
   no folder and sweeps nothing. At the tap the list's dot changes on the
   letter and on its copies under other mailboxes' ids, held over a
   listing until the server has answered (`ListLetters.setRead`, over
   B-089's `reading`), and the rows are redrawn. The write is one vouched
   `UID STORE n -FLAGS.SILENT (\Seen)`, or `+FLAGS.SILENT` for Mark as
   Read, onto the letter its Gmail id names (D-016), and the copy kept on
   the iPad follows once it lands. Taken, `ListLetters.readTaken`: the
   bookkeeping Edit mode's Mark did, now the one function both call, the
   mark held over a listing asked before now and one back on every folder
   the letter is counted in, or one off, once. Refused, the dot goes back
   on the list and in the pane, and he is told with Flag's alert. A row
   kept on the iPad that the server says is another letter comes off the
   list, and nothing is sent.
5. *Billed from the list's copy as it was at the tap.* Nothing goes on or
   comes off when the list had the letter so already. Edit mode marks only
   rows whose dot says otherwise, so for it this is what it did. The sheet
   offers its item by the same dot, but the dot can change while the
   sheet is open, the read mark of the tap that opened the letter refused
   meanwhile: a Mark as Unread then put one on for a letter that was
   counted already. A letter the list has no row for, a hit after its
   search ended, is billed from the pane's copy, which says read unless
   the pane marked it unread.
6. *The pane.* The letter stays in it. In a stack, the pane's row for the
   letter is marked unread too, so a tap that opens its line marks it read
   again, as in Mail. Nothing else marks it read: no redraw, reload, new
   mail, or WebKit drawing the page again.
7. *One at a time* (`PaneWrites.startRead`): a read mark on a letter whose
   last one is still on its way goes nowhere, and the sheet greys it, as a
   second Flag goes nowhere. Two STOREs in flight that both fail, as they
   do into a dead socket, would leave the mark the first one only asked
   for. The read item is greyed too while the list has a read mark on the
   letter or on its copy on its way (`FlagMenu.Dot.onItsWay`): the tap
   that opened it, its STORE still on the wire. The list answers a read
   mark by the letter's id (`readAnswered`), and the answer to that one
   would have acted on the pane's.

**Not changed.**

- Edit mode's Mark sheet: its words, its two items, what it marks and
  when. Its bookkeeping moved, as it was, into `readTaken`.
- Offline, nothing is queued (D-016): each item fails with Flag's alert.
- A tap on a row and a line opened in a stack mark a letter read as
  before, and nothing else does.
- Move to Junk is not in the sheet. It is built on the `feat-flagmenu`
  branch's last commit, which the merge leaves out until the owner says
  yes (D-022). iOS 7's sheet had it beside Mark as Unread, and Apple
  Community users wrote of junking letters while reaching for Mark as
  Unread just beside it (https://discussions.apple.com/thread/5362045,
  2013); Mail's shake to undo brought them back there, and Blackmail has
  no Undo.

**What he sees.** A tap on Flag opens a small sheet under it: Flag, or
Unflag, then Mark as Unread. Flag flags the letter as the button did, and
is two taps now. Mark as Unread puts the blue dot back on its row at once
and one back on the Inbox's count, and the letter stays where it is; next
time the sheet offers Mark as Read. A tap on its row marks it read again.
The sheet goes by the dot on the row, however it got there: marked
unread in Edit mode, the letter in the pane gets Mark as Read.

**Tests.** `FlagMenuTests`, twenty-four, new. The sheet's items for a
letter flagged or not and read or not, in their order, and for a letter
kept on the iPad; Mail's words; a read mark's effect from every folder;
one read mark per letter at a time, apart from the Flags, and the greying.
Over the shipping repository and client against the scripted server: Mark
as Unread sends one `UID STORE n -FLAGS.SILENT (\Seen)` and nothing else,
with the dot back at the tap and one back on the letter's folders once
taken, nothing swept; read again by a tap on its row, one off, once, and
Mark as Read from the pane one `+FLAGS.SILENT` and one off; refused, the
dot back, `\Seen` kept and the counts as they were; a letter the list has
unread already counts nothing; a hit after its search ended reaches the
Inbox's copy and its folders; a kept row that is another letter now sends
nothing, the flags under its UID as they were, and the row comes off;
after a Mark as Unread, a listing asked before the STORE, the list fetched
afresh and new mail found by a NOOP answered with EXISTS send no `+FLAGS`
and leave the dot. On the list alone: billed only where the list had the
letter otherwise, a refusal counting nothing, and the rows redrawn at the
tap and at a refusal. Which read item, by the dot on the list's row: gone
and on its way at the tap that opened the letter, back when that is
refused, back at Edit mode's Mark as Unread, gone at Edit mode's Mark as
Read after the pane's Mark as Unread, on its way for a mark made on its
All Mailboxes hit, and none for a hit after its search ended, a row under
its id that is another letter, or no row. Read from the source: the sheet
anchored on the Flag button's own item, its items, Cancel, the guard and
the greying, and nothing written at the first tap; the read item from the
dot the container hands (`dotOnList`, the list's `dot(on:)`), the pane's
own mark only without one, never `summary.isRead`; Flag and Unflag written
as the button wrote; the read mark handed as the pane has the letter, and
put back if refused; the pane's own mark forgotten at each show and at the
line's tap; no read STORE without a tap, the calls counted across the app
and none in the pane's redraws; Edit mode's Mark sheet as it was, its
bookkeeping `readTaken`; and no Move to Junk anywhere in the app.
`ReadOnEveryCopyTests` reads Edit mode's bookkeeping as `readTaken` now.

Each rule undone in the worktree, one at a time, and ten classes run, 231
tests, counted as failures in tests. The sheet with no read item: 4 in 1;
the read item the wrong way round: 4 in 1; the flag item the wrong way
round: 8 in 2; the read item for a letter kept on the iPad: 4 in 1; the
read item first: 4 in 1; iOS 7's "Mark As Unread": 1 in 1. A read mark
that sweeps: 15 in 2. No dot at the tap: 7 in 5. The STORE never sent: 20
in 7; sent the other way: 10 in 4. Nothing billed once taken: 5 in 3; the
one back on never billed: 7 in 4; billed where the list had the letter so
already: 2 in 2; the mark not held over a listing asked before it was
taken: 8 in 5. Refused and the dot not put back: 1 in 1. No redraw at the
tap: 3 in 1; at a refusal: 2 in 1. A second read mark on the letter
going: 1 in 1; never greyed: 1 in 1. In the pane, read from the source:
Flag at the first tap again, 1 in 1; the sheet hung from Reply, 1 in 1;
no Cancel, 1 in 1; the item read off the pane's `summary.isRead`, 1 in 1;
an item acting after the pane has moved on, 1 in 1; the read item not
greyed, 1 in 1; the letter handed with the pane's old read mark, 1 in 1;
refused and not put back in the pane, 1 in 1; the stack's row not marked
unread, 1 in 1; the pane's mark kept over another letter, 2 in 1; the
line's tap not clearing it, 2 in 1; a redraw marking the letter read, 2 in
1. Edit mode billing by itself again: 3 in 2, one of them
`ReadOnEveryCopyTests`. Thirty-two in all, with nothing else failing.
In the first round, Flag at the first tap again passed every test; the
test now reads that nothing in the button's own tap writes.

Then the sheet following the list's dot, each undone in the worktree
with the whole suite run, 2,004 tests: the item read off the pane's own
mark again, 3 in 2; the dot taken from a row that is another letter, 1 in
1; on its way only for a mark made under its own id, 1 in 1; never on its
way, 4 in 1; the dot from the pane's copy and not the row's, 7 in 2; the
read item not greyed for the list's mark, 1 in 1; no dot handed by the

`summary.isRead`, 3 in 2; the read item never greyed, 1 in 1.

The full suite, serially: 2,004 tests, 5 skipped, none failing. The
release build for the iPad links.

**Not covered.**

- Seen on the iPad, below: the popover, with no Cancel in it. Not seen:
