## B-116 — FIXED 2026-10-23, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. With labels in the account, Gmail's Important and Starred were drawn as folders inside the labels above them, and a label inside another under whichever label came before it

**What he saw.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-23, in the size test's
round (TODO, gap review), a build of int12 (140df65), three panes, and
again from a fresh start of the app the same morning, against the test
account with fourteen labels at the top level. The Mailboxes pane drew the
Inbox; then, one step in, Drafts, Sent Mail, Spam, Trash and All Mail;
then the labels at the left edge, Bank to House; then "Important", one
step in with a plain folder's icon, directly under House; Notes to
Recipes; then "Starred", one step in, directly under Recipes; then Taxes
and Travel 2017. Each read as a folder inside the label above it. LIST
has neither inside a label: `(\HasNoChildren \Important) "/"
"[Gmail]/Important"`, `(\Flagged \HasNoChildren) "/" "[Gmail]/Starred"`,
and every label `(\HasNoChildren)` at the top. The folder list kept on the
iPad had the same order. With no labels in the account the two fell after
All Mail, among Gmail's own folders, which is why it was not seen before.

His own account, read only on 2026-10-23, has sixteen labels of his with
more shapes than these: a label inside another, one whose name holds
slashes, which Gmail splits into folders that hold no mail, a label inside
"[Gmail]", and labels named as folders of Gmail's or of other mail
programs. The test account carries the same shapes now, under made-up
names (its LIST is `FolderTreeTests.testAccountsList`). The app's order of
that LIST, on the host: "17", two steps in, directly under "[Gmail]Trash",
for the label "Unopened 4/17/17"; Junk E-mail's "Drafts" one step in under
the label "Drafts"; Important under House; Sent Messages and Starred under
Recipes; and [Gmail]All Mail's "Trip 2017" under Travel 2017. Found on the
host with it: a tap on the label "Drafts" opened Gmail's Drafts, a letter
moved to it went into Gmail's Drafts, and a letter in it was never shown
from the copy kept on the iPad.

**What it was.** `IMAPMailRepository.mailboxes(from:unread:)` gave every
folder the depth of its name's path and the last part of its name, and
sorted every folder with no role by that last part alone, after the Inbox
and the roles. Important and Starred have no role (`specialUse` maps
neither `\Important` nor `\Flagged`), so they were sorted among the labels
by name, one step in as "[Gmail]/" put them. A label inside another went
wherever the last part of its name fell, at its depth, and a label inside
folders that are not drawn was a step in for each of them. A folder inside
the Inbox, on a server that keeps folders there, went among the labels
one step in, reading as a folder inside the label above it. And `resolve`, which
turns a folder's id into the name SELECTed and moved to, took any id that
spells a role word in any case for that role: the label "Drafts" for the
app's "drafts", Gmail's Drafts. The folder of a letter kept on the iPad
was found by the same rule (`keptFolderName`), and the pane's matching of
an id (`firstIndex(matchingMailboxID:)`, `role(of:)`) fell back on it for
an id its list did not hold. All older than the size test; no account the
app had met had labels in these shapes.

**What Mail does.**

- *Gmail's own folders* (high for iOS 10, low to medium for iPadOS 18).
  The reference this app copies, iOS 10's three panes on a 12.9-inch iPad
  (`spec/references/REFERENCE_SCREENSHOTS.md`, primary), is a Gmail
  account's Mailboxes pane: the Inbox and VIP; then Drafts, Sent, Junk,
  Trash and All Mail at the left edge; then a row for "[Gmail]", with
  Important and Starred one step in under it, plain folder icons; then a
  label "[Gmail]Trash" at the left edge; then the labels by name, one with
  three labels inside it drawn one step in under it. For iOS 18 a user's
  written description of the Mailboxes on an iPhone, not a picture (a
  question on justanswer.com, as quoted elsewhere; the page itself could
  not be read from here): under the Gmail account,
  Inbox, Drafts, Sent, Junk, Trash, All Mail, then the Gmail container,
  Important and Starred. Apple's guide for iPadOS 18 ("Organize email in
  mailboxes on iPad",
  support.apple.com/guide/ipad/organize-your-email-in-mailboxes-ipadc7ea6d10/18.0/ipados/18.0)
  says only that mailboxes can be shown or hidden, reordered, made,
  renamed and deleted, and nothing of their order or of one inside
  another.
- *The order within a level* (high, iOS 18.6's Message framework, read
  statically from the simulator runtime on the Mac, its arm64 code).
  `-[MFMailboxUid sortChildren]` sorts each mailbox's children with
  `MFCompareMailboxUids`: by the mailbox's type first, then by name with
  `compare:options:range:locale:`, case-insensitive and numbers as
  numbers, in `+[NSLocale currentLocale]`, and with case counted for a
  tie. So a tree, each level by name, in the iPad's language. EmailCore
  holds the string "[Gmail]", and the name Gmail gives that folder in
  some countries; what Mail does with them was not traced.
- *A folder that holds folders but no mail* (`\Noselect`; medium, from
  the reference's "[Gmail]" row). Mail draws it as a row. Mail with a
  label whose name holds slashes was not seen.

**Changed.**

1. *Gmail's own, together* (`FolderTree`, new; the repository's
   `mailboxes(from:unread:)` asks it). The Inbox, then the roles in their
   fixed order, each named and indented as before. Then the other folders
   inside the folder that holds the server's own: "[Gmail]", known by what
   is in it, a folder LIST flags as one of the server's
   (`IMAPMailboxListing.isServersOwn`), and not by its name, so the name
   Gmail gives it in some countries is one too. Important, "Sent
   Messages" (a label made inside "[Gmail]") and Starred, by name, one
   step in, as Gmail's other folders are; never among the labels.
   "[Gmail]" itself is not drawn, as before.
2. *The labels, a tree.* A label, then the labels inside it one step
   further in, each level by name, Mail's way: case-insensitive with
   numbers as numbers, in the iPad's language, then with case counted,
   then by the server's name, so the order is the same at every launch
   and whatever order LIST gives the folders in. "[" comes before the
   letters, as in the reference's pane, so the labels whose names begin
   with "[Gmail]" are the first labels, at the left edge, "[Gmail]All
   Mail" with "Trip 2017" under it; "Junk E-mail" has "Drafts" under it.
3. *Inside folders that are not drawn.* A label inside folders none of
   which is drawn, `\Noselect` or not listed, is named by its path from
   the nearest folder that is, or the whole of it: "Unopened 4/17/17" at
   the left edge, among the labels by that name, not "17" two steps in.
   Mail would draw the two folders above it as rows; this app draws no
   row that cannot be opened, as before.
4. *Inside the Inbox.* A folder inside the Inbox, on a server that keeps
   folders there, is drawn among the labels at the left edge, by its own
   name, with the folders inside it one step in under it, as a label at
   the top is. The Inbox's block is the Inbox alone (`FolderCounts`), so
   it cannot be drawn under the Inbox as Mail draws it, and one step in
   among the labels, as it was, it read as a folder inside the label
   above it.
5. *A role from the flags alone.* As before, a role comes from LIST's
   flags or INBOX's name (`specialUse`): "Drafts", "[Gmail]Drafts",
   "Sent Messages", "Junk E-mail" and "Deleted Messages" are labels. New:
   an id is taken for a role word only as the app spells its own, in
   lowercase ("inbox", "drafts"), or INBOX in any spelling
   (`Mailbox.Role(word:)`), and a folder LIST names exactly so is that
   folder before any role (`IMAPMailRepository.serverName`, for `resolve`
   and the kept copy alike). The pane's matching takes the exact name,
   then the app's role word, then the name in another case. So a tap on
   the label "Drafts" opens it, a letter moved there goes there, a letter
   in it opened before is shown from the copy, and an id of a label the
   list does not hold matches nothing, never Gmail's Drafts. The app's
   "drafts" is Gmail's Drafts, beside a label "Drafts" too.

**Not changed.** Every row's tap: its id is the LIST name, as before. Each
role, each icon, and the indent of a step (31 pt). The counts: a STATUS
for each folder that can be opened, none for one that cannot. The folder
list kept on the iPad (`folders.json`): the same fields meaning the same,
the name being the one drawn, written in the new order at the next sweep;
the first frame of the first launch of the new build draws the order kept
before until that sweep lands, as any change of the folders does. The
Inbox's block and the folders' block (`FolderCounts.blocks`). The Move
sheet: the pane's order, as before without the indent. With no labels,
and no folder inside the Inbox, the pane is as it was, row for row.

**What he sees.** The Inbox; then, one step in, Drafts, Sent Mail, Spam,
Trash, All Mail, Important and Starred, and any other folder of Gmail's
own; then his labels at the left edge, by name, each with the labels
inside it one step in under it. No new words.

**Tests.** `FolderTreeTests`, seventeen, on the test account's LIST as Gmail
gives it, thirty-seven rows read by the client's own parser: the pane, row
by row, with each row's id, name, depth and role, and Important and
Starred above the first label; the same with LIST's rows reversed, and
with every child before its parent; one row for each folder that can be
opened, none for the three that cannot, each with its own count; with
"Unopened 4" and "Unopened 4/17" labels that can be opened, "17" one step
and two steps in under them, in either order; with "[Gmail]" one that can
be opened, it drawn among the labels with Important, Sent Messages and
Starred under it by name; the account before its labels, as the round
logged it at its start, with its counts, row for row as the order before
B-116 gives it (kept in the test to compare with) and as listed literally,
in either order, and the scripted server's account the same over the wire;
no label a role, and the role words; the pane's matching and `role(of:)`
for a label it does not hold; `serverName`; over the wire, the
repository's names alone and its sweep in that order, 34 STATUS and none
for a folder that cannot be opened, the kept list read back as the next
launch reads it, equal, and its two blocks; a tap on each folder with a
role's name, or inside one, SELECTing that folder and no other, the app's
"drafts" SELECTing Gmail's Drafts, and a letter moved to the label
"Drafts" landing there and not in Gmail's Drafts; and the kept list naming
a label by its own name, and one it does not hold not as Gmail's Drafts.
And the folder that holds Gmail's own, known by what is in it: with
"Show in IMAP" off for all of Gmail's own, the seven flagged rows gone,
"[Gmail]/Sent Messages" a label at the left edge by its path, the Inbox
the one role; with Gmail's folders listed but no flag on any, each a
label at the left edge by its path, by name; and with "Junk E-mail" one
that cannot be opened and its "Drafts" flagged as Starred is, as "[Gmail]"
under another name, that "Drafts" drawn with Gmail's others, one step
in, by name, and no row for "Junk E-mail"; each in either order. Inside
the Inbox: the test account's labels kept inside the Inbox drawn as they
are at the top, row for row, in either order, and one inside the Inbox
with one inside it, beside two labels at the top, at the left edge
between them by its own name.
`KeptLetterOpeningTests`, one: a letter in the label "Drafts", opened, is
shown from the copy the second time with nothing sent. The scripted
server adds a `\Noselect` folder (`addFolder(selectable:)`).

With the order as it was put back whole, nine of these fail, 21
failures; the two with no labels pass. Each change undone by hand, those classes run
(`FolderTreeTests`, `KeptLetterOpeningTests`, `RepositoryWireTests`,
`MailboxNameTests`, `EraseQuestionTests`, `FolderCountsTests`,
`PaneActionsTests`), then put back and passing, counted as failures in
tests: Gmail's others among the labels, 8 in 3; no tree, every label at

of its name at the depth of its path, 4 in 2; Gmail's others in LIST's
order, 7 in 4; a label's children in LIST's order, 1 in 1; the depths
taken in LIST's order, 1 in 1; a count looked up by the name drawn, 12 in
2; Gmail's others before the roles, 21 in 8; folders that cannot be opened
drawn, 17 in 8; a role word in any case, 5 in 4; `serverName` without
LIST's names first, 1 in 1; the matching as before, the name in any case
first, 1 in 1; `role(of:)` taking a name in any case, 1 in 1; `resolve` as
before, 9 in 2; and the kept copy's folder found as before, 2 in 1.
Those counts were taken before the four tests on the container and the
Inbox were added; for those four, the same way: "[Gmail]" taken for the
container by its name alone, 6 in the three on the container; by its name
and only when it holds a folder flagged as the server's, 2 in 1, the one

The full suite, serially: 2,341 tests, 6 skipped, none failing. The

**Not covered.**

## B-117 — FIXED 2026-10-23, found on the iPad and seen there fixed. Go to Date landed on the day's first letter, and with Organize by Thread on a reply to it in the page above took it out of sight 0.14 s later

**What he saw.** Seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-23, in the size test's
second round (TODO, gap review), a build of int14 (4448544), three panes,
Organize by Thread on, and made again twice, the first time from a fresh
start of the app. Inbox, Go to Date, 1 June 2012, Current Mailbox, Go.
The jump itself was right: the dated SEARCH, which found 5 letters, the
FETCH of their dates, `UID SEARCH ALL`, and the window, `UID FETCH 723:772`,
answered 0.54 s from Go; "Showing June 1, 2012". In the frame ending
0.65 s from Go the top row was the day's first letter, Harper Mock,
01/06/12, "Watch and winter evening weather lunch", UID 762, 9:26 am, and
Hayden Lorem, 30/05/12, UID 761, under it. In the next, ending at 0.79 s,
and from then on, Museum Members, 01/06/12, UID 763, 11:02 am, was on top,
761 still second. The page above, `UID FETCH 773:822`, had gone out 26 to
57 ms after the window was answered, nothing touched, and was answered
between the two frames. 762 had no row of its own then: scrolled up to,
it was in "Re: Watch and winter evening weather lunch", Harper Mock,
05/06/12, with the conversation mark, nine rows above. From the host, read
only, 762 and 773 are one conversation (X-GM-THRID), 773 dated 5 June.

Not by design: a jump lands on the row that carries the day's first
letter, its conversation's if it is in one, which is what `show(_
window:)` does when the window holds the conversation whole, and stays
there until he moves the list. *Since B-118, on the owner's ruling, it
opens on the oldest row dated on or after the day, a conversation dated by
its newest letter, as Mail's list shows the day: on 1 June 2012, 763; and
a reply on a later page to a letter in that row takes it up the list, the
day's next row coming into its place.* With his volume, about 71 letters
a day and many answered, a reply among the next fifty letters is common.

**What it was.** Two things, each recorded and neither wrong alone.

- The window keeps at most ten letters above the one a jump lands on
  (`PageWindow.window`, `newerRowsAboveAnchor`), so of a conversation that
  letter begins it held the letter alone: 773 was the eleventh newer
  letter. The row the jump landed on was the letter's own.
- The page above is asked for as the day lands (B-094): `show` lays the
  rows out at the old list's offset before it scrolls, and at the top of
  the Inbox the first rows laid out there start it. B-094 said that
  nothing moves on screen, then or later. With Organize by Thread on,
  773 on that page joined 762's row, and the row, headed by 773 now, went
  up the list to 773's place, dated 5 June. The list is put back by the
  rows he could see (`ListPlace.landing`, B-042): a row newer mail has
  joined is passed over and the next he could see, 761, stays where it
  was, so the row above that, 763, came down into the top place. B-093's
  closing up does not act: the row was joined, not taken out.

**Changed.**

1. *The page above in the window's FETCH* (`PageWindow.jumpWindow`). A
   jump's window is the window around the letter as before, ten above it
   and the rest of the page older, and over it the page of fifty above
   that, the letters a page upward would bring next, all in the window's
   one FETCH: on the iPad `UID FETCH 723:822`. No round trip more; the
   FETCH is fifty rows longer, and the anchor and the end of the folder
   are worked out on the whole (`IMAPMailRepository.messages(around:)`,
   and the Mock repository's the same). A reply among the next sixty
   letters is in the letter's conversation's row as the list is first
   drawn, and the jump lands on that row, from the first frame (*since
   B-118 that row is up the list where the reply puts it, and the jump
   opens on the oldest row dated on or after the day,
   `ListOpening.dayRow`*). The page
   asked for as the day lands is the one above it now.
2. *The landed row held, by its letter* (`LandedLetter`,
   `ListPlace.landing(in:holding:)`, `ListPlaces.Move.holding`). A reply
   on the page asked for as the day lands, or on one after it, joins the
   row as before. A page above is drawn holding the row that carries the
   letter where it is on screen, found by the letter, not by the row's
   id, which the reply has taken; the row then is the conversation's, as
   in 1. *Since B-118 the letter is the one heading the row the jump opens
   on, and the row is held only while no newer mail has joined it: joined
   by a reply, it goes up the list where the reply puts it, and the day's
   next row comes into its place.* Held while he has not moved the list.
   Let go by a drag, a tap on another row (a tap on the row itself keeps
   it) or on the status bar, Edit, a search typed or run, the list
   fetched afresh (Refresh, the folder opened, after an edit of his, the
   watch's fetch), another day,
   the panes moving (`panesMoving`), the list laid out at another size
   (two panes or three, a turn of the iPad), and a page that comes with
   the letter out of his sight. After that a page above keeps the rows he
   can see where they are, as before (B-042). Only the pages above are
   drawn by it: a letter taken out or put back (B-093, B-062), the
   grouping switch, the watch's letters at the top (B-049), a page below,
   a search's results and its end draw as they did.
3. *The previews from the row landed on* (`PreviewPass.groups(for:from:)`):
   from that row down first, then the page above, so the rows he sees
   fill as soon as they did when the window was all there was.
4. *An anchor the server leaves out of the FETCH* (`PageWindow.anchorRow`).
   The jump landed on the window's first row then, ten letters newer than
   the day at most, and with the page above in the window sixty, near
   enough a whole day at his volume. Now on the nearest row older than
   the anchor, and from there `PageWindow.landing` moves up to the nearest
   dated on or after his day, as it does from a landing dated before it.
5. The docs that said a jump keeps ten above the day, and that the page
   above moves nothing on screen (`PageWindow`, `MailRepository`, the
   list's `willDisplay`; B-094 and B-115 here), say what is so now.

**Not changed.** The window around the letter, ten above it at most and
the rest older; the SEARCHes, the FETCH of the dates and the landing by
his calendar (B-058, B-115); "Showing" the day landed on. B-094: the page
above the window's is still asked for as the day lands, as is the page
below where the old offset reaches it. B-042's rule for a page above once
he has moved the list: a row newer mail has joined leaves for the top,
and the rows he can see stay. With Organize by Thread off nothing joins a
row, and held or not the rows stay where they are, as before. VoiceOver's
row is put back on its letter after each redraw, as before (B-079). No
new words.

**What he sees.** A jump to a day whose first letter was answered in the
days after it opens with that letter's conversation at the top, dated as
its newest letter, the days after it above, and under it the letters
that came between the two, newest first, the rest of the day he picked
the last of them; and it stays there until he moves the list. With
Organize by Thread off, or a first letter not answered, the day's first
letter on top, as before. *Since B-118, on the owner's ruling: such a jump
opens on the oldest row dated on or after the day, the day's next letter

reply puts it, as Mail's list shows the day; held there until he moves the
list, and a reply on a later page to a letter in it takes it up the list,
the day's next row coming into its place.*

## B-118 — CHANGED 2026-10-23 on the owner's ruling, seen on the iPad the same day. With Organize by Thread on, Go to Date opened on a conversation answered days after the day picked; it opens where Mail's list shows the day

**Asked** on 2026-10-23. B-117's check on the test iPad left a question for
the owner (TODO, "Go to Date with Organize by Thread on"): a jump landed on
the row that holds the day's first letter, and when that letter had been
answered the row was its conversation's, placed by its newest letter, so
the rows in sight could be dated days after the day asked. As built, or
land on the first row dated on or before the day. His ruling: "Copy how
Apple Mail works in terms of the date."

**What Mail does.** Mail has no Go to Date (D-012); what there is to copy
is where its list shows a day. With Organize by Thread on, a
conversation's row shows the date of its newest letter, and the rows go by
that date, newest first; a letter on its own is a row of its own, dated by
itself. So the list's place for a day is where its rows are dated that
day: the rows dated after it above, the rows dated before it below, and a
conversation that began on the day but was answered later up where its
newest letter puts it. This app's rows were already built so
(`MessageThread`, B-022, B-084): a row is dated by its newest letter and
takes the place of the letter the list has first in it, which in a folder
in date order is that same letter. As the ruling and Mail's long-standing
list have it; not seen on a screen for this, and Mail does not run in the
simulator (B-074).

**What it was.** `show(_ window:)` put the row that carries the letter
landed on at the top (`rowIndex(showing:)`), and held that letter as the
pages above came (B-117). The letter landed on is the day's first where
the folder's letters came in order (B-115). Answered among the sixty
letters above it in the jump's window, it is in its conversation's row,
headed by the reply and placed by it. On the iPad, 1 June 2012: "Re: Watch
and winter evening weather lunch", Harper Mock, 05/06/12, on top, the rows
of 4 to 2 June under it, then Casey Dummy (764) and Museum Members (763)
of 1 June, then 30 May; 12 January 2014 the same with the conversation of
the 17th, 21 March 2018 with that of the 25th, then the 28th (B-117,
seen). With Organize by Thread off, the day's first letter, which was
already Mail's place. In the size test's Inbox, by its plan's
conversations counted on the host, 405 of the 5,263 days with mail had the
first letter answered within the window and another letter of the day
heading a row of its own, and 14 had every letter answered so.

**Changed.**

1. *The row a jump opens on* (`ListOpening.dayRow`, new). Of the list's
   rows as it draws them from the jump's window, the oldest dated on or
   after the day, a row dated by its newest letter. Found from the letter
   landed on, upward: the first letter, from that one up, that heads a row

## B-119 — CHANGED 2026-10-24 to copy Apple Mail, not yet seen on the iPad. Every date was written day first, 03/10/26 for 3 October, where his iPad writes month first; every date is now written the iPad's way

**Found** in the read-only look at the gaps between this app and iPadOS 18
Mail, 2026-10-24, the first of those to close before the install: the
owner's standing rule, "copy Apple Mail".

**What Mail does.** Mail writes a date the way the iPad's region does: a
time for today, "Yesterday", the weekday within the week, then the short
date, which on a US-region iPad is 10/3/26; the header's long date,
"October 3, 2026 at 9:14 AM". The region sets "the date format" (Apple's
iPadOS 18 guide, Change the language and region,
support.apple.com/guide/ipad/change-the-language-and-region-ipad0cc6a80b/18.0/ipados/18.0,
high). That Mail's list uses the short style is not in Apple's iPad Mail
chapters; Mail on the Mac uses the system's short date format
(support.apple.com/en-in/guide/mac-help/mh27073/12.0), and people with a
UK region report day first in Mail (discussions.apple.com/thread/251057286):
medium-high. Mail's reply line is its own words around the region's
medium date and short time, "On Oct 3, 2026, at 9:14 AM, Jane
<jane@example.com> wrote:", and its forward's Date line the long date and
long time with the zone. His region: of his sent replies of the last 90
days, the 16 to 19 (two counts) whose snippet shows Apple Mail's line all
have the US month-first form, "On <Mon> <d>, <yyyy>, at <h:mm> AM/PM", and
none is day first. The British form of the reply line, "On 20 Oct 2026, at
09:12, …", is the one the suite's iPad Mail reply has
(`PanePageTests.appleMailReply`); not seen on a British iPad here
(medium).

**What he saw.** He has not had the app; this is what it drew. A row
older than a week, every row after a Go to Date jump, and a closed letter
in a conversation's stack: "03/10/26" for 3 October 2026, which with his
region he reads as March 10 (`MailFormat.listTimestamp`, "dd/MM/yy", from
the first commit). The reading pane's header for a letter older than
yesterday, and every printed letter (B-110): "3 October 2026 at 9:14 AM"
("d MMMM yyyy 'at' h:mm a"). `DisplayDates` set those patterns
literally, so the region changed the month's name and nothing else, and
the 24-hour switch in Settings was ignored ("h:mm a"). The reply line and
a forward's Date line were month first in `en_US_POSIX` for every region,
so a reply opened from a row reading 03/10/26 said "On Oct 3, 2026". Go
to Date's "Showing", "Going to" and "No mail on or after", and the
"Updated" line, already followed the region (`IMAPDate.spokenDay`,
`UpdatedLine.age`), as did Go to Date's calendar, a `UIDatePicker` given
no locale.

**Changed.**

1. *Every date shown is a form of the locale's* (`DisplayDates.Form`,
   new): the short time, the weekday, the short date, the medium date,
   the long date with the short time, and the long date with the long
   time, each the locale's `dateStyle`/`timeStyle` or, for the weekday, a
   template; no fixed pattern. Kept and made again as before.
2. *The rows* (`listTimestamp`), and so the conversation's closed lines
   (`ConversationDocument`), the kept page's rows and a search's: today's
   time, "Yesterday", the weekday, then the short date. With his US
   region "9:14 AM", "Yesterday", "Thursday", "10/3/26"; with a British
   one "09:14", "Yesterday", "Thursday", "03/10/2026"; with a Canadian
   one "9:14 AM" and "2026-10-03".
3. *The header and the paper* (`detailTimestamp`, `fullTimestamp`):
   "Today at" and "Yesterday at" with the locale's time, as before, and
   otherwise the long date and the time joined as the locale joins them:
   "October 3, 2026 at 9:14 AM"; "3 October 2026 at 09:14". The print
   (`PrintPage.head`) is the same words, the date in full whatever the
   day, as B-110 has it.
4. *The composer's lines* (`quoteAttribution`, `forwardedDate`): Mail's
   words, "On …, at …, … wrote:" and "Date:", around the locale's medium
   date and short time, and its long date and long time: with his region
   "On Oct 3, 2026, at 9:14 AM" and "October 3, 2026 at 9:14:03 AM EDT",
   as before on his iPad; with a British one "On 3 Oct 2026, at 09:14" and
   "3 October 2026 at 09:14:03 BST". The space before AM and PM is the
   iPad's formatter's: U+202F on iPadOS 17 and later, as in his own sent
   mail, an ordinary space on the test iPad's 16.5.1, as its Mail writes
   it. The literal U+202F and `MailFormat.narrowNoBreakSpace` are gone. A
   forwarded letter shown in the pane (`ForwardedFields`, B-114) has the
   same Date line.
5. *Go to Date's day* (`IMAPDate.spokenDay`) takes a locale, the iPad's
   unless a test hands in another, so the three regions are pinned; the
   words are as they were.
6. The comments that said otherwise (`RFC5322Builder`'s reason for
   quoted-printable HTML, the tests' fingerprints of forwarded letters,
   B-043 here, B-112's check in TODO) say what it is now.

**Not changed.** The day: today, yesterday and the week are worked out
from `now` in his zone as before. The words around the dates, all Mail's
and all English: "Today at", "Yesterday", "Updated", "Showing", "On …
wrote:", "Begin forwarded message:", "Date:". What goes on the wire: the
Date header, IMAP's SEARCH days and the parsers keep their `en_US_POSIX`
patterns. The connection log's times ("HH:mm:ss.SSS") and a set-aside
folder's name (`LocalDrafts`), which are not read as dates by him.
Settings shows no date. A draft already saved keeps the line it was
written with. No new words.

**What he sees.** With his US region every date month first, as in
Mail: a row older than a week "10/3/26", the rows of a day he jumps to
the same under "Showing October 3, 2025", the header "October 3, 2026 at
9:14 AM", the paper the same, and the reply line as before. Today's times
and "Yesterday" as before. Were his iPad's 24-Hour Time switch on, the
times would follow it, as Mail's do; the "AM" and "PM" in his replies'
lines say it is off.

**Tests.** `DatesTheIPadsWayTests`, ten, new. In three regions, each in
its own zone (the United States in New York, Britain in London, Canada
in Toronto), exactly this host's ICU's words: the rows for a letter of
today, yesterday, this week and 3 October; the header for the same four;
the printed head; "Showing" for this year and last; the "Updated" line
today and on 3 October; the reply line; the forward's Date line. Then
the source, read: the only fixed patterns in the app are the six on the
wire, in the log and in a folder's name, each in `en_US_POSIX`, the one
locale any line names; every `DateFormatter` in the app, file by file,
with no other kind of formatter; the three templates, letters alone; Go
to Date's calendar given no locale; and every place a date reaches him
calling these with the iPad's locale, none with one of its own.
`DisplayDatesTests` now pins his region's words, "9/27/26" and "September
27, 2026 at 11:50 PM", and checks the kept formatters against ones built
afresh from the same styles in five languages and four zones;
`ReplyForwardTests` and `PrintPageTests` give the locale, en_US and
en_US_POSIX, whose strings they pin; the forwarded letters' fingerprints
(`OrdinaryMail.decodedFingerprints`) are put back in `en_US_POSIX` as well
as GMT, and are the recorded ones unchanged.

Each part undone by hand, the date tests run (`DatesTheIPadsWayTests`,
`DisplayDatesTests`, `ReplyForwardTests`, `PrintPageTests`,
`FeedbackTests`, `IMAPDateTests`, `RichQuoteTests`, `AppleMailHTMLTests`,
`GoToDateRowTests`), then put back and passing, counted as failures in
tests: the short date back to "dd/MM/yy", 93 in 6; the long date and time
back to "d MMMM yyyy 'at' h:mm a", 163 in 8; the time back to "h:mm a",
866 in 14; the reply line back to `en_US_POSIX` and a fixed pattern, 4 in
3; the forward's Date line so, 4 in 3; "Showing" without the locale, 2
in 1; the "Updated" line's date as "dd/MM/yy", 6 in 4; a formatter of its
own in `MessageCell`, 2 in 2; the row's date asked for in en_GB there, 4
in 2; Go to Date's calendar given en_GB, 3 in 2.

The full suite, serially: 2,414 tests, 10 of them new, 6 skipped, none

## B-120 — CHANGED 2026-10-24 to copy Apple Mail, not yet seen on the iPad. A letter opened with no caret and no keyboard; Mail's opens ready to type

**What Mail does.** Apple's iPadOS 18 guide goes from Reply straight to
"Type your response, then tap Send", and from Forward to "Enter the email
addresses of the new recipients", with no tap between
(support.apple.com/guide/ipad/reply-to-and-forward-emails-ipad45e27452/18.0/ipados/18.0);
for a new letter it says "tap the To field" and is silent on where the
caret starts. Mail's composer is MessageUI's: its share sheet entry opens
it, and its kinds of letter (`_MFMailCompositionContext`) are the Mail
app's own, a reply, a forward, a draft, the Outbox's and Send Again's;
the Mail app's own code is not in the simulator, so that it opens this
composer is taken from them. Its choice was read from iOS 18.6's
simulator runtime on the Mac,
`-[MFMailComposeController pickInitialFirstResponder]`: To while it holds
no address; then Subject while its text is empty; then the body, the
caret at its start (`-[MFComposeWebView placeCaretAtStartOfBodyField]`).
It has no case of its own for a reply, a forward, a share or a draft
reopened from Drafts, the Outbox or Send Again: each is those three
questions, so a reply opens in the body above the signature and the quote,
and a new letter, a forward and a share in To. It is asked as the sheet is
about to appear and again once the letter's content has loaded; before
the sheet has appeared, and unless whatever opened it asked for the
keyboard at once, it takes no field, and a field it had before a sheet
went over it (the camera, a scan, markup, a person's card) is given back
instead of a new choice. Its Subject step goes past the one the gap list
asked for (To, otherwise the body): a letter to someone with no subject
yet opens in Subject. Not seen on a screen: Mail does not run in the
simulator (B-074), and the iPad's iPadOS 18.7 was not read.

**What he does.** In 30 days of his Sent Mail, about 421 replies, 136
forwards and 479 letters of his own: some 35 letters a day through this
composer (gap list, 2026-10-24).

**What it was.** The composer had no `viewDidAppear` and gave focus to
nothing as it opened; its one `becomeFirstResponder` was Return in
Subject. Its body's caret was set at 0 (B-069) on a body that was not
first responder, so his first tap put the caret wherever his finger
landed, in a reply often in the quote. The share sheet went into To as it
appeared whenever the share had nobody in To, every time it appeared.

**Changed.**

1. *The rule* (`ComposeForm.firstField`, new): To while it holds no one
   (an entry of spaces is no one); then Subject while it is empty (a
   subject of spaces is a subject, as Mail asks the length); then the
   body.
2. *When* (`ComposeForm.readiesOnAppearing`, new): the first time the
   sheet appears, and only then; not with an alert or another sheet put up
   over it; not once he is in a field himself. The one chance is taken
   whatever it decides, so a caret he has put somewhere is never moved.
3. *The composer* (`readyToType`, from a new `viewDidAppear`): To or
   Subject made first responder, or the body with the caret at 0 and its
   line brought into view, the keyboard coming up with it. The letter is
   whole as the sheet opens here, so the rule is asked once, where Mail's
   asks again when its content has loaded.
4. *The share sheet*: the same rule and the same once, in place of To
   whenever it appeared. A share has nobody in To, so it opens in To, as
   it did.

**Not changed.** Return in Subject and the body's caret at 0 for Tab
(B-069); To offering nothing as he goes in (B-073), so the list stays
closed; the sheet ending above the keyboard (B-069); Cancel's question,
since a caret changes nothing in the letter and an untouched letter still
closes without a word; the address rows' email keyboard. No new words.

**What he sees.** A new letter and a forward open with the keyboard up and
the caret in To, no list under it. A reply, a Reply All and a draft
reopened from Drafts open with the keyboard up and the caret on the empty
line at the top, above his signature and the quote. A `mailto:` link with
an address and no subject opens in Subject. A share opens in To, as
before. A caret he puts elsewhere stays there when a picker or Cancel's
question has come and gone. With a hardware keyboard, the caret in the
same places and no keyboard on the screen.

**Tests.** `ReadyToTypeTests`, seven: a new letter and a forward in To; a
reply and a Reply All in the body, its first line the empty one above the
signature and the quote, with and without a signature; a draft by the
same rule, Subject when it has To and no subject, To when only Cc holds
someone or To holds spaces; a subject of spaces is a subject; a share
from a page, a link alone or words in To; once, never over something,
never with him in a field; and the source read in both sheets, the rule
asked from `viewDidAppear` alone, the chance marked taken whatever it
decides, To, Subject, or the body at 0 with its line in view.
`ComposeLikeMailTests.testOnlyTypingShowsTheListInEither` reads the share
sheet's new `viewDidAppear`.

Each part undone by hand, the two classes run, then put back and passing,
counted as failures in tests: no Subject step, 2 in 2; a subject of
spaces no subject, 1 in 1; To read raw, so spaces are someone, 1 in 1; To
never asked, 8 in 4; not once, 1 in 1; over an alert, 1 in 1; with him in
a field, 1 in 1; the composer with no `viewDidAppear`, as it was, 3 in 1;
the chance marked taken only when the caret was put, 1 in 1; the body
made first responder with its caret left where it was, 1 in 1; the share
sheet into To only, as it was, 4 in 2.

The full suite, serially: 2,411 tests, 7 of them new, 6 skipped, none

## B-122 — CHANGED 2026-10-24 to copy Apple Mail, not yet seen on the iPad. A tap on a photo in a letter did nothing; Mail opens it full screen, with Save Image and Save to Files

**Found** in the gap review of 2026-10-24, the fifth of the gaps to close
before the install: a photo shown among a letter's words could not be
opened. A tap on it did nothing, and a touch and hold gave WebKit's menu,
with Save to Photos and no Save to Files (B-067). Pinch-zoom, never checked
on the iPad, was the only way to see it larger. In his mailbox, by counts
only, 31 letters from others in 30 days had a photo-sized picture, over
150 KB, shown in the body by `cid:`, about one a day, and 2 had one with no
`Content-ID`; 75 carried pictures, and he opens about 2 picture letters a
day.

**What Mail does.** Apple's iPadOS 18 guide, "Download email attachments
in Mail on iPad"
(support.apple.com/guide/ipad/download-email-attachments-ipad09ffdc70/18.0/ipados/18.0):
"In the message, tap the attachment to open the document"; "Open a message
with an attachment, then touch and hold the attachment", then "Choose Save
Image", "Choose Save to Files", or Share; and "Touch and hold the photo,
then choose Look Up". That a picture shown inside the letter opens the same
way is in developers' reports rather than Apple's guide: for pictures
embedded by `cid:`, "the iPhone mail app shows a quicklook of those images
when the users taps on them", not for a picture from the web ("I tried
changing from cid to a remote URL for the image - then the iPhone mailer
does not display the Quicklook"), and for one inside a link it opens the
link and the picture both, which the reporters take for a fault; an answer
tested on iOS 15 Mail in 2025 finds that a `<picture>` with a `cid:` source
does not open (stackoverflow.com/questions/76543486, 2023). Confidence:
high that a tap on a picture the letter carries opens Mail's viewer, with
Save Image and Save to Files from its share button and from the touch and
hold; medium that the iPad and iPadOS 18 do it as the iPhone does, which
the reports do not name. No size rule of Mail's is known: by the reports
it opens every picture the letter carries.

**What it was.** The pane acted on taps on links only (`PaneNavigation`):
a picture is no navigation. A picture the body shows by `cid:` has no row
in the header (`Attachment.isShownInBody`, B-101), so nothing on the
screen opened it. The pane's script, in the app's content world, wired the
stack's lines and nothing else, and on a letter's own page nothing at all.

**Changed.**

1. *A tap on a picture of the letter's own opens it* (`PanePictures`,
   new; the pane's `openPicture`). The pane's script
   (`ConversationDocument.script`) gives each `<img>` whose `src` is the
   loader's address, `bmcid://`, a click listener: the `src` as WebKit
   reads it (`img.src`), the address the loader is asked for, with any
   space a sender left around it trimmed, not the attribute as written,
   in which a space before the address hid it. The listener is given on
   a letter's own page as the document ends, and in a stack as `bmFill`
   puts each body in, the only way a body goes into one. The click, which WebKit makes of a tap as
   it makes a link's, tells the pane, through a handler of its own,
   `bmPicture`, registered in the app's content world alone as `bmLetter`
   is, the picture's address, the section it is in and its sizes. The pane
   reads the `Content-ID` from the address as the loader reads it
   (`InlineImageRewriter.contentID(of:)`, which the loader now calls), takes
   the letter's part with it, the last of two under one id as the loader
   serves, and opens it by `openAttachment`, the path a file's row in the
   header takes: from the copy kept on the iPad (B-111) or the letter last
   fetched, or downloaded, written as the one staged file (B-063), and shown
   in Quick Look full screen, whose share button has Save Image and Save to
   Files. A picture the header lists as well, sent as a file and shown by
   `cid:`, opens the same, its row busy while it comes if the header shows
   its letter.
2. *Which letter.* On a letter's own page, the letter. In a stack, the
   letter whose section the picture is in, the section that is the page's
   own child, so a section a letter's markup draws inside itself names
   nothing: one of the conversation's whose body has come, or his own from
   Sent Mail (B-104), which the pane now keeps once its body has come
   (`PaneRelated.keep`) and lets go with the conversation.
3. *Which pictures.* Not one inside a link, however deep, an image map or
   a button: the tap is theirs, a link going where a tapped link goes ("Open
   this link?", or the composer for `mailto:`), and the picture does not
   open with it, where Mail's reportedly does. A link is an `<a>` with an
   `href`, an empty one too, as WebKit has it. An `<a>` with none is a
   bookmark, no link, and a tap in it goes nowhere: Outlook and Word wrap
   a signature, a letter quoted or a passage in one, named
   `_MailAutoSig`, `_MailOriginal`, `OLE_LINK1` or `_Hlk…`, and a photo
   inside opens as any other. Not a picture from the web, as Mail
   does not. Not a picture under 100 each way in pixels in itself, nor
   one drawn under 100 points along its longer side or under 44 along its
   shorter (`PanePictures.least`, `leastAcross`), a bound of the app's own,
   as no rule of Mail's is known; 44 is the least a thing to be tapped is
   by Apple's guidelines, as the app's buttons are. It leaves out a spacer
   or a tracking pixel drawn large, a picture that has not come, an icon,
   and a logo drawn small whatever its own size: his own signature's is
   210 by 156 drawn at 35 by 25 (INVESTIGATIONS, 2026-09-21). An Outlook
   banner of 1,200 by 300 drawn at 300 by 75 opens, as Mail's would. The
   shorter side is not held to 100, so that whether a photo opens does not
   hang on the panes: a panorama from an iPhone, about 6 to 1, drawn the
   letter's width on his iPad, some 650 points in two panes and some 500
   in three, is some 108 high in two and some 83 in three, and opens in
   both; held to 100 each way as drawn, as first built, it opened in two
   panes and not in three. A photo from an iPad or an iPhone is thousands
   of pixels each way and drawn as wide as the pane allows; one of 320 by
   240 drawn at 160 by 120 still opens.
4. *Nothing a letter writes can open anything.* Its script does not run
   (B-055), its markup has no handler to post to, and what the pane's
   script posts says only where to look: a part, by a `Content-ID` the
   letter has, of the letter the picture is in. `PaneNavigation` and its
   guard are as they were.
5. *Never over another letter.* A picture that comes after the pane has
   moved on, to another letter, the same row tapped again or nothing, is
   not shown, and no failure is said for it: the pane notes what it shows
   at the tap (`PaneLoads.shown`), and `openAttachment` asks, once the
   part has come or failed, whether it still shows that
   (`PaneLoads.stillShows`), the rule a letter's body has
   (`PaneLoads.draws`): a letter he tapped past never says "could not be
   downloaded" over the one he stopped on. A picture has no spinner, and
   comes from the server when its letter is neither kept on the iPad nor
   the last fetched, a letter of a stack once another has opened among
   them; so he could tap it, see nothing for some seconds, tap the next
   row, and have the first letter's photo come up full screen over the
   next one, or "Attachment could not be downloaded." after a time out.
   Another letter of the conversation opened meanwhile, or his letters
   from Sent Mail put in, is the same conversation shown, and the picture
   opens. The download is not called off: it ends, and is let go. In
   `openAttachment`, so a file's row, in the header or among the words
   (B-113), is held to it as well; its file used to come up over whatever
   the pane showed by then.
6. The comments that said a letter's page gets nothing from the script,
   and that the pane keeps nothing of his letters from Sent Mail but their
   bodies, say what is so now (`ConversationDocument`, `PaneRelated`,
   `PaneNavigation`, the pane).

**Not changed.** The touch and hold: WebKit's menu with Save to Photos, as
before (B-067); WebKit's public hook for the menu names a link only
(`WKContextMenuElementInfo.linkURL`). Pictures from the web load as before
(B-055, the owner's question). A tap on a link, a picture in one included,
on a file's row among the words (B-113) or on a stack's line (B-095) does
what it did, and pinch-zoom, but for 5: a file that comes once the pane has
moved on is not shown. Nothing is fetched that was not before but
the picture's part at the tap, as a file's row fetches it; nothing is sent.
No new words: Quick Look's are iOS's.

**What he sees.** A tap on a photo in a letter opens it full screen over
the app, as a PDF's row does: Done closes it, the share button offers Save
Image and Save to Files among the rest. It comes at once when the letter is
kept on the iPad or was the last downloaded, and otherwise after its
download, with no sign meanwhile; if he taps another row first, nothing
comes up over that letter, and nothing is said. A photo in an Outlook
letter's signature or quoted letter opens as any other. A tap on a logo,
an icon, a picture from the web or a picture that is a link does what it
did.

**Tests.** `PictureTapTests`, eleven. A tap read as the script posts it,
numbers as WebKit hands them over or as Swift holds them, the scheme in
any case, and nothing for an address of another scheme or naming no id, or
a field missing or of another kind. The `Content-ID` a tap reads is the
one the loader serves, through `InlineImageRewriter.rewrite`, for ids as
Apple Mail, Outlook, Gmail and the app's own signature write them. The
bound: a photo, 100 by 100 drawn 100 by 44 either way up, a photo of 320
by 240 drawn at 160 by 120, a panorama drawn as in two panes and as in
three, and a banner logo drawn 300 by 75 open; his logo, spacers, a
picture not come, an icon drawn small or large, 99 any way in itself,
drawn 99 each way or 43 across, a rule drawn thin, and NaN and infinity,
in itself or as drawn, do not. The part: the letter's own, a picture the
header lists too, the last of two under one id, as `PanePage.pictures`
has it, and none for an id the letter lacks or a picture too small. The
letter: on its own page the letter, whatever section; in a stack, the
section's, his from Sent Mail by his section, none for "", another section
or a letter not come. His letter kept once come, not another than the one
asked for, let go with the conversation, and not back when the
conversation is shown again until it comes again. In node, on the model of
the pane's page (`ModelPage`, which now has clicks, pictures' sizes, and
their `src` as WebKit reads it, trimmed): on a letter's own page the photo
and the logo are posted, with no section, and a picture in a link, in a
`<div>` in a link, in a link with an empty `href`, with `usemap`, in a
button, from the web, or by a `cid:` the letter lacks is not, nor a tap on
the words; one in a bookmark, `<a name="_MailAutoSig">`, is, and one whose
`src` has a space before and after it is, by the address trimmed; the pane
opens the photo, the bookmarked picture and the spaced photo from what was
posted and leaves the logo. In a stack the section is the letter's, for a
picture inside a section a letter's markup drew too; a body put in again
is wired again, once; no letter opens or closes. What the pane shows: still
shown with another letter of the conversation opened and his letters
looked for, and not once another row is tapped, the same row again, or the
pane emptied. The script, the pane's wiring, `openAttachment` asking it
before the file is shown and before a failure is said, and the loader's
reading read from the source; `CompleteThreadsTests`' pin of his letter's
settling has the keep.

Each part undone by hand, `PictureTapTests` and `CompleteThreadsTests` run,
then put back and passing, counted as failures in tests. As first built:
the scheme not checked, 3 in 1; the address's host read in lower case, as
a parser that lowered it would, 8 in 3; the first of two parts under one
id, 2 in 1; the stack not looked at, the letter alone taken, 11 in 1; his
letters not let go with the conversation, 1 in 1; a body put in not wired,
3 in 2; a letter's own page not wired, 3 in 2; the nearest section, not
the page's own child, 2 in 2; the handler not registered, 1 in 1; his
letter not kept, 2 in 2; the loader reading the address its own way, 1 in
1. Not the percent-decoding after the host is read, 0: Foundation on this
host gives the host decoded already, so here it is a belt, as it was in
the loader. Since the bookmark, the trimmed `src`, the shorter side and
the pane moving on, `PictureTapTests` run: the size as drawn not checked,
7 in 3; no size checked, 18 in 3; the drawn size's shorter side held to
100, as first built, 4 in 1; no floor for it, 3 in 1; NaN and infinity
let through, 3 in 1; the link and button rule dropped, 5 in 3; every
`<a>` a link again, 4 in 2; an empty `href` no link, 4 in 2; the `src` as
written, 5 in 2; `openAttachment` not asking before it shows the file, 1
in 1, nor before it says it failed, 1 in 1; what the pane shows never
changing, 4 in 1.

The full suite, serially: 2,415 tests, 11 of them new, 6 skipped, none

## B-123 — CHANGED 2026-10-24 to copy Apple Mail, not yet seen on the iPad. A half-typed name found nothing in search until the last letter of it was in; Mail's search matches the start of words, so "Marg" finds Margaret's letters

Built in the `bm-halfname` worktree (branch `fix-halfname`), off master at
b9ca9a4.

**What Mail does.** Apple's iPad User Guide for iPadOS 18: "The most
relevant messages appear in Top Hits above the search suggestions as you
type" (support.apple.com/guide/ipad/search-for-email-ipadedcc14e6/18.0/ipados/18.0).
How a word half typed is matched it does not say. iOS 18.6's
Message.framework, read from the binary in the simulator runtime and not
run, has the on-device criterion `= '%@*'cdwt`: the start of a word,
ignoring case and accents, so "Marg" finds Margaret among the letters on
the iPad. That this is 18.6's code is sure; that his 18.7 takes that path
as he types is likely, not seen. Mail's own search of an IMAP server asks
for whole words, as this app does (B-105).

**What he saw.** Not on his own iPad, where the app is not installed yet.
What the app does there: each pause of 350 ms in his typing sends a SEARCH
of whole words (`SearchCriteria`, the list's `queryChanged`), and Gmail
matches whole words only (B-105, measured 2026-10-22: "conver" and "gard"
found nothing). So a name typed slowly reads "No results" after every
letter until the last one is in. On the test account, read only, during
the audit of 2026-10-24: a sender's whole name found about 2,000 letters
in From and Subject, and its first four letters none, for each of three
names. He searches all the time (D-012). The address book the composer
offers addresses from was already on the iPad, filled from every envelope
the list fetches and from his sends (`RecipientBook`, B-017), and search
did not use it.

**Changed.**

1. *The word he is still typing* (`SearchCriteria.halfWord(of:)`): the
   last word of the text as B-105 reads it, when nothing was typed after
   it, not a space, a closing quote mark, a closing single quote or a
   dash, and it has three letters or digits or more, and the text ends
   with it as a word of its own: nothing, white space, a quote mark or a
   dash before it, with any single quotes that open it. So in "Joann ann
   joann" the last "joann", asked already, leaves no such word, though
   the text ends "ann". A word with a space after it is whole, as the
   keyboard's suggestions finish a word with one. Three, not Mail's two: two letters are often a name or a word on
   their own, "Ed", "Jo", "to", "my", which the word finds whole, and the
   people of a book of 300 whose name starts with two letters can be many
   more than four, so the four asked for would be picked by the book's
   order and not by his typing. A three-letter name, "Ann", "Sam", is
   still found whole, its letters among the hits.
2. *The people it may be the start of*
   (`RecipientBook.addresses(startingWith:besides:)`): every address in
   the book whose name has a word that starts with it, or whose part
   before the @ does ("ellis" of "m.ellis1947"), or the whole address
   ("margaret@exa"); ignoring case and accents ("nun" and "Núñ" start
   "Núñez") and apostrophes ("O’Bri" as his keyboard types it starts
   "O'Brien"). Never the middle of a word, and never the part after the
   @: "gmai" starts most of his correspondents' addresses and nobody's
   name. In order: a name before an address, then the addresses he has
   written to most, then those seen last, then by address, the
   composer's own order. Never himself: none of the addresses his
   account lists as his and its login (`OwnAddresses(account:)`, as
   Reply All leaves them out, B-076), as Settings last saved them, so
   one added there since the app was opened is his at once; nor an
   address under a name the book has for any of them: his account's
   name for his address (B-082), and for his second address whatever
   name his letters to it carried, or none, as the list passes over
   only the account's own address when it notes names. Every letter in
   his mailbox is to him or from him, and about half he sends go to his
   second address (the gap review in TODO: 1,186 YouTube and 256
   Wikipedia links in 30 days), so one of his beside "Bla" would turn a
   search for a Blair into his whole mailbox, or half of it, ranked
   first by those sends; his own name typed whole finds what it found.
   Not by the name of a letter sent on someone's behalf, with "via" as a
   word in it: "'Margaret Ellis' via Garden Club" at the group's
   address, "Jane Doe via LinkedIn" at the service's. The book keeps the
   last name it saw for an address, so her name would have asked for
   every letter of the group, other people's too. Such an entry is still
   found by its address, "gard" for the group.
3. *The SEARCH* (`SearchCriteria.imap(for:people:)`): that word's group
   asks for the word in its five fields as before and, beside it in the
   same OR, each of up to four of those addresses in From, To and Cc:
   `OR OR OR OR OR OR OR FROM "Marg" TO "Marg" CC "Marg" SUBJECT "Marg"
   BODY "Marg" FROM "m.ellis1947@example.net" TO "…" CC "…"`. The other
   words' groups, and every key with no such word or nobody found, are
   byte for byte as before. An address over 100 bytes, one with a control
   character, one without an @, one given twice in any case, and the word
   itself, are passed over (`askable`), each address escaped as a word
   is, and one with 8-bit text in it goes as a literal as any word does
   (B-105). So the line grows by 1,316 bytes at most, four addresses of
   100 bytes in three fields; Gmail took 17.6 KB in 112 ms (B-105).
4. *The repository* (`IMAPMailRepository.search`) looks the people up as
   the search starts, from the text as the list hands it in, untrimmed,
   since the space is what says a word is whole; the list hands in the
   field's text as typed, as before. A later page of the same words asks
   what its first page asked (`SearchSession.query` and `criteria`): the
   first page's own envelopes teach the book, and Margot, learned from a
   letter Margaret was copied on, asked for at the second page would have
   started the search again at its first page, its rows twice. The same
   words with a space typed after them since go on as well.
5. *Comments and docs:* `SearchCriteria`'s header, `RecipientBook`'s,
   `MailRepository.search`'s `query`; B-105 here and its TODO line, which
   said nothing is found by the start of a word.

**Not changed.** B-105's rules: each word asked for in From, To, Cc,
Subject or the body, all of them required; quote marks straight and curly,
the dashes, single quotes around a word, one-letter words left out, the
first twenty words, CHARSET UTF-8 and literals for 8-bit words. The two
scopes, the Trash and Spam merge, paging. The 350 ms pause. Recent
searches: kept at Search on the keyboard and at a letter opened from the
results, never at a keystroke, as before. No suggestion list as he types,
which stays dropped, and no subject or body found by the start of a word:
that needs an index of the whole mailbox on the iPad, which D-016 does not
keep. The book itself: what it learns, its 300 entries, what the composer
offers. The Mock repository, which matches any part of a field, as before.
No new words on his screen. The connection log carries the longer line;
the addresses in it were in its envelopes already (D-016).

**What he sees.** "Marg", after a pause: Margaret's letters, from her, to
her and those she was copied on, newest first, with any letter that has
"Marg" as a whole word, and the letters of up to three others in the book
whose name or address starts "Marg"; the same as he types on to
"Margaret". With a space after it, the word is searched whole, as before.
"lunch Marg" finds her letters about lunch. A person the app has never
listed a letter of, or seen him write to, is not found by half a name;
the whole name finds them as before.

**Tests.** `HalfNameSearchTests`, fourteen, new. Over the scripted
server, which now matches whole words in From, To, Cc, Subject and the body
when asked (`matchesWholeWords`), as Gmail does, so "Marg" alone finds
nothing there. "Marg" in All Mailboxes, after the Inbox was listed: her
letter, his to her and one she was copied on, not Carlo's, the Trash, Spam
and All Mail each asked the word and her address in one group; with the
book emptied, as before and nothing. "Zeb", nobody, and "Ma", two letters:
byte for byte as before, and nothing. "lunch Marg": her two letters about
lunch; "Marg Ell": the first word whole, and nothing. "Marg ", "Margaret "
and “Marg”: as before, "Margaret " finding her three by her name. "Núñ",
the word a literal, and "nun" and "Jos", plain, each finding José Núñez;
"O’Bri", a literal, finding Peggy O'Brien. Pages: a page's rows teach the
book Margot, and the next pages, the last asked with a space typed after
the word, go on with one SEARCH and no row twice, while a new search asks
for both, Margaret first. Never himself: "Mars" asks for Marshall and
neither the account's address nor his other address under his name, "Owe"
for nobody; with no name for the account, "Own" asks for nobody, where his
address would have found every letter. His second address listed under
his account, in the book with no name, then under the name his letters
to it carried, with an old address of his under that name too: "Vid",
the start of its part before the @, and "Gra", of that name, each asked
byte for byte as before and finding nothing, where with the account's

## B-124 — CHANGED 2026-10-24 to copy Apple Mail, not yet seen on the iPad. A cold launch showed white for about 130 ms before the dark rows; the launch screen is dark

**Found** in the same look at the gaps between this app and iPadOS 18
Mail as B-119, the last of those to close before the install, from what
the test iPad showed on 2026-10-21 (B-053).

**What Mail does.** Apple's iPad Mail chapters say nothing of its launch;
Mail opens in the iPad's appearance, its launch screen and its first
screen alike (low). Apple's Human Interface Guidelines, Launching: design
a launch screen that is nearly identical to the first screen of the app
(developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/launching, high).
This app's first screen is dark (D-010).

**What he saw.** He has not had the app; on the test iPad, from a screen
recording at 60 frames a second (B-053, 2026-10-21): Blackmail ended, its
icon tapped, the system's launch screen, white, for about 130 ms, then
the kept rows, black, at every cold launch. `UILaunchScreen` is an empty
dict, the system's plain screen in the app's style, and Info.plist's
`UIUserInterfaceStyle` said Light, from the first commit, before D-010
made the app dark. The window is pinned dark in code, but only once the
app's code runs, after the launch screen. Recorded then and left.

**Changed.** Info.plist's `UIUserInterfaceStyle` is Dark, with a comment
saying why; `AppDelegate`'s note on the window's style says so too. What
else the key reaches, read from the code, each with whether it is right
for D-010:

1. *The launch screen:* black, where it was white; the status bar's words
   over it light, by `UIStatusBarStyleDefault`. Right: the app's canvas is
   black. Where iOS puts the launch screen in the app's place, as it may
   in the app switcher before it has a picture of the app, the same.
2. *Everything in the app's window:* nothing. The app makes one window,
   pinned dark before anything is put in it, and everything he is shown
   is presented in it, so was dark whatever the plist said and stays so:
   the composer; every alert and sheet ("Open this link?", the Reply
   sheet, Cancel's question, Settings' alerts); Quick Look, full screen
   over the pane; the connection log's share sheet; the photo picker and
   Files, from the composer; Go to Date's calendar; the Print panel, a
   presentation over the pane (B-110's check logged `PRINT panel
   over=true`, the centred Print Options sheet on 16.5.1). Right: all
   dark, as D-010 has it.
3. *The paper:* nothing. The print's web view is pinned light and its
   page says "light only" (`LetterPrint`, `PrintPage`), and a letter that
   prints as words is drawn black. Right: paper is light (D-010,
   2026-10-22).
4. *A letter he sends:* nothing. Its HTML names its own light colours
   (`AppleMailHTML`), and the plist reaches no other mail client.
5. *The share sheet* (the extension): nothing. It has a plist of its own,
   with no style, comes up over another app with no launch screen of its
   own, and pins its sheet and its window dark in code (B-069). Not
   given the key: it is for a launch screen, and the extension has none.
6. *The keyboard, the edit menu and the loupe:* the system's, drawn for
   the field he types in, which is in the dark window; the window's
   comment has always said its style keeps the keyboard dark. Nothing
   records the keyboard seen either way. If one of them went by the plist
   rather than the window, it was light and is dark now, which is right
   for D-010; one look in the check.
7. *The system's own prompts,* such as Photos' question: SpringBoard's,
   in the iPad's appearance. Nothing.
8. *Smart Invert,* which the app cannot live with (B-006): the launch
   screen and the app are inverted alike, both white, so no flash there
   either.

**Not changed.** The window's pin, `Theme`, the rows, the pane, the
print, the share extension's plist and code. Nothing reads the app's
style from outside a window. No new words.

**What he sees.** At a cold launch, black from the icon's zoom to the
rows, no white.

**Tests.** `InfoPlistTests`, two new: the plist's style is Dark, its
`UILaunchScreen` an empty dict and its status bar style the default; and
from the source, the app's one `UIWindow`, pinned dark after it is made
and before its root is put in it, the one pin to light the print's web
view, the print's page "light only", no pin to the system's style, the
share extension's controller and window pinned dark with no style in its
plist, and nothing reading `UITraitCollection.current` or the screen's.
Each undone by hand, `InfoPlistTests` and `ShareInfoPlistTests` run, then
put back and passing, counted as failures in tests: the plist Light
again, 1 in 1; the window's pin gone, 1 in 1; the print's web view not
pinned light, 2 in 1; the share extension's plist Light, 1 in 1; its

## B-121 — CHANGED 2026-10-24 to copy Apple Mail, not yet seen on the iPad. Subject began in lower case and was not corrected, and his apostrophes and quotes went straight; Mail's Subject takes a capital and corrections, and both it and the body Smart Punctuation

**What Mail does.** Apple's guide is silent. Mail's composer, read from
iOS 18.6's MessageUI in the simulator runtime, sets capitals,
corrections and the keyboard type only on its address fields
(`MFComposeRecipientTextView`, `MFComposeRecipientView`: no corrections,
no capitals, the email keyboard), and Smart Punctuation on nothing at all:
its Subject (`MFComposeSubjectView`) and its body (a web view) keep the
system's own, a capital to begin, corrections, and Smart Punctuation, each
as Settings > General > Keyboard has it, all on from the factory. His own
letters show it: of the 479 letters he began in 30 days, 467 subjects
start with a capital and 1 with a small letter; in 90 sampled letters, 16
have a curly apostrophe he typed and none a straight one; in his subjects
9 curly against 2 straight (gap list, 2026-10-24).

**What he would have seen.** About 16 subjects a day typed: each in lower
case unless he reached for Shift, no word corrected, and every apostrophe
and quote in Subject and the body straight, where his letters from Mail
have them curly.

**What it was.** Subject, in the composer and the share sheet: capitals
none, corrections off, Smart Dashes and Smart Quotes off, left from when
the same row served To, Cc and Bcc (before B-076). The body, in both:
Smart Dashes and Smart Quotes off, from a code comment calling them no
help, with no decision behind it.

**Changed.** Subject, in both sheets: capitals by sentence, corrections,
Smart Dashes and Smart Quotes at the system's default, written out so the
choice is seen. The body, in both: Smart Dashes and Smart Quotes at the
default; its capitals and corrections were already the system's. So
"don't" typed has a curly ’ when Settings' Smart Punctuation is on, quotes
come out “ ” and ‘ ’, and "--" a dash, as in Mail; with any of the three
switched off in Settings, off here as in Mail.

**Not changed.** To, Cc and Bcc keep `RecipientField`'s email keyboard,
no capitals, no corrections and straight quotes: an address corrected or
curled bounces. The search field keeps its own (B-105). On the wire
nothing changed, and nothing had to: Subject goes as UTF-8 encoded words,
the text and the HTML twin as quoted-printable UTF-8, and the app's own
reader gives back what he typed; B-105's search keeps ’ inside its word,
reads “ ” as a phrase's marks and — as a space, and asks for a word with
’ in it as a UTF-8 literal (`SearchLiteralTests`). No new words.

**What he sees.** In Subject, the first letter a capital as he begins and
a misspelt word corrected as he goes on, in both sheets. In Subject and
the body, his apostrophes and quotes curly and "--" a dash, as Settings
has them. In To, Cc and Bcc, nothing different.

**Tests.** `TypingAsInMailTests`, six: Subject in both sheets with
capitals, corrections and Smart Punctuation at the system's own and none
of the four off; the body in both with Smart Punctuation and nothing
off; the address rows' email keyboard and their four settings kept, and
Subject's row the only one in either sheet setting capitals; a letter
with “ ” ‘ ’ ’ — and – in Subject and body, built by the app and read
back by it: every byte seven-bit, Subject in UTF-8 encoded words reading
back as typed, the plain part's and the HTML twin's words as typed under
`charset=utf-8`, no straight apostrophe anywhere; the share sheet's
letter the same, its link still a link; and the subject's words as
B-105's search takes them, "Don’t", "miss", "Tosca", "Sunday’s", "at".

Each part undone by hand, the class run, then put back and passing,
counted as failures in tests: the composer's Subject in lower case, 2 in
1; uncorrected, 2 in 1; with straight quotes, 2 in 1; the share sheet's
Subject as it was, 5 in 1; the composer's body as it was, 3 in 1; the
share sheet's body as it was, 3 in 1; the address rows curling quotes, 1
in 1; Subject's header not encoded past ASCII, 4 in 2; the bodies' bytes
past ASCII left eight-bit, 2 in 2; the twin labelled Latin-1, 2 in 2
(before its label was asserted, 0: the app's own reader takes UTF-8
whatever the label says); the twin straightening apostrophes, 8 in 2; the
share's linked twin doing so, 4 in 1; the search splitting a word at its
’, 1 in 1; and keeping “ ” in a word, 1 in 1.

The full suite, serially: 2,417 tests, 6 of them new, 6 skipped, none
failing. The release build for the iPad links.

## B-125 — CHANGED 2026-10-24 to copy Apple Mail, not yet seen on the iPad. A YouTube share was left with no subject as Mail's would be; Mail's has the video's title, and the subject is what the share hands over that names it, Safari's page title, the YouTube app's none

**The ruling reopened.** On 2026-10-21 the owner ruled: "Leave the
two-tap Send, the 'View recent photos.png' name, and the subjectless
YouTube share as they are, since each matches what Mail or iOS would do."
The gap list of 2026-10-24 found the ground untrue for the share: of about
950 YouTube shares he sent through Mail in 30 days, none had an empty
subject. Mail gives the video's title: 920 of them carry youtu.be links,
the YouTube app's own, and none a title ending in Safari's " - YouTube".
They come back into his Inbox through his second address (B-061), about
31 a day, and in this app each would be a row "(no subject)" that a
search by its title cannot find. The owner said to go on copying Mail.
The rest of the ruling stands.

**What Mail does.** Read from iOS 18.6's ShareSheet framework in the
simulator runtime on the Mac. Mail's entry in the share sheet
(`UIMailActivity`) takes its subject from the sharing app's answer to
`activityViewController(_:subjectForActivityType:)` asked for Mail, else
the share sheet's own subject, and from nothing else; the words and
addresses shared are its body. Safari answers with its page's title, for
every kind of share but AirDrop (`_SFActivityItemProvider`,
SafariServices). The YouTube app answers with the video's title, by his
letters. Mail fetches nothing to fill a share's Subject: its share entry,
preparing the letter, asks LinkPresentation for nothing, and the
composer's `contentURLs` serve its donation to Siri's suggestions
(`hasDuetDonationContext`), not a fetch. Its composer does fetch a page's
preview for a link pasted into a letter's body, which it makes a rich
link (`-[MFComposeWebView pasteRichLink]`,
`insertRichLinkWithURL:completionHandler:`, `MSRichLinkGenerator`,
`richLinkDidStartLoading:` and `richLinkDidFinishLoading:`, MessageUI of
iOS 18.6); that is the body's, not a share's Subject.

**What a share extension is handed.** The share sheet asks the subject
question for Mail, Messages, Reading List and AirDrop only. A share
extension (`UISocialActivity`, `com.apple.share-services`) is handed the
items as attachments and, as the item's words (`attributedContentText`),
any words the app shares. Seen in the iPadOS 18.6 simulator on the Mac,
an iPad (A16), with a share extension made only to write down what it was
handed, and a small app to share from:

- *An app offering a subject and a LinkPresentation title* (the title the
  share sheet's header showed): one item, the link alone, with no
  `attributedTitle`, no `attributedContentText` and no suggested name.
  The app was asked for the link for the extension and never for a
  subject.
- *The same app sharing words and the link:* the words as
  `attributedContentText` and as a text, then the link.
- *Safari on a Wikipedia page:* `attributedContentText` "Opera house -
  Wikipedia", no `attributedTitle`, and the link: the subject Mail gives
  the same share.
- *The YouTube app,* which the simulator does not have: the link alone,
  seen on the test iPad on 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-21 (B-036).

So an extension has Safari's title as Mail has it, and never the YouTube
app's.

**What it was.** The subject was the item's `attributedTitle`, else its
`attributedContentText`, worked out in the extension's own line under a
comment saying that was how Mail takes it; a YouTube share had none.

**Changed.**

1. *The naming, in one place the host runs* (`ShareItems.name`, new): the
   item's title, else its words, trimmed; nothing when neither has any.
   The same rule as before, now held by tests in the shapes seen: Safari's
   page title is the subject, an app's own title comes before its words,
   and a link handed over alone has no subject. The subject is the
   share sheet's ordinary Subject, his to change.
2. *What the comments say*: that Mail's subject is the app's answer,
   which no extension is given; that Safari hands over its title and the
   YouTube app none (`ShareItems.name`, `SharedItem.link`, the share
   sheet's own).
3. *No fetch.* Nothing in the share sheet asks for the page, by
   LinkPresentation, a URL session or YouTube's oEmbed, since Mail fetches
   nothing to fill a share's Subject; a test holds it so.

**Not changed.** What any share's subject is: Safari's as before, the
YouTube app's still empty, now for want of anything naming it rather than
by the ruling. Words an app shares beside a link are its subject and its
body's first line, as before (Mail's subject would be the app's answer,
which the extension is never given). The body, the HTML twin, the sheet.
No new words.

**What he sees.** As before: a Safari page's title in Subject, which he
can change like any subject; a YouTube share with Subject empty and "New
Message" over the sheet.

**Left for the owner.** Naming a YouTube share as Mail does needs the
page's title fetched while the sheet is up. Mail fetches nothing to fill
a share's Subject, though its composer does fetch a pasted link's preview
(TODO, "Blocked on the owner", a YouTube share's subject).

**Tests.** `ShareNameTests`, five: Safari's shape, the words "Opera house
- Wikipedia" and no title, the subject, the link alone in the body; an
app's own title before the words, a blank title giving way to them, a
blank one alone nothing; the YouTube app's shape, nothing, the subject
empty and the link alone; the extension reading its items through
`ShareItems.name` and its words in no other place; and no LinkPresentation,
URL session or connection, `dataTask`, page read, oEmbed or web view in
any Swift file of the share sheet's folder (`Sources/Blackmail/Share`,
five named files checked to be among those read).

Each part undone by hand, the class run, then put back and passing,
counted as failures in tests: the words before the title, 1 in 1; the
title alone, Safari's words not read, 3 in 2; names not trimmed, 3 in 2;
the extension reading its own way, as it did, 1 in 1; LinkPresentation
brought into the share sheet, 1 in 1; a metadata fetch in
`ShareMirror.swift`, a file of the share sheet the test once did not
read, 3 in 1; a web view in `ShareViewController.swift`, 1 in 1; a URL
connection in `ShareSheet.swift`, 1 in 1.

The full suite, serially: 2,422 tests, 5 of them new, 6 skipped, none
failing. The release build for the iPad links.
